genres.name: 16-bit
genres.description: Created using video game consoles with audio hardware using 16-bit audio samples, most notably the Super Nintendo Entertainment System.

genres.name: 2 Tone
genres.description: Combines 1960s Jamaican Ska with Punk Rock and New Wave to create tracks played at faster tempos and with a harder edge than the original Jamaican records.

genres.name: 2-Step
genres.description: Originating in London and popular in the late 1990s; jittery, shuffling rhythms rarely following a four-on-the-floor pattern.

genres.name: 3-Step
genres.description: Distinct three-kick-drum rhythm, blends influences from Amapiano and Broken Beat, resulting in relaxed, freeform, playful, Jazz-like feel.

genres.name: Aak
genres.description: Korean Classical Music that dates back to the early 12th century.

genres.name: Abakuá Music
genres.description: Ritual music associated with the Abakuá religious fraternity of Cuba, descending from the Ékpè tradition of West Africa.

genres.name: Abkhazian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Republic of Abkhazia, a disputed territory on the Black Sea in northwestern Georgia.

genres.name: Aboio
genres.description: Cattle-herding songs originating in rural Northeastern Brazil.

genres.name: Aboio cantado
genres.description: Aboio that features rhyming verses.

genres.name: Abstract Hip Hop
genres.description: Uses much more abstract lyricism than what is considered conventional within the genre, typically through use of metaphors, symbolism, and cryptic meanings.

genres.name: Acholi Music
genres.description: Music of the Acholi people, who inhabit a region known as “Acholiland,” spanning parts of northern Uganda and southern South Sudan.

genres.name: Acholitronix
genres.description: Fusion of traditional Acholi rhythms and melodies with Electronic production, originating in the city of Gulu.

genres.name: Achomi Music
genres.description: Musical traditions of the Achomi people, an Iranian people native to the Persian Gulf coast.

genres.name: Acid Breaks
genres.description: Incorporates prominent "squelching", resonant low pass filter sounds typical to Acid House, and often other "trippy" effects into intense, syncopated, broken rhythms in the tempos of 110-150 BPM.

genres.name: Acid House
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1980s, characterised by repetitive basslines created with the distinctive modulated "squelching" sound of the Roland TB-303 synthesiser.

genres.name: Acid Jazz
genres.description: Eclectic scene consisting of influences from Jazz, Funk, Hip Hop, Soul, and various styles of Dance that gained popularity during the 1990s.

genres.name: Acid Rock
genres.description: Heavier with an emphasis on instrumental jamming and "wah" guitar effects.

genres.name: Acid Techno
genres.description: Incorporates "squelching" synths from Acid House into a mechanical and usually more energetic Techno context.

genres.name: Acid Trance
genres.description: Incorporates "squelching" acid basslines into Trance's evolving structure.

genres.name: Acidcore
genres.description: Developed out of the 1990s Acid Techno scene utilizing its prominence of "acid" TB-303 bassline sequences into more intense rhythms derived from earlier Hardcore [EDM], Gabber and Trance music.

genres.name: Acousmatic Music
genres.description: Fixed-media Electroacoustic music designed to be reproduced by multiple loudspeakers without the presence of instrumentalists and visual cues.

genres.name: Acoustic Blues
genres.description: Developed out of Work Song and Spirituals to become the most prominent early form of Blues.

genres.name: Acoustic Chicago Blues
genres.description: Unplugged Blues made in the Chicago region, primarily during the 1930s and 1940s.

genres.name: Acoustic Rock
genres.description: Rock with acoustic instrumentation, as opposed to the typical electric instrumentation.

genres.name: Acoustic Texas Blues
genres.description: Laid-back swing rhythms and guitar ornamentation, including solos.

genres.name: Adhunik geet
genres.description: Nepali popular music which fuses elements of light Hindustani Classical Music, Ghazal and Western music.

genres.name: Adult Contemporary
genres.description: Slow to midtempo with a light and soothing tone, emerged as a successful radio format in the late 1970s and early 1980s.

genres.name: Aegean Islands Folk Music
genres.description: Music of the Greek Aegean Islands.

genres.name: Afar Music
genres.description: Music of the Afar people, who inhabit an area spanning parts of Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti.

genres.name: Afoxé
genres.description: Afro-Brazilian genre originating in the states of Pernambuco and Bahia, characterized by the ijexá rhythm invented by the Yoruba people.

genres.name: African Folk Music
genres.description: Indigenous music of Africa that is passed down orally from generation to generation, the authors of the songs are usually unknown.

genres.name: African Music
genres.description: All forms with roots in Africa.

genres.name: Afrikaner Folk Music
genres.description: Musical traditions developed by the Afrikaner community in southern Africa.

genres.name: Afro House
genres.description: Emerged by fusing Deep House with Southern African Music, characterized by hypnotizing drum patterns of shakers and congas, often sampled African vocals or soulful original features, and spiritual, organic, melodic atmosphere.

genres.name: Afro Trap
genres.description: Centered mostly in France, features production influenced by modern styles developed in West and Central Africa with Trap-styled vocal flows.

genres.name: Afro-Cuban Jazz
genres.description: Combines Jazz with the rhythms of Afro-Cuban music.

genres.name: Afro-Funk
genres.description: Strongly mixed with traditional and more modern genres in sub-Saharan West Africa.

genres.name: Afro-Jazz
genres.description: African-styled percussion and rhythms.

genres.name: Afro-Rock
genres.description: Incorporates West African influences; initially emerged in the early 1970s.

genres.name: Afrobeat
genres.description: Merges West African styles such as traditional Yoruba Music and Highlife with elements of Funk and  Jazz, typically resulting in extended improvisatory jams with call-and-response vocals.

genres.name: Afrobeats
genres.description: Originated in West Africa during the early 2010s and includes elements from Pop Rap, Contemporary R&B, and Dancehall.

genres.name: Afrofuturism
genres.description: Movement rooted in Jazz and Funk, blending futuristic aesthetics and themes with African and Afrodiasporic culture.

genres.name: Afropiano
genres.description: Blends the easy-going, poppy, and melodic Afrobeats sound and rhythms with major Amapiano elements, like lush, jazzy, and laid-back atmospheres often featuring light piano chords.

genres.name: Afroswing
genres.description: Emerged in the United Kingdom during the mid-2010s, incorporating influences from Dancehall, Afrobeats, Contemporary R&B, and a variety of West African Music.

genres.name: Agbadza
genres.description: National dance-drumming tradition of the Ewe people in Ghana.

genres.name: Agbekor
genres.description: War dance of the Ewe people utilizing various percussive instruments and polyrhythms.

genres.name: Aggrotech
genres.description: Merges aggressive-sounding synths and apocalyptic atmospheres with harsh 4/4 beats and fast tempos.

genres.name: Ahwash
genres.description: Associated with the Tashelhit-speaking peoples of southern and central Morocco, and performed in large groups, combining singing, poetry and drumming.

genres.name: Ainu Music
genres.description: Music of the Ainu people from Hokkaidō, the Kuril Islands, and part of Sakhalin.

genres.name: Aita
genres.description: Arabic Folk Music from rural Morocco with piercing singing, scratchy viola, and rollicking hand drums.

genres.name: Akan Music
genres.description: Music of the Akan people of Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire, including a variety of traditional and neo-traditional styles which are based on some of the oldest traditions in West Africa.

genres.name: Akishibu-kei
genres.description: Otaku inclined update of the style pioneered by the Shibuya-kei scene, mixed with J-Pop and often tied to Anime and Video Game Music.

genres.name: Akron Sound
genres.description: Early Punk and New Wave scene in Akron, Ohio and nearby Kent from the mid-1970s to the early 1980s.

genres.name: Al jeel
genres.description: Emerged in the 1970s as an alternative to Shaabi, taking influence from foreign Pop and incorporating rhythms of Reggae while retaining a distinctly Egyptian sound.

genres.name: Al-Jadīd
genres.description: Modern Arabic music that emerged in the mid-20th century, blending traditional Arabic modes and vocal styles with Western harmonic, orchestral, and structural elements.

genres.name: Albanian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Albania, including the area's traditions as well as influence from Turkish Music.

genres.name: Aleke
genres.description: Derived from traditional Surinamese Maroon music, especially aukansi, features distinct faster rhythms.

genres.name: Alevi Folk Music
genres.description: Anatolian folk pioneered by Turkish poets and bards, connected to the Alevist heterodox Islamic tradition.

genres.name: Algerian Chaabi
genres.description: Features mournful vocals over an orchestral setting of violins, mandolins, pianos, and percussion.

genres.name: Algorave
genres.description: Generative dancefloor-oriented music produced live via algorithms.

genres.name: Alloukou
genres.description: Created by the Bété people of Côte d'Ivoire, featuring a distinctive rhythm that uses polyrhythms and triplets.

genres.name: Alpenrock
genres.description: Mixes Hard Rock and Blues Rock with traditional Alpine Folk Music elements such as Yodeling and use of the accordion.

genres.name: Alpine Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Alps, including parts of Germany, Austria, Slovenia, Switzerland, and Italy.

genres.name: Alsatian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional music of the Alsatians.

genres.name: Alt-Country
genres.description: Arose in the 1980s and 1990s, performed by artists with roots in Alternative Rock and Indie Rock who were disconnected from the mainstream Country industry.

genres.name: Alt-Pop
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2000s and early 2010s, combines chart Pop conventions with alternative/indie genre sensibilities sometimes on a more minimal and contemplative atmosphere, often extracted from Alternative R&B.

genres.name: Altai Music
genres.description: Music of the Altai people, an ethnic group who live in central Russia near the border of Mongolia and Kazakhstan.

genres.name: Alternative Dance
genres.description: Incorporates rhythms and synthesizers from Electronic Dance Music within the context of Alternative Rock and related styles; predominantly popular in the 1990s.

genres.name: Alternative Idol
genres.description: Unconventional approaches characterized by alternative music styles and often unusual public images.

genres.name: Alternative Metal
genres.description: Mid-tempo style emphasizing melodicism and rhythmic heaviness; branches outside of the stylistic conventions of Metal.

genres.name: Alternative R&B
genres.description: Deviating from the traditional styles of Contemporary R&B and featuring smooth, reverberated, Electronic-influenced production with heavy bass and often reverberated vocals.

genres.name: Alternative Rock
genres.description: Performed with a less commercial sensibility, utilizing more eccentric, Punk-influenced sounds, moodier or quirkier lyricism, and sometimes ample amounts of distortion, often paired with Pop-influenced songwriting.

genres.name: Alté
genres.description: More subdued, atmospheric, minimalist, and eclectic production and vocal styles compared to earlier styles, as well as more socially conscious lyrics.

genres.name: Amami shimauta
genres.description: Tradition from the Amami Islands, located in southern Japan.

genres.name: Amapiano
genres.description: House from South Africa deriving from previous popular genres including Gqom, Kwaito, and Deep House.

genres.name: Amazigh Music
genres.description: Music of the Amazigh people, the indigenous people of Northwest Africa (with main hubs in Morocco and Algeria) and certain parts of West Africa.

genres.name: Ambasse bey
genres.description: African Folk Music developed by the Yabassi people of Cameroon.

genres.name: Ambient
genres.description: Emphasizes texture and tone over traditional musical structure, aimed at evoking a particular atmosphere or mood.

genres.name: Ambient Americana
genres.description: Made using traditional Americana and Country instrumentation, typically to evoke a pastoral atmosphere.

genres.name: Ambient Dub
genres.description: Takes cues from Ambient and Dub reggae, featuring the atmosphere of the former and the Jamaican-style basslines, percussion, and psychedelic production techniques of the latter.

genres.name: Ambient House
genres.description: Primarily British genre developed in the 1990s with beats, synthesizers, and vocals in styles similar to House, treated with effects that are often described as "dream-like" or "chilled out".

genres.name: Ambient Noise Wall
genres.description: Soft, sparse textures inspired by the static composition of Harsh Noise Wall.

genres.name: Ambient Plugg
genres.description: Strong atmosphere and texture taken from Ambient music; featuring tight drums and minimal low-end and 808s.

genres.name: Ambient Pop
genres.description: Emphasizes texture and atmosphere with a degree of structural experimentation, drawing on Dream Pop, Neo-Psychedelia, and Post-Rock while tending towards more minimal, repetitive arrangements which may incorporate elements of Electronic or Krautrock.

genres.name: Ambient Techno
genres.description: Blends the mechanical, repetitive beats of Techno with atmospheres and textures inspired by Ambient music, resulting in slower tempos and more understated rhythms.

genres.name: Ambient Trance
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1990s mainly in the form of Chillout remixes of Trance tracks; incorporates its arpeggiated synthesizer sound into Downtempo and Ambient contexts.

genres.name: Ambrosian Chant
genres.description: Liturgical chant practiced in parts of Italy and Switzerland, characterized by stepped melodic progression.

genres.name: American Folk Music
genres.description: Traces back through the history of European and West African settlement and migration to North America, including parts of northern Mexico and Canada in addition to the United States.

genres.name: American Gamelan
genres.description: Mid-20th-century style, influenced by arrangements, instrumentation, rhythms, timbres, and tunings of Indonesian Gamelan.

genres.name: American Primitivism
genres.description: Blends avant-garde and neo-classical compositions with traditional Country Blues fingerpicking techniques.

genres.name: Americana
genres.description: Incorporates a broad swath of American Folk Music and Contemporary Folk influences, evolving alongside Alt-Country.

genres.name: Amigacore
genres.description: Gabber-like forms of Hardcore [EDM] written in first-gen trackers for the Amiga like ProTracker and OctaMED, resulting in a minimalistic raw lo-fi sound.

genres.name: Anarcho-Punk
genres.description: Intentionally rougher and sloppier sound, with lyrics pertaining to anarchist ideology and sociopolitical injustices.

genres.name: Anatolian Rock
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Turkish Folk Music, particularly traditional instruments such as the bağlama and saz alongside traditional scales and melodies.

genres.name: Ancient Chinese Music
genres.description: Covers a very large era of creation from approximately 2100 BCE to 200 CE.

genres.name: Ancient Egyptian Music
genres.description: Music of ancient Egyptian civilization.

genres.name: Ancient Greek Music
genres.description: Music of ancient Greek civilization.

genres.name: Ancient Levitical Music
genres.description: Reconstruction of Jerusalem temple music.

genres.name: Ancient Music
genres.description: Umbrella term encompassing all the genres coming after the Prehistoric Music and before the Medieval music eras from ancient civilizations, roughly before 500 CE, following the Western Classical Music point of view with the date of the Roman Empire fall (476 CE).

genres.name: Ancient Roman Music
genres.description: Music of ancient Roman civilization.

genres.name: Andalusian Classical Music
genres.description: Arabic Classical Music tradition that had its beginnings in Al-Andalus, the medieval Islamic Iberian peninsula, which later spread and developed in the Maghreb.

genres.name: Andalusian Folk Music
genres.description: Flamenco of Andalusia in southern Spain, rooted in traditional music and dances and developed mostly after the 18th century by the Romani people of Andalusia (known locally as gitanos).

genres.name: Andean New Age
genres.description: Takes heavy influence from Indigenous Andean Music, emphasizing a peaceful and harmonious atmosphere and often using the flute.

genres.name: Anglican Chant
genres.description: Simple, harmonized, English-language setting of the Christian liturgy, principally devised by the Anglican Church.

genres.name: Animal Sounds
genres.description: Recordings which are done in order to capture sounds produced by animals.

genres.name: Anti-Folk
genres.description: Rawer approach to folk, with an often self-mocking and sarcastic tone.

genres.name: AOR
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1970s and early 1980s as an amalgamation of Hard Rock, Pop Rock, and Progressive Rock; characterized by a rich, layered sound, slick production and a heavy reliance on commercial melodic hooks.

genres.name: Apala
genres.description: Yoruba Music developed by Muslims during the late 1930s and early 1940s in the Ijebu region of Yorubaland, the current Ogun state.

genres.name: Appalachian Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Appalachian Mountains in the Eastern United States.

genres.name: Aquacrunk
genres.description: Syncopated, half-time rhythms inspired by Dubstep and Grime, funky, sludgy, "aquatic"-sounding synths and sound design.

genres.name: Arabesk
genres.description: Arabic-style productions by Turkish musicians, who also draw influence from their native forms, including Turkish Folk Music, Balkan Music, and Byzantine Music.

genres.name: Arabesque Rap
genres.description: Emerged from Turkey in the late 2000s, based almost exclusively around Arabesk samples and featuring aggressive rap vocals.

genres.name: Arabic Bellydance Music
genres.description: Accompaniment to traditional belly dances.

genres.name: Arabic Classical Music
genres.description: Arabic Classical Music tradition, whose guidelines for modulation, rhythm, and tuning were set down in treatises in the 8th and 9th centuries, based around Maqāmic Music.

genres.name: Arabic Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Arabic people.

genres.name: Arabic Jazz
genres.description: Blending of Arabic Music and Jazz.

genres.name: Arabic Music
genres.description: Originating with and primarily performed by the Arab people.

genres.name: Arabic Pop
genres.description: Synthesis of Arabic Music with Western Pop melodies, almost always sung in Arabic and typically performed with Arabic instruments, alongside some Western instruments like the guitar.

genres.name: Aragonese Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Aragonese people.

genres.name: Argentine Music
genres.description: Music developed by the Argentine people.

genres.name: Armenian Church Music
genres.description: One of the oldest branches of Christian culture, this is the predominantly vocal music of the Armenian Apostolic Church.

genres.name: Armenian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Armenians, which is attested in historic Armenia since antiquity, with unique regional dialects unified by general melodic structure.

genres.name: Armenian Music
genres.description: Music of Armenia.

genres.name: Aromanian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Aromanians.

genres.name: Arrocha
genres.description: Influenced by Brega's romantic style, with further influence from Axé and Forró, giving it a more sensual and euphoric feel.

genres.name: Arrocha funk
genres.description: Slow and gritty Reggaetón-like drums with an emphasis on brass sections influenced by Arrocha.

genres.name: Arrocha sertanejo
genres.description: Merged the Arrocha style with the younger audience creating a more energetic and more danceable rhythm.

genres.name: Ars antiqua
genres.description: Mainly sacred European medieval music from the period of 1170 to 1310, featuring the birth of measuring time in music and the use of polyphonies for four voices.

genres.name: Ars nova
genres.description: Period (around 1310-1380) that succeeded Ars antiqua, mixing the sacred with the secular.

genres.name: Ars subtilior
genres.description: Emerged in the final period of late medieval music (around 1380-1420) and continued to use the technique of isorhythms but with added complexity.

genres.name: Art Pop
genres.description: Inventive, idiosyncratic, or artistically ambitious, often experimenting with unconventional musical elements and conceptual approaches while retaining accessibility.

genres.name: Art Punk
genres.description: Combines the stripped-down aggression of rudimentary Punk Rock with frequent experimentation ranging from instrumental interplay, noise, dissonance, and/or influences from other genres such as Jazz or Funk.

genres.name: Art Rock
genres.description: Attempts to expand the bounds of Rock within conventional structures, often using outside influences or experimentation for conceptual or thematic purpose.

genres.name: Art Song
genres.description: Vocal music with text often set to Poetry, typically for single vocalist with instrumental accompaniment, distinguished by its design for concert recital and high artistic demands requiring classically trained musicians.

genres.name: Artcore
genres.description: Combines an eclectic mix of Electronic Dance Music genres with the instrumentation and melodic stylings of genres like Cinematic Classical for a maximalist and emotional sound.

genres.name: Ashkenazi Cantorial Music
genres.description: Artistic, refined form of Chazzanut that greatly borrows from and implements elements of Western Classical Music and Christian Liturgical Music into the context of liturgical singing and chanting.

genres.name: Ashkenazi Music
genres.description: Encompasses the various traditions and genres of the Ashkenazi Jews, an ethnoreligious group that was prominent and influential in Europe throughout most of the Middle Ages and the modern period.

genres.name: Asian Music
genres.description: Rooted in the traditions of Asian peoples.

genres.name: Asian Rock
genres.description: Dense PluggnB percussion in combination with airy bells, synth plucks, and soaring synthetic guitar leads.

genres.name: Asian Underground
genres.description: South Asian diasporic movement defined by musical acts, producers and DJs fusing contemporary Electronic music with Bhangra and other traditional styles.

genres.name: ASMR
genres.description: Recordings intended to induce a pleasurable tingling sensation in the listener.

genres.name: Assamese Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Assamese people, a people group mostly from the Northeastern Indian state of Assam.

genres.name: Assiko
genres.description: Music and dance of the Bassa people of southern Cameroon, which features a singer accompanied by a guitarist and improvised percussion.

genres.name: Assyrian Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Assyrian or Syriac people, who are indigenous to the Upper Mesopotamian region roughly corresponding to ancient Assyria (which includes modern-day northern Iraq, northwestern Iran, northeastern Syria, and southeastern Turkey).

genres.name: Asturian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional music of the Asturian people.

genres.name: Athabaskan Fiddling
genres.description: Fiddle playing of the Northern Athabaskan Dene people of modern-day Alaska, the Yukon, and the Northwest Territories.

genres.name: Atlanta Bass
genres.description: Originated in Atlanta, slower tempos and a more melodic approach than Miami Bass.

genres.name: Atmospheric Black Metal
genres.description: Repetitive riffs and melodies, slower tempos, synthesized ambient textures, and guitar effects creating atmospheric soundscapes.

genres.name: Atmospheric Drum and Bass
genres.description: Prominent in the mid-1990s, uses faster, de-emphasized breakbeats, and places a greater focus on melodic elements such as slow, warm basslines and atmospheric melodies inspired by Ambient and Ambient House.

genres.name: Atmospheric Sludge Metal
genres.description: Combines slow, churning guitar riffs and thunderous percussion with dark, extensive otherworldly sonic landscapes.

genres.name: Audio Documentary
genres.description: Form of documentary that uses audio to document or explore a subject or theme.

genres.name: Aussie Pub Rock
genres.description: Straightforward Rock acts associated with the Australian pub circuit of the 1970s and 1980s.

genres.name: Australian Folk Music
genres.description: Folk traditions of the European colonists and convicts in Australia.

genres.name: Austronesian Music
genres.description: Music developed by Austronesian ethnic groups.

genres.name: Authenticité
genres.description: Post-independence cultural movement born in socialist Guinea aiming to reclaim pre-colonial heritage and forge a shared national identity, largely through government-funded programs, national orchestras, and radical rejection of European influences.

genres.name: Autonomic
genres.description: Mechanical, machine-like, "autonomic" rhythms that take primary influence from the cold, minimal sounds of mid-2000s UK Dubstep.

genres.name: Avant-Folk
genres.description: Experimental-influenced and playing with instrumentation, rhythm, and other factors not commonly found in folk.

genres.name: Avant-Garde Jazz
genres.description: Combines traditional or mainstream Jazz stylings with non-traditional techniques of avant-garde art music by experimenting with characteristics such as rhythm, harmony, structure, melody, and instrumentation.

genres.name: Avant-Garde Metal
genres.description: Often breaking the bounds of the genre through experimental structures and instrumentation, or by incorporating outside influences.

genres.name: Avant-Prog
genres.description: Focuses on highly complex, dense arrangements often featuring high amounts of dissonance and uncommon time signatures, sometimes extending towards atonality, free time, improvisation, and other avant-garde techniques.

genres.name: Avanzada
genres.description: Fusion of Polka paraguaya and Guarania with elements of Bossa nova and MPB.

genres.name: Avar Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Avar people.

genres.name: Avtorskaya pesnya
genres.description: Originating in the Soviet Union taking cues from forms of Russian Romance and Russian poetry with the main focus on lyrics.

genres.name: Axé
genres.description: Developed from a fusion of Frevo, Maracatu, Forró, Reggae and Calypso with roots in the Salvador de Bahia carnival.

genres.name: Ayyalah
genres.description: Traditional Khaliji-Bedouin weapon performance, commonly found across the United Arab Emirates and Northwestern Oman.

genres.name: Azerbaijani Mugham
genres.description: Highly improvisational form of modal music characterized by the singing style and the themes of Azerbaijan’s history.

genres.name: Azerbaijani Music
genres.description: Music of the Azerbaijani people, who inhabit the modern day country of Azerbaijan, along with a significant population in the neighboring country of Iran.

genres.name: Azmari
genres.description: Ethiopian/Eritrean singer/songwriters or minstrels equivalent to the Western European bard, the West African griot or the Romanian wandering taraf.

genres.name: Bacardi
genres.description: Bacardi is a type of House music from South Africa derived from Kwaito, delivering upbeat, danceable rhythms with lively snares and hi-hats.

genres.name: Bachata
genres.description: Romantic dance and accompanying music originating in the Dominican Republic, featuring arpeggiated chords in the melody.

genres.name: Bachatón
genres.description: Mixes Bachata melodies and instrumentation with Reggaetón rhythms, rapping, and DJing.

genres.name: Baganda Music
genres.description: Music of the Baganda people, a Bantu ethnic group indigenous to Uganda.

genres.name: Bagatelle
genres.description: Brief composition with an unpretentious, playful sound.

genres.name: Baggy
genres.description: Blends Dance and Funk-based grooves with a laid-back, psychedelic atmosphere; frequently features jangly guitars, looping basslines, four-bar drum patterns, and a hypnotic, carefree feel that originated in the Madchester scene of the late 1980s.

genres.name: Baguala
genres.description: Slow, triple-meter form of traditional Indigenous Andean Music originally performed by Diaguita people in present-day North-Western Argentina.

genres.name: Baila
genres.description: Sri Lankan popular music and dance genre that is believed to have its origins in Afro-Portuguese performance traditions brought to Sri Lanka during the Portuguese occupation.

genres.name: Bailecito
genres.description: Agile and lively dance derived from Zamacueca, typical of the western and central region of Bolivia.

genres.name: Baisha xiyue
genres.description: Mainly performed for funeral ceremonies of the Naxi ethnic group in the Yunnan province in China.

genres.name: Baithak gana
genres.description: Indo-Caribbean genre from Suriname, consisting of Bhojpuri Folk Music with local Caribbean influence.

genres.name: Baião
genres.description: Commonly performed with accordions and violas caipiras, and often accompanied by agogô and triangle.

genres.name: Bakersfield Sound
genres.description: Heavily based on electric instrumentation and a defined backbeat.

genres.name: Balani Show
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1990s in Mali; peaks at around 170BPM and prominently features looping, cut-up balafon samples.

genres.name: Balearic Beat
genres.description: Variety of relaxed, laid-back music that originates from the Balearic Islands off the coast of Spain, and particularly the club scene in Ibiza.

genres.name: Balinese Gamelan
genres.description: Broad classification grouping various forms of Gamelan with native roots in Bali.

genres.name: Balinese Music
genres.description: Music of the Balinese people.

genres.name: Balitaw
genres.description: Folk originating in the Visayas islands of the Philippines; dialogue or debate in which a man and a woman compete at improvising romantic verses.

genres.name: Balkan Brass Band
genres.description: Balkan Folk Music played by brass bands.

genres.name: Balkan Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Balkan region of Southeastern Europe.

genres.name: Balkan Music
genres.description: Meta-genre covering all forms developed in the Balkan Peninsula.

genres.name: Balkan Pop-Folk
genres.description: Balkan popular music which blends Pop, Folk, and ethnic music.

genres.name: Ballad Opera
genres.description: English reaction to the Italian Opera styles with a satirical sense of humor and scores borrowing from Traditional Folk Music and popular music.

genres.name: Ballet
genres.description: Western art music, often Orchestral Music, written to accompany classical dance productions of the same name.

genres.name: Ballet de cour
genres.description: Earliest form developed by the French royal court and characterized by its artistic diversity, regimented structure, grand spectacle, and overt political elements.

genres.name: Ballroom
genres.description: Emerging from the predominantly Black and LGBT Harlem ballroom culture, it is characterized by hard-hitting rhythms, generally improvised chanting by MCs known as commentators, and a distinctive crash sample.

genres.name: Balochi Music
genres.description: Music of the Baloch people.

genres.name: Baltic Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Balts.

genres.name: Baltimore Club
genres.description: Drew on the "booty bass" syncopation of Miami Bass, combined with Breakbeat rhythms around 130 BPM and chopped up vocal samples as found in Ghetto House.

genres.name: Balto-Finnic Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Balto-Finnic peoples.

genres.name: Bamar Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the majority ethnic group of Myanmar.

genres.name: Bamar Music
genres.description: Music of the Bamar people, the majority ethnic group of Myanmar.

genres.name: Bambuco
genres.description: Follows a 6/8 or 3/4 time signature with non-percussive instrumentation, often melancholic in sound with bright guitars and a rich melodic base.

genres.name: Banda de pífano
genres.description: Lively music played by bands consisting of two fifes and percussion.

genres.name: Banda Music
genres.description: Music of the Banda people, a Central African ethnic group mostly residing in the Central African Republic and its neighboring countries.

genres.name: Bandari
genres.description: Iranian dance music, often festive and energetic and set in 6/8, that traditionally makes primary use of Iranian bagpipes (ney-anbān).

genres.name: Bandas de viento de México
genres.description: Mexican ensemble with many regional variations dating back to the 1860s and 1870s, when locals attempted to imitate the military bands that were present in the country.

genres.name: Bandinha
genres.description: Popular style of music from the Southern region of Brazil. Borrows elements from German Folk Music, Sertanejo romântico and Brega.

genres.name: Banga
genres.description: Sufi ritual trance music of southern Tunisia performed by Black communities.

genres.name: Bantengan
genres.description: Traditional costumed animal dance with possession ritual features from eastern Java, accompanied by percussive music using the large jidor drum.

genres.name: Baqashot
genres.description: Collection of prayers, songs, supplications, and poems traditionally sung by Sephardic Jewish communities on Saturdays mornings.

genres.name: Barber Beats
genres.description: Borrows elements from Downtempo, Trip Hop, and Instrumental Hip Hop; emulates 1990s and 2000s Chillout music.

genres.name: Barbershop
genres.description: Harmonized singing consisting of four vocal elements: the 'lead' (2nd tenor), the 1st tenor, the baritone, and the bass.

genres.name: Bard Rock
genres.description: Mixes Rock music and styles with Avtorskaya pesnya.

genres.name: Bardcore
genres.description: Rearranges contemporary music with an array of acoustic instrumentation to evoke the aesthetic of medieval Europe.

genres.name: Baroque Music
genres.description: Constant rhythmic flow, or a steady motion throughout, generally focusing on a single melodic idea and including some form of counterpoint.

genres.name: Baroque Pop
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Western Classical Music, commonly featuring harpsichord or strings as well as the rhythmic flow and counterpoint of Baroque Music.

genres.name: Baroque Suite
genres.description: Collection of varied dance pieces, usually in the same key, structured on the music of European courtly dances.

genres.name: Bashkir Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional folk of the Bashkir people, a Turkic ethnic group inhabiting the Republic of Bashkortostan (Bashkiria), a federal subject of the Russian Federation, and its neighboring areas on both sides of the Ural mountains.

genres.name: Bashment Soca
genres.description: Highly energetic, Dancehall-influenced form of Soca developed in Barbados featuring dancefloor-oriented lyrics delivered in an aggressive chanting style.

genres.name: Basque Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Basque people.

genres.name: Bass House
genres.description: Busy, punchy percussion, prominent basslines and dirty, distorted synths resembling other bass music genres, with influences including Brostep, Fidget House, Bassline, Speed Garage, and Tech House.

genres.name: Bassline
genres.description: Strong emphasis on intricate basslines as well as four-on-the-floor beat patterns.

genres.name: Batak Music
genres.description: Music of the Batak people, an Austronesian people native to Sumatra.

genres.name: Batida
genres.description: Initially developed in the late '80s in Luanda, Angola, as a mixture of Soca- and Zouk-based percussion samples.

genres.name: Batonebi Songs
genres.description: Traditional Georgian Lullabies often meant to soothe sick children.

genres.name: Battle Record
genres.description: Compilations of sounds, samples, and beats pressed on vinyl records for use in DJ performances.

genres.name: Batucada
genres.description: Heavily percussive and polyrhythmic Samba.

genres.name: Batuque
genres.description: Tradition from Cape Verde, unusual among the islands' music due to its lack of polyphonic singing and its usage of polyrhythms.

genres.name: Baul gaan
genres.description: Songs performed by the Bauls, a movement of mystic entertainers influenced by diverse spiritual traditions.

genres.name: Bay Area Thrash Metal
genres.description: Highly influential Thrash Metal scene centered around the San Francisco Bay Area.

genres.name: Bayawan
genres.description: Distinct muqam tradition of the Dolan subgroup of the Uyghur people, often considered the wildest of the regional muqam variations.

genres.name: Beach Music
genres.description: Danceable 4/4 "blues shuffle" rhythmic structure, vocal harmonies, and moderate tempos.

genres.name: Beat
genres.description: Emerged in the early 1960s in the United Kingdom, drawing on Rock & Roll and the late 1950s Skiffle revival in a simple guitar-band format with strong melodies.

genres.name: Beat bolha
genres.description: Defined by its squeaky wisps and chopped bubbling samples, usually played around 130 to 170 BPM.

genres.name: Beat bruxaria
genres.description: São Paulo-originated Funk brasileiro with aggressive, distorted and high-pitched beats featuring minimalistic percussion and diversified sampling.

genres.name: Beat fino
genres.description: High pitched or sped up metallic percussion and Beatboxing loops with little to no bass.

genres.name: Beat Poetry
genres.description: Stream-of-consciousness Poetry originating with the Beats in the 1950s.

genres.name: Beat Rock
genres.description: Japan-exclusive subgenre which combines Pop melodicism with a punchy, driving sound drawing on Punk Rock and New Wave.

genres.name: Beatboxing
genres.description: Form of vocal percussion developed during the 1980s, primarily involving the art of producing drum beats, rhythm, and musical sounds using one's mouth, lips, tongue, voice, and more.

genres.name: Beatdown Hardcore
genres.description: Heavy, urban-inspired and breakdown-oriented with strong relations to Metalcore.

genres.name: Bebop
genres.description: Fast tempos, improvisation, melodic chromaticism, and complex harmonies and chord progressions.

genres.name: Bedouin Music
genres.description: Music made by the Bedouin, nomadic Arab tribes that have historically inhabited desert regions all across the Arab world.

genres.name: Bedroom Pop
genres.description: Named for solo producers and singer-songwriters from the 2010s onward who created intimate, "authentic" music in their own homes, outside of a traditional studio environment.

genres.name: Beijing New Sound
genres.description: Pioneering Chinese indie Rock movement in the late '90s that renewed the heavy narratives of early '90s Chinese rock with its stylish sound and personal themes.

genres.name: Beja Music
genres.description: Music of the Beja people of Africa’s Eastern Desert region.

genres.name: Belarusian Folk Music
genres.description: Eastern Slavic Folk Music, including traditional ceremonial, wedding, and harvest songs.

genres.name: Bele
genres.description: Drum-based folkdance with a strong Afro-influence, conducted by duos of dancers and accompanied by call-and-response singing, particularly popular in Martinique, Dominica and Trinidad and Tobago.

genres.name: Belgian Techno
genres.description: Early form of Hardcore [EDM], resulting from the further evolution of New Beat due to the strong influence of Techno and EBM.

genres.name: Belwo
genres.description: Somali poems with themes of love and romance and brief, syncopated tunes.

genres.name: Bend-skin
genres.description: Most closely linked to the Bamileke people of the Western Province of Cameroon; drums and improvised maracas are the sole instrumentation backing up a vocalist who alternates between rapping and singing.

genres.name: Benga
genres.description: Kenyan popular music based around the Traditional Folk Music of the Luo people from the area.

genres.name: Bengali Folk Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Bengali people found mainly in the Indian state of West Bengal and the country of Bangladesh.

genres.name: Beni
genres.description: Festive Zanzibari Marching Band music that emerged in the late 19th century.

genres.name: Benna
genres.description: Traditional music of Antigua & Barbuda, using call-and-response and bawdy lyrics.

genres.name: Beompae
genres.description: Korean genre of Buddhist chants and songs performed by monks while celebrating religious rituals in temples.

genres.name: Berlin School
genres.description: Atmospheric, multi-layered synthesizer textures; pioneered in Berlin in the 1970s as an offshoot to the Krautrock movement.

genres.name: Bernese Dialect Scene
genres.description: Influential scene of artists centered in the Swiss city of Bern, featuring poetic lyrics in Bernese German.

genres.name: Bhajan
genres.description: Song-based form of devotional music within Dharmic religions, with lyrical themes having an emphasis on deep adoration for a deity.

genres.name: Bhangra
genres.description: Percussion-driven blend of Punjabi Folk Music with modern Pop, with its name coming from a traditional folk dance celebrating the harvest.

genres.name: Bhojpuri Folk Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Bhojpuri people of India, originally from the states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

genres.name: Bhojpuri Pop
genres.description: Modernized pop-folk variant of Bhojpuri Folk Music.

genres.name: Big Band
genres.description: Commonly associated with the golden era of Swing in the 1930s and 1940s, performed by a large ensemble including brass, woodwinds, and usually a rhythm section.

genres.name: Big Beat
genres.description: Popular in Britain during the late 1990s, driven by edited breakbeats and prominent basslines.

genres.name: Big Music
genres.description: Rooted in Post-Punk and popular in the 1980s, with anthemic songwriting and a grandiose, stadium-ready sound.

genres.name: Big Room House
genres.description: Energetic, festival-oriented style characterized by heavy reverb, intense build-ups, strong kicks, minimalistic drop melodies, and sparse, raw breakdowns.

genres.name: Big Room Trance
genres.description: Incorporates production features associated with Big Room House and dirty, distorted leads influenced by Electro House, Dutch House and Hardstyle.

genres.name: Biguine
genres.description: Dating back to the 19th century; originating as a fusion of traditional Bele music with Polka.

genres.name: Bikutsi
genres.description: Developed from the Traditional Folk Music of the Ewondo people in Cameroon, with a name translating as "let's beat the earth" that comes from the stomping dance style that often accompanies it.

genres.name: Binaural Beats
genres.description: Auditory illusions created when two different frequencies are played simultaneously in separate ears.

genres.name: Biraha
genres.description: Call-and-response style of folk music developed from the Ahir and neighboring castes of the Bhojpuri people.

genres.name: Bird Sounds
genres.description: Recordings of birds, including vocalizations (songs and calls) and mechanical sounds produced by bills, wings, or feathers.

genres.name: Birmingham Sound
genres.description: Cold, mechanical, and hypnotic tracks, typically lacking the harsher and noisier elements of later Industrial Techno.

genres.name: Bit Music
genres.description: Created by sound chips, cards, and sequencers found in video game consoles, personal computers, and arcade machines, as well as synthesizers emulating these sounds.

genres.name: Bitpop
genres.description: Fuses Bit Music with additional synths, beats, guitars and modern production values, emphasizing highly catchy melodies and relatively fast tempos.

genres.name: Black 'n' Roll
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Hard Rock, Glam Rock, and Heavy Metal.

genres.name: Black Ambient
genres.description: Incorporates elements such as guitars, synthesizers, harsh or whispered vocals, raw production, or other elements associated with Black Metal and Dungeon Synth.

genres.name: Black Metal
genres.description: Highly distorted, treble-heavy guitars, tremolo-picked riffs, blast beats and double bass drumming, shrieked vocals, and raw, lo-fi production; often focuses on occult, dark imagery and atmosphere.

genres.name: Black MIDI
genres.description: Consists of extremely dense MIDI piano compositions, impossible to play on physical instruments.

genres.name: Black Noise
genres.description: Incorporates unconventional sounds with overpowering or constant Noise and Black Metal elements, often being heavily texture-oriented, abrasive, dissonant, atonal, or repetitive.

genres.name: Blackened Crust
genres.description: Borrows heavily from Black Metal production, blast beats, tremolo guitar, and vocals, while retaining the core Crust Punk sound, lyrical themes, and aesthetic.

genres.name: Blackgaze
genres.description: Fuses tremolo-picked riffing, intense drumming and harsh vocal techniques with mellow, dreamy textures, major-key melodies and extended build-ups.

genres.name: Bleep Techno
genres.description: Established in the late 1980s in the breakdancing and early rave scene of Yorkshire in the North of England, notable for its "bleepy" synth lines and heavy sub-bass.

genres.name: Bloghouse
genres.description: Internet-based movement from the mid-to-late-2000s which broadly distilled scenes most associated with online music blogging, mp3-sharing and remix culture, intersecting within Dance styles such as Electroclash, Electro House, New Rave and Nu-Disco in a brash and carefree fashion.

genres.name: Blue-Eyed Soul
genres.description: Usually refers to a Pop or Pop Rock song that contains strong Gospel-like elements, primarily popularized by white American and British singers in the 1960s through the 1980s.

genres.name: Bluegrass
genres.description: Born in the Appalachian region of the United States during the late 1930s, characterized by fingerpicked banjo along with other traditional instruments.

genres.name: Bluegrass Gospel
genres.description: Incorporates the religious topics and harmony vocals found in Country Gospel.

genres.name: Blues
genres.description: Originated toward the end of the 19th century in African American communities in the United States, particularly the Deep South; drew on traditional Spirituals and Work Song; highly influential to the whole of Western popular music.

genres.name: Blues Rock
genres.description: Relies on the chords/scales and instrumental improvisation of Blues.

genres.name: Bocet
genres.description: Traditional Romanian music sung by women mourning at a funeral.

genres.name: Boduberu
genres.description: Traditional, percussion-based form of music popular in the Maldives, usually following a crescendo structure.

genres.name: Bogino duu
genres.description: Mongolian Music with tuneful composition and simple structure.

genres.name: Bolero
genres.description: Ballad with a 2/4 time signature that appeared in eastern Cuba towards the end of the 19th century.

genres.name: Bolero español
genres.description: Spanish genre originating in the 18th century, based around moderate tempos in a 3/4 time signature accompanied by a dance of the same name.

genres.name: Bolero son
genres.description: Blend of Bolero and Son cubano that appeared during the 1920s.

genres.name: Bolero Việt Nam
genres.description: Romantic Vietnamese popular music, originating from standards mixing Latin American Bolero with local music.

genres.name: Bolero-Beat
genres.description: Latin American style stemming from both Canción melódica and the British Beat.

genres.name: Bolivian Huayño
genres.description: One of the most popular genres of Andean music in Bolivia, particularly present in the departments of Cochabamba, Chuquisaca, La Paz, Oruro and Potosí.

genres.name: Bomba
genres.description: Percussive style from Puerto Rico, generally considered to be derived from West Africa.

genres.name: Bongo Flava
genres.description: Tanzanian genre originating in the mid-1990s in the Dar es Salaam area, combining the influence of Rhythm & Blues, Afrobeat, and Dancehall with native Tanzanian styles like Taarab and Muziki wa dansi.

genres.name: Boogaloo
genres.description: Upbeat fusion of American Rhythm & Blues and Jazz with Son cubano which originated in the early 1960s in New York City and became popular with both its Black and Latino communities.

genres.name: Boogie
genres.description: Continuation of the Disco sound with increased influence from Funk, Synth Funk, and R&B and a slower tempo, often featuring drum machines and filter modulated synthesizers.

genres.name: Boogie Rock
genres.description: Straightforward groove-oriented style influenced by Rock & Roll and Boogie Woogie.

genres.name: Boogie Woogie
genres.description: Early, uptempo Blues featuring the piano as the main instrument, with soloing and improvisation played over the top of a repetitive eight note bassline.

genres.name: Boom Bap
genres.description: Production style identified by an acoustic-sounding drum pattern of a kick drum on the downbeat followed by a cracking snare on the upbeat.

genres.name: Bop
genres.description: Grew out of the Chicago Drill scene in the early 2010s, characterized by autotuned vocals and upbeat synth melodies.

genres.name: Bosnian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Bosnians.

genres.name: Bossa nova
genres.description: Conceived as a new style to perform original Samba, with major American Jazz influences.

genres.name: Bosstown Sound
genres.description: Short-lived Psychedelic Rock and Psychedelic Pop scene in Boston, Massachusetts; marketed by MGM Records as Boston’s response to the San Francisco Sound.

genres.name: Bounce
genres.description: Developed in New Orleans in the early 1990s, initially defined by a slow to midtempo beat with a double-time hi-hat on top.

genres.name: Bounce Beat
genres.description: Modernized, youth oriented form heavily utilizing rototoms, timbale and keyboards for grooves.

genres.name: Bouncy Techno
genres.description: Average tempo of 160 to 180 BPM, four-on-the-floor beats, melodic and repetitive synth melodies, drums with hard kicks, short breaks, progressive stomping rhythms, and offbeat notes.

genres.name: Bouyon
genres.description: With a name translating to "broth", this fast-paced genre from Dominica originated as a blend of various traditional and modern Caribbean styles.

genres.name: Boy Band
genres.description: Male vocal groups often put together by talent managers or record producers.

genres.name: Brazilian Bass
genres.description: Originated in the 2010s in Brazil, taking influences from Deep House and Tech House, characterized by deep, punchy basslines making use of detuning and filtering effects.

genres.name: Brazilian Classical Music
genres.description: Originated in the late 19th century, taking the European music that had been brought to the country by colonists and brought in parts of Brazilian Music.

genres.name: Brazilian Folk Music
genres.description: Comprises the various traditions of folk music found in Brazil, often resulting from the interplay of Indigenous, African and European music.

genres.name: Brazilian Music
genres.description: All forms of music with roots in Brazil.

genres.name: Brazilian Phonk
genres.description: Merges Funk automotivo's rhythms, vocals, and energy, with the energetic and nocturnal production typical of the Drift Phonk scene, and Phonk House.

genres.name: Break-In
genres.description: Comedy with narrator posing questions or commentary, answered with a song sample.

genres.name: Breakbeat
genres.description: Syncopated drum patterns (breakbeats), generally driving the groove at 110-160 BPM, emerging in the late 1980s from sampling drum breaks, before forming an umbrella genre separate from Drum and Bass, Downtempo, and Hip Hop.

genres.name: Breakbeat Hardcore
genres.description: Originated from the combination of sampled breakbeats and energetic rhythms with the "rave" influences set by early-1990s Techno and Acid House, including upbeat "stab" riffing and sample-based production.

genres.name: Breakbeat Kota
genres.description: Indonesian style that slows down the syncopated rhythms of Funkot to moderate tempos around 130 BPM.

genres.name: Breakcore
genres.description: Mixes Hardcore [EDM] with cut-up, complex, and frequently noisy breakbeats at very high tempos inspired by Jungle and Drum and Bass, often with heavy use of sampling.

genres.name: Breakstep
genres.description: Hard-hitting Breakbeat rhythms and heavy, rolling basslines.

genres.name: Brega
genres.description: Overstated, dramatic music with a romantic singing style.

genres.name: Brega calypso
genres.description: Romantic vocals and lyrics, bubbly and sensual melodies and rhythms, horn sections and lush Caribbean-like guitar riffs over fast tempos.

genres.name: Brega funk
genres.description: Rooted in Tecnobrega, features glossy syncopated MIDI pianos and synths, distinct pitched metallic snares and vocal chops over a wonky kick rhythm.

genres.name: Breton Celtic Folk Music
genres.description: Movement in the Brittany region of France which translated Celtic Folk Music from Ireland and Scotland into the Celtic Breton language.

genres.name: Breton Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Brittany region in France, including Breton Celtic Folk Music and music in the regional Romance language, Gallo.

genres.name: Briddim
genres.description: Combining the kick-clap rhythms and syncopation of Riddim with Brostep sound design.

genres.name: Brill Building
genres.description: Elaborate, polished, and typically melodramatic composition and arrangement associated with the songwriting teams at the Brill office building during the late 1950s and early 1960s.

genres.name: Bristol Sound
genres.description: UK-based scene associated with Bristol's soundsystem culture and early Trip Hop within the late 1980s to late 1990s, featuring a bass-heavy, spaced-out sound largely inspired by Dub, Soul and Hip Hop.

genres.name: Britcore
genres.description: British subgenre from the late 1980s and early 1990s featuring fast breakbeats and rapping.

genres.name: Britfunk
genres.description: Energetic, up-tempo style born out of late-1970s British Jazz-Funk nightclubs.

genres.name: British Blues
genres.description: Heavily influenced by the burgeoning United States Blues scene, particularly Chicago Blues.

genres.name: British Brass Band
genres.description: An ensemble consisting of a standardized range of brass and percussion instruments whose performances are based on the British tradition established in the early 19th century.

genres.name: British Dance Band
genres.description: Came from the dancehalls of the 1920s and 1930s, combining a British take on Jazz with the Music Hall tradition.

genres.name: British Folk Rock
genres.description: Developed in the late 1960s; influenced by traditional British folk music, particularly English Folk Music.

genres.name: British Music
genres.description: Music of Great Britain, including the music of the English, Welsh and Scottish people.

genres.name: British Rhythm & Blues
genres.description: A style infusing Rock and R&B that was hugely popular in the United Kingdom between 1963 and 1966.

genres.name: British Trad Jazz
genres.description: Popular mid-1950s to early '60s revival of Dixieland; pushed out commercially by Beat music in 1963.

genres.name: Britpop
genres.description: Emerged in the United Kingdom in the early 1990s, with a style hearkening back to the traditional guitar-driven songs and melodic hooks found in the British Pop Rock of the 1960s.

genres.name: Brno Alternative Scene
genres.description: Semi-official, avant-garde scene active primarily in the the 1980s in the Czech Socialist Republic.

genres.name: Bro-Country
genres.description: 21st century style with an often party-oriented sound and lyrical content, taking strong influence from Hard Rock, Hip Hop and Pop.

genres.name: Broadband Noise
genres.description: Audio signals with energy distributed across a wide range of frequencies; usually split into "colours" of noise and often marketed for relaxation or as a sleep aid.

genres.name: Broken Beat
genres.description: Choppy, syncopated grooves and loose influence from 1970s Jazz-Funk, with eclectic roots spanning Drum and Bass, Deep House, Acid Jazz, and Afrobeat.

genres.name: Broken Transmission
genres.description: Manipulates samples from TV broadcasts, advertisements, film, radio, and other sources.

genres.name: Bronx Drill
genres.description: Bronx scene that popularized Sample Drill and aggressive New York Drill delivery and production in the early 2020s.

genres.name: Brony Music
genres.description: Fan works, created by the brony community, relating to the My Little Pony franchise.

genres.name: Brooklyn Drill
genres.description: Brooklyn scene that kickstarted New York Drill in the mid-2010s, primarily through adopted UK Drill production.

genres.name: Brostep
genres.description: Offshoot of Dubstep which replaces its sub-bass-oriented sound with an emphasis on catchy or aggressive mid-range melodies.

genres.name: Brukdown
genres.description: Belizean Creole genre typified by the use of accordion, banjo, and a distinctive percussion section.

genres.name: Brutal Death Metal
genres.description: Emphasizes abrasiveness, chunky rhythmic atonal riffs, and low guttural vocals.

genres.name: Brutal Prog
genres.description: Highly intense and visceral songwriting, usually featuring substantial reliance on dissonance, odd time signatures, blistering tempos, angular and mercurial rhythms, and Punk's DIY attitude.

genres.name: Bubblegum
genres.description: Upbeat, catchy, simple, and targeted at children and young teens; especially popular in the 1960s and 1970s.

genres.name: Bubblegum Bass
genres.description: Originated in the early 2010s, exaggerating the cutest and most feminine parts of 2000s Pop and combining them with bouncy, plastic synths over rhythms and sounds derived from a variety of contemporary club styles.

genres.name: Bubblegum Dance
genres.description: Playful, childlike style with a Bubblegum-like atmosphere that often incorporates high-pitched, light-hearted, and usually female-fronted vocals.

genres.name: Bubbling
genres.description: Originating in the Netherlands in the late 1980s, fusing sped-up Dancehall with Dutch Antillean music and contemporary Dutch rave.

genres.name: Bubbling House
genres.description: Developed in the Netherlands in the 2000s, combining the older style of Bubbling with more modern House, especially Dutch House.

genres.name: Buddhist Music
genres.description: Encompassing the various musical practices that have developed throughout Buddhist history and across the many regions Buddhism spread to.

genres.name: Budots
genres.description: Originated from the southern Philippines; notable for its distinct high-pitched synth hooks.

genres.name: Buganda Royal Court Music
genres.description: Highest traditional and refined musical forms of Buganda, reserved for the Kabaka (the king of Buganda).

genres.name: Bugle Call
genres.description: Short tunes played on a bugle; used in militaries for communication.

genres.name: Bulawayo Jazz
genres.description: Emerged from the city of Bulawayo, Zimbabwe in the early 1950s, led by the alto sax and accompanied by ensembles.

genres.name: Bulería
genres.description: Fast flamenco made up of a 12 beat cycle characterized by its vibrant, spontaneous and festive style.

genres.name: Bulgarian Folk Music
genres.description: Consists of a variety of traditions and styles, with distinct sounds originating from current and historical regions such as Sofia, Dobrudzha, Macedonia and Thrace.

genres.name: Bullerengue
genres.description: Afro-Colombian popular genre which features a strong emphasis on rhythm and improvisation and a call-and-response format.

genres.name: Burger-Highlife
genres.description: Created by Ghanaian immigrants to Germany in the late 1970s, generally employing synthesizers and Western post-production techniques alongside guitar-driven Highlife instrumentation.

genres.name: Burmese Classical Music
genres.description: Traditional court music of Myanmar, developed from Southeast Asian, Hindu and Chinese influences.

genres.name: Burning Spirits
genres.description: Emphasis on delivering a very energetic and triumphant sound with flashy and soaring Metal solos, "melodramatic" or "uplifting" chord progressions, and singalong, over the top, harsh vocals.

genres.name: Burrakatha
genres.description: Traditional form of narrative music, featuring a tambura player paired with two drummers who interrupt the main storyteller to provide additional remarks.

genres.name: Burushaski Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Burusho people of northern Pakistan.

genres.name: Buryat Music
genres.description: Music of the Buryat people, an ethnic group native to the Republic of Buryatia in Russian Far East.

genres.name: Byzantine Chant
genres.description: Liturgical chant of Christian churches following the Orthodox rite.

genres.name: Byzantine Music
genres.description: Music from Byzantine era.

genres.name: Bérite Club
genres.description: Originated in the underground club scene of Paris in the mid-to-late 2010s, drawing on a variety of international club styles for its combination of prominent and erratic drum programming with freezing and looping chopped-up samples.

genres.name: C-Pop
genres.description: Commercialized style performed by Chinese communities across China and Taiwan, alongside its large diaspora.

genres.name: C86
genres.description: Distinctly ramshackle, often Twee Pop-infused combination of British Indie Rock and Jangle Pop.

genres.name: Ca trù
genres.description: Sung poetry from northern Vietnam, performed by a female vocalist to the accompaniment of a three-stringed lute and percussion.

genres.name: Cabaret
genres.description: Entertainment featuring Comedy, song, dance, and theatre.

genres.name: Cabo-Zouk
genres.description: Popular in Cape Verde and the Cape Verdean diaspora in Europe and North America, with a slow and sensuous tempo, and favoring more sophisticated studio productions.

genres.name: Cadence lypso
genres.description: Caribbean genre originating in the 1970s, combining elements of Haiti's Cadence rampa and Compas with Trinidad's Calypso.

genres.name: Cadence rampa
genres.description: Developed in parallel with Compas, based on Méringue with a stronger Cuban influence.

genres.name: Cajun Music
genres.description: Associated with the Cajun people of Louisiana where the genre was born, commonly regarded as an uptempo, accordion-driven style with a harsh, infectious beat.

genres.name: Cakewalk
genres.description: Typically in 2/4 time with a distinctive "oompah" rhythm, named for a dance created by enslaved Black Americans as a mockery of the social dances of white slaveholders.

genres.name: Calipso venezolano
genres.description: Derived from Trinidadian Calypso, popular in the eastern region of Venezuela and associated with Carnival.

genres.name: Calypso
genres.description: Genre from Trinidad and Tobago featuring a brass section and percussion.

genres.name: Cambodian Pop
genres.description: Popular music produced in Cambodia or by Khmer people.

genres.name: Campursari
genres.description: Javanese form of popular music originating as a mixture of local Gamelan with Western elements.

genres.name: Campus Folk
genres.description: Born in Taiwan in the mid-1970s, this movement originated with university students creating their own modern-style songs in the wake of international tensions like Taiwan's isolation from the United Nations and the United States' embrace of the PRC as a diplomatic partner.

genres.name: Canadian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional folk of the European settlers who arrived in Canada.

genres.name: Canadian Maritime Folk
genres.description: Traditional folk of Canada's Maritimes (Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and New Brunswick).

genres.name: Canarian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional folk of the Canary Islands.

genres.name: Canción melódica
genres.description: Sentimental vocal music sung in Spanish with a focus on the chorus, originally developed in the first half of the 20th century from a variety of traditional Hispanic genres.

genres.name: Candombe
genres.description: Uruguayan popular music originating among Montevideo's Afro-Uruguayan population, based on three differently-sized drums.

genres.name: Candombe beat
genres.description: Fusion of Uruguayan Candombe with elements of Rock music.

genres.name: Candomblé Music
genres.description: Music of the Afro-Brazilian Candomblé religion that influenced the secular Afoxé.

genres.name: Cantata
genres.description: Vocal style for solo singers with instrumental & Choral accompaniment comparable to Oratorio, though often smaller in scale, more songlike, and with less focus on dramatic narrative.

genres.name: Cante alentejano
genres.description: Traditional Portuguese Music based on vocal music from the Alentejo region.

genres.name: Canterbury Scene
genres.description: Developed in the counterculture of Canterbury in the late 1960s, emphasizing the influence of Jazz-Rock and Jazz Fusion.

genres.name: Canto a lo poeta
genres.description: Sung poetry traditional to Chile and transmitted orally from one generation to another.

genres.name: Canto beneventano
genres.description: Extinct plainchant tradition of Southern Italy characterized by lengthy melodies, extensive use of repetition, and a steady, undulating progression.

genres.name: Canto cardenche
genres.description: Overtly dramatic, and melancholic A cappella performed in the Comarca Lagunera region in northeast Mexico.

genres.name: Canto degli Alpini
genres.description: Created and traditionally sung by choirs formed from the Italian army's Alpine mountain infantry corps, mainly dating back to WWI.

genres.name: Canto mozárabe
genres.description: Iberian form of plainchant that flourished roughly 550-1085 AD.

genres.name: Cantopop
genres.description: Modern commercial Pop music sung in the Cantonese language, usually produced in Hong Kong or adjacent regions.

genres.name: Cantoria
genres.description: Sung poetry of itinerant cantadores from Northeastern Brazil.

genres.name: Cantu a tenore
genres.description: Secular Polyphonic Chant from the Mediterranean island of Sardinia.

genres.name: Canzona
genres.description: Song-like structures and a contrapuntal texture technique known as imitation.

genres.name: Canzone d'autore
genres.description: Music of the Italian Singer-Songwriters that emerged in the 1960s and early 1970s, initially influenced by French Chanson with the addition of uniquely Italian sensibilities.

genres.name: Canzone napoletana
genres.description: Sung in the Neapolitan language by a male voice with instrumental accompaniment, originating in the Italian city of Naples and the surrounding regions.

genres.name: Canzone neomelodica
genres.description: Elements are derived from Canzone napoletana.

genres.name: Cape Breton Folk Music
genres.description: Celtic Folk Music that emerged in Cape Breton, an island at the eastern shore of Nova Scotia, through immigrants from Scotland and Ireland.

genres.name: Cape Jazz
genres.description: Developed parallel to American Jazz in the early 20th century, named for its origin in Cape Town, South Africa.

genres.name: Cape Verdean Music
genres.description: Music developed in the archipelago of Cape Verde.

genres.name: Capoeira Music
genres.description: Afro-Brazilian style that accompanies and sets the rhythm and energy of the capoeira martial art, originating in the 19th century with the relocation of African slaves to the states of Bahia and Rio de Janeiro.

genres.name: Caporal
genres.description: Bolivian neofolkloric dance music characterized by a double beat bass drum pattern that emerged in the latter half of the twentieth century.

genres.name: Capriccio
genres.description: Typically short and loosely structured, characterized by spontaneity, humor, and technicality.

genres.name: Car Audio Bass
genres.description: Slow and minimalistic extreme form, focused on ultra-low frequency sine wave notes and mainly intended for stress testing subwoofer sound systems.

genres.name: Caribbean Folk Music
genres.description: Meta-genre that covers the different forms of Traditional Folk Music from the Caribbean.

genres.name: Caribbean Music
genres.description: Meta-genre covering all forms with roots in the Caribbean region.

genres.name: Carimbó
genres.description: Originated in rural areas in the state of Pará, danced frenetically to the beat of syncopated drums, with international recognition after its modernization.

genres.name: Carnatic Classical Music
genres.description: Culture shared by the Dravidian cultures in South India separate from regional folk genres.

genres.name: Carnaval cruceño
genres.description: Danceable genre, similar to the Polka, from the city of Santa Cruz, Bolivia, characteristic of the area’s Carnival celebrations and generally composed for brass band musicians.

genres.name: Carnavalito
genres.description: Fast and lively; mostly played in northwestern Argentina in the provinces of Jujuy, Salta, and Tucumán.

genres.name: Carranga
genres.description: Colombian folk music that originated in Boyacá province, best known for its wordplay and humorous lyrics.

genres.name: Cartoon Music
genres.description: Zany and uptempo; incorporates elements of Western Classical Music and Modern Classical into frantic Big Band arrangements, playfully chaotic to match the on-screen actions of Cartoon characters and the beat of their movements.

genres.name: Cascadian Black Metal
genres.description: Scene hailing from the Pacific Northwest region of the United States and Canada marked by nature-centric imagery, oftentimes incorporating elements of Post-Metal.

genres.name: Catalan Folk Music
genres.description: Blend of local styles and influences from the Iberian Peninsula region and the Catalonian area of Southern France.

genres.name: Caucasian Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Caucasus region, a mountainous area that connects Eastern Europe to Asia.

genres.name: Caucasian Music
genres.description: Music of the region of the Caucasus, a mountainous region bordered by Russia to the north and Turkey/Iran to the south, with the Black and Caspian seas to its sides.

genres.name: CBGB Scene
genres.description: Early Punk scene built around artists who frequently played at the East Village's CBGB club in the mid-1970s.

genres.name: CCM
genres.description: Popular music focused on Christian spirituality and faith.

genres.name: Celtic Chant
genres.description: Extinct tradition of Catholic liturgical chant developed by the Celtic Christians of Britain, Ireland, and Brittany.

genres.name: Celtic Electronica
genres.description: Fusion of Celtic Folk Music with various types of Electronic Dance Music.

genres.name: Celtic Folk Music
genres.description: Derived from Celtic traditions of Ireland, Scotland, Wales, Cornwall, the Isle of Man, Brittany, Galicia, Cantabria, Asturias, and Trás-os-Montes (Portugal).

genres.name: Celtic Metal
genres.description: Features Celtic Folk Music elements.

genres.name: Celtic New Age
genres.description: Incorporates influences and performing styles from Celtic Folk Music, emphasizing pastoral imagery and wistful themes.

genres.name: Celtic Punk
genres.description: Infuses the sounds of Celtic Folk Music into Punk Rock.

genres.name: Celtic Rock
genres.description: Incorporates influences from Celtic Folk Music and its regional variants.

genres.name: Central African Music
genres.description: Music of the areas speaking Adamawa-Eastern languages and many Bantu languages, through most of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, all of Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, the islands of São Tomé and Príncipe, Republic of the Congo, most of the Central African Republic, and large parts of Cameroon, Angola, and the northern parts of Zambia.

genres.name: Central American Music
genres.description: Music from the Central American region (including Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama).

genres.name: Central Asian Music
genres.description: Music of the former Soviet Central Asian republics, Mongolia, Western China and related neighbouring peoples.

genres.name: Central Asian Throat Singing
genres.description: Shared polyphonic vocal tradition of Mongolia and southern Siberia characterised by complex manipulation of harmonics.

genres.name: Chacarera
genres.description: Originated in northwest Argentina and southern Bolivia around 1850, typically in 6/8 and traditionally performed with instruments like the guitar, bombo legüero (traditional drum), and violin.

genres.name: Chachachá
genres.description: Ballroom dance music derived from Danzón.

genres.name: Chalga
genres.description: Bulgarian blend of Contemporary Folk (Turkish, Bulgarian, Arabic & Romani) with Dance-Pop.

genres.name: Chamamé
genres.description: Mixes native Guaraní music with Polka paraguaya and European schottische music.

genres.name: Chamamé tropical
genres.description: Takes heavy influence from the energy and instrumentation of Cumbia, popular in the late 1970s and 1980s.

genres.name: Chamarrita açoriana
genres.description: Refers to a popular folkloric dance, of the Azores islands, as well as the accompanying music.

genres.name: Chamarrita rioplatense
genres.description: Traditional genre and dance featuring similar rhythms to Milonga and typically performed with the guitar and accordion.

genres.name: Chamber Folk
genres.description: Gentle fingerpicked acoustic guitar or harp-led music that commonly includes a backing ensemble of harpsichords, strings, horns, or other orchestral instruments.

genres.name: Chamber Jazz
genres.description: Made by mostly small acoustic-based ensembles with emphasized improvisation and influenced by Neoclassicism and Traditional Folk Music.

genres.name: Chamber Music
genres.description: Western Classical Music performed by a small ensemble, usually only a few performers.

genres.name: Chamber Pop
genres.description: Based on the smooth and melodic songwriting of Lounge and other Easy Listening, as well as the orchestration of Baroque Pop and the production styles of other 1960s pop genres.

genres.name: Champeta
genres.description: Colombian genre heavily influenced by the traditional music of San Basilio de Palenque as well as modern Caribbean and African sensibilities.

genres.name: Changa tuki
genres.description: Emerged in Caracas; highly influenced by 1990s Techno and Tribal House, featuring fast tempos, strident synthesizers, hard-thumping percussion lines, and plenty of breakbeats.

genres.name: Change Ringing
genres.description: English tradition of ringing tuned bells in accordance with mathematically-derived patterns, creating a distinctive cascading effect.

genres.name: Changjak gugak
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-twentieth century as an attempt to preserve the sound of Korea's traditional music while adapting it to modern sensibilities and Western compositional norms.

genres.name: Changüí
genres.description: One of the oldest popular Cuban styles, originating in the 19th century with slaves that worked in sugar refineries near Baracoa who combined elements of Spanish popular songs with Bantu traditions.

genres.name: Chanson
genres.description: French-language Singer-Songwriters for whom the quality of the text is essential and where the rhythm follows that of the text.

genres.name: Chanson alternative
genres.description: Usually politically engaged and humorous with eclectic influences of Regional Music, especially Fanfare, Musette, Jazz manouche and Romani Folk Music.

genres.name: Chanson québécoise
genres.description: French-language music of the Québécois singer-songwriters.

genres.name: Chanson réaliste
genres.description: Very popular in France in the late 19th century up to World War II, typically performed by female singers in a Cabaret or Vaudeville style and featuring "realist" lyrics.

genres.name: Chanson à texte
genres.description: French-language songs emphasising sophisticated and poetic lyricism.

genres.name: Chaozhou xianshi
genres.description: Traditional and instrumental ensemble music originating from Chaozhou; played mainly on stringed instruments.

genres.name: Chap Hop
genres.description: Satirises British cultural stereotypes with posh rapping and a distinctive retro aesthetic drawn from the "chap" and steampunk subcultures, often with elements of Music Hall.

genres.name: Character Piece
genres.description: Broad instrumental genre, usually for solo piano, written to evoke an extramusical concept or mood.

genres.name: Chazzanut
genres.description: Traditions used by the Jewish cantor, the chazzan when reciting and chanting different parts of the Jewish prayer in Jewish Liturgical Music.

genres.name: Chechen Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Chechens, a Northeast Caucasian ethnic group predominantly living in the Republic of Chechnya, a federal subject of Russia.

genres.name: Chicago Blues
genres.description: Heavily inspired by old-time rural blues, transferring it into a small band setup, while maintaining the rough and gritty edges of its ancestry.

genres.name: Chicago Drill
genres.description: Bass-heavy, dense, and typically syncopated percussion, featuring ticking hi-hats and gunshot-like snare rolls, usually accompanied by menacing synth melodies and violent Gangsta Rap lyricism.

genres.name: Chicago Hard House
genres.description: Originated from Chicago around the mid-1990s as a development of Ghetto House, emphasizing hard-hitting, off-beat drum patterns, fast tempos, and lack of melodies.

genres.name: Chicago House
genres.description: Umbrella term for a broad variety of House that originated from Chicago in the (mostly mid-to-late) 1980s and early 90s.

genres.name: Chicago No Wave
genres.description: 1990s Experimental Rock scene in Chicago, Illinois; so named due to its deconstructionist approach to Rock music, similar to that of the No Wave scene in late 1970s New York City.

genres.name: Chicago Polka
genres.description: Polish-American style known for slower tempo, improvisation and the ensemble typically including the clarinet, trumpet, and concertina.

genres.name: Chicago School
