genres.description: Predominantly 1990s Post-Rock scene which blends influences from Indie Rock and Jazz with an expanded instrumental palette and a diverse approach to sonic exploration.

genres.name: Chicago Soul
genres.description: Combination of the hard, groove-oriented rhythms of Southern Soul and the sophisticated gloss of the Motown Sound which was developed in Chicago.

genres.name: Chicano Rap
genres.description: Latin Rap with a Mexican twist.

genres.name: Chicha
genres.description: Emerged during the Andean migration to the Peruvian coast between the 1960s and 1980s; largely influenced by Huayno and occasionally Psychedelic Rock

genres.name: Children's Music
genres.description: Recorded for an intended audience of children.

genres.name: Chilean Music
genres.description: Music developed by the Chilean people.

genres.name: Chilena
genres.description: Developed when music from the Costa Chica of Guerrero and Oaxaca in Mexico mixed with Cueca brought by Chilean sailors to the region in the 19th century.

genres.name: Chillout
genres.description: Broad category of many relaxed styles of Electronic music which predominantly draw influence from Electronic Dance Music subgenres and Ambient.

genres.name: Chillstep
genres.description: Relaxed Dubstep influenced by Downtempo and Ambient.

genres.name: Chillsynth
genres.description: Mixes Synthwave with major Chillwave elements, characterized by a dreamy and relaxed sound.

genres.name: Chillwave
genres.description: Emulates vintage aesthetics and popular musical styles of the 1980s/1990s altered by modern recording technology to create a hazy dreamlike atmosphere.

genres.name: Chilote Music
genres.description: Music of the Chiloé Archipelago.

genres.name: Chimaychi
genres.description: Slower variant, traditionally lacking guitar or mandolin, found in the eastern provinces of Áncash department.

genres.name: Chimurenga
genres.description: Popular style from Zimbabwe based on the traditional mbira thumb piano, but with electric instrumentation as well.

genres.name: Chinese Classical Music
genres.description: Classical Music of China, encompassing royal court music.

genres.name: Chinese Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional folk of the Chinese people.

genres.name: Chinese Literati Music
genres.description: Music of the Chinese literati; primarily played on the guqin and invoking emotional restraint, self-cultivation, and introspection.

genres.name: Chinese Music
genres.description: Music of the Chinese people, which is primarily derived from the culture of the Han Chinese.

genres.name: Chinese Opera
genres.description: Traditional Chinese theatre, existing in several regional variations, combining traditional instruments and vocals along with other art forms like Poetry, dance, acrobatics, and martial arts.

genres.name: Chipmunk Soul
genres.description: Sped-up vocal samples and slick, soulful production.

genres.name: Chiptune
genres.description: Used primarily in the 1980s within the context of 8-bit Video Game Music, combining simple synthesized waveforms and noise in a compositionally limited but overtly melodic style.

genres.name: Chopped and Screwed
genres.description: Remixing technique that consists of skipping effects ("chopping") and dropping the tempo ("screwing").

genres.name: Chopper
genres.description: Originated in the American Midwest in the 1990s; initially defined by slow jam beats rapped over with very fast flows and resonant choruses.

genres.name: Choral
genres.description: Choir-sung classical works covering periods from medieval music (an early form being Gregorian Chant) up to present day.

genres.name: Choral Concerto
genres.description: Composition for unaccompanied choir, set to sacred texts of Eastern Orthodox tradition.

genres.name: Choral Symphony
genres.description: Combines symphonic Orchestral Music forces & structure with vocal parts for choir.

genres.name: Choro
genres.description: Brazilian urban genre named after the crying-like harmony generated by the very particular group of instruments used to play it: seven-string acoustic guitar, mandolin, flute, cavaquinho, and pandeiro.

genres.name: Chotis madrileño
genres.description: Spanish variant of schottisch, a slow version of German Polka which developed through the incorporation of regional folk influences and an association with the local castizo culture in Madrid, the capital of Spain.

genres.name: Christian Hardcore
genres.description: Developed in the 1990s in the United States, incorporating faith-based Christian messages into Hardcore [Punk] music.

genres.name: Christian Hip Hop
genres.description: Employs lyrics with a pro-Christianity message to profess the performer's faith, often to attract attention from new potential converts.

genres.name: Christian Liturgical Music
genres.description: Traditionally accompanies church services, as well as extra-liturgical functions such as processionals and sermons.

genres.name: Christian Rock
genres.description: Incorporates Christian lyrics, with topics such as faith, metaphysics, or biblical characters.

genres.name: Chukchi Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Chukchi people.

genres.name: Chuntunqui romántico
genres.description: Vibrant Bolivian genre set in 6/8 meter featuring choral refrains, harmonic progressions, and lyrics exploring the subject of romantic love.

genres.name: Chutney
genres.description: Indo-Caribbean genre developing as a fusion of Bhojpuri Folk Music with traditional Caribbean songs; later influenced by Calypso, Soca and Filmi.

genres.name: Chutney Soca
genres.description: Mixture of Soca rhythms with Chutney's Indo-Caribbean traits and instrumentation.

genres.name: Chuvash Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Chuvash people.

genres.name: Chèo
genres.description: Northern Vietnamese folk musical theatre, characterized by minimal set design and satirical content.

genres.name: Chöd
genres.description: Tibetan Buddhist and Bönpo practice incorporating ritualized liturgical chants and instrumental accompaniment from the chöd damaru, drilbu, and kangling.

genres.name: Cinematic Classical
genres.description: Orchestral compositions generally associated with soundtracks to modern high-budget films, games, and other non-live media.

genres.name: Circassian Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the native Circassian peoples of Northern Caucasus, residing in the Republics of Adygea, Karachay-Cherkessia, and Kabardino-Balkaria respectively, which are federal subjects of the Russian Federation, as well as the territories of the former Ottoman Empire, with a significant diaspora population in modern Turkey.

genres.name: Circus March
genres.description: Marches composed for use in circuses, one of the most popular forms of entertainment in the early 20th century.

genres.name: City Pop
genres.description: Wave of Japanese Pop intended to reflect urban life during the period of the country's booming economy in the 1970s and 1980s, featuring a contemporary Western sound and lush arrangements.

genres.name: Classic Ragtime
genres.description: Draws on the complexity and formal structures of Western Classical Music, cycling through multiple strains (themes); emerged from Missouri's Sedalia school.

genres.name: Classical Crossover
genres.description: Takes specific Western Classical Music conventions and applies them into a straightfoward Pop context for mainstream appeal.

genres.name: Classical Music
genres.description: Part of a broad generalization about the structure and function of music throughout history across the globe, describing traditions distinct from Traditional Folk Music and popular music.

genres.name: Classical Period
genres.description: Refers to the phase in Western Classical Music history occurring from roughly 1750 to 1820, characterized by its emphasis on clarity, simplicity, and balance.

genres.name: Cleveland Punk
genres.description: Early Punk scene in Cleveland, Ohio during the 1970s and early 1980s.

genres.name: Close Harmony
genres.description: Traditional two-part harmony singing performed mostly by brothers.

genres.name: Cloud Rap
genres.description: Emerged in the early 2010s, known for its relaxed, dream-like, and reverb-heavy production style, taking influence from Chillwave, and producers' obscure sample choices.

genres.name: Clube da esquina
genres.description: Brazilian movement from the state of Minas Gerais, mostly active in the 1960s and 1970s.

genres.name: Cocktail Nation
genres.description: Decidedly ironic take on Lounge that emerged in the early 1990s.

genres.name: Coco
genres.description: Performers usually gather in a circle which rounds the dancers, clapping and spinning according to the rhythm; influenced by cultures originating from Africa, conceived in Northeastern Brazil.

genres.name: Coke Rap
genres.description: Lyrics with heavy reference to street-level drug dealing, specifically cocaine.

genres.name: Coladeira
genres.description: Originated as a more uptempo and lively form of Morna before bringing in outside influences.

genres.name: Coldwave
genres.description: Originated in Europe in the late 1970s and early 1980s and is known for its generally dark, gloomy atmosphere and heavy reliance on synthesizers.

genres.name: Colinde
genres.description: Christmas music from Romanian folklore with ritualistic and pagan roots.

genres.name: Colour Bass
genres.description: Combines aggressive wobbling basses with the euphoric drops of Melodic Dubstep and Future Bass.

genres.name: Comedy
genres.description: Range of styles, both musical and non-musical, that always set out to make the listener laugh through humor.

genres.name: Comedy Rap
genres.description: Primarily intended to be humorous, through the use of comedic lyrics, production, delivery, or other musical aspects.

genres.name: Comedy Rock
genres.description: Roughly defined as a mix of Rock or any of its subgenres with elements of Comedy such as Satire and Musical Parody, as well as concepts of Novelty.

genres.name: Comfy Synth
genres.description: Calm, peaceful and soothing sounds, as well as nostalgic, sentimental, or childish atmospheres and aesthetics; often incorporates wholesome themes while utilizing lo-fi or hazy recordings and influences from New Age.

genres.name: Comorian Music
genres.description: Music of the Comoros Islands and Mayotte off the eastern coast of Africa, combining influences from other East African Music and Malagasy Music.

genres.name: Compas
genres.description: Popular genre from Haiti, updating the older Méringue style with influences from Mambo and Jazz.

genres.name: Complextro
genres.description: Features densely-layered sound design, fast-paced cut-up sections, aggressive stabs, and common crossover with Brostep and Fidget House.

genres.name: Comédie-ballet
genres.description: French form of musical drama from the 17th century that combines operatic singing, classical dance, and theater.

genres.name: Concertina Band
genres.description: Ensemble consisting of concertinas of various pitches and percussion instruments originating in 19th-century England.

genres.name: Concerto
genres.description: Multi-movement classical works for one or more soloists and an ensemble.

genres.name: Concerto for Orchestra
genres.description: Mostly modern form in which virtuosic solo passages are alternately played among different portions of the orchestra.

genres.name: Concerto grosso
genres.description: Oldest form developed during the Baroque Music era in which the body of the music is alternately shared between a small group of soloists and a larger orchestra.

genres.name: Conducted Improvisation
genres.description: Collective improvisation directed by a conductor.

genres.name: Conga
genres.description: Evolved alongside Rumba cubana in the late 19th century, featuring large and heterogenous percussion sections performing simple and syncopated rhythms alongside a small wind section.

genres.name: Congolese Rumba
genres.description: Blend of Congolese musical elements with Cuban Music (specifically Son cubano and  Rumba cubana) popular between the 1940s and early 1970s.

genres.name: Conjunto andino
genres.description: Urban folk ensembles using musical instruments of Andean Indigenous origin or association; despite frequent association with Indigenous villages, they bear little resemblance to the Indigenous expressions of the Southern Andes.

genres.name: Conscious Hip Hop
genres.description: Artists whose lyrics deal with social issues.

genres.name: Contemporary Country
genres.description: Incorporates both heavily Pop-influenced styles, and the more pop-averse movement of Neo-Traditionalist Country.

genres.name: Contemporary Folk
genres.description: Generally acoustic and rooted in modernized Traditional Folk Music, originated with the 20th century American folk revival.

genres.name: Contemporary R&B
genres.description: Soulful, passionate and melismatic vocals originally derived from popular Soul and Disco, as well as smooth, lush and often synthesized production variously influenced by Hip Hop, Funk, and related strands of Pop.

genres.name: Contenance angloise
genres.description: Distinct style of Polyphonic Chant developed in fifteenth-century England.

genres.name: Cool Jazz
genres.description: Developed in the late 1940s alongside and in response to Bebop, featuring a more restrained, emotionally "cool" style.

genres.name: Coon Song
genres.description: Lyrical trend popular in the United States from around 1880 to 1920 that presents a racist and highly stereotyped image of African Americans connected with the subject matter and style of minstrel shows.

genres.name: Copla
genres.description: Evolved from Spanish theatrical styles like Cuplé and has strong links to Flamenco.

genres.name: Coptic Music
genres.description: Church music specifically made for worship in the Coptic (Egyptian) Orthodox Church.

genres.name: Cornish Folk Music
genres.description: Musical traditions developed by the Cornish people, mainly found in the county of Cornwall in South West England.

genres.name: Corrido
genres.description: Narrative ballad which arose in the late 18th century and flourished after the Mexican Independence War, originally meant for folk singers to spread news throughout Mexico accompanied by a guitar.

genres.name: Corsican Folk Music
genres.description: French folk from Corsica, sung mainly in Corsican and sometimes in French.

genres.name: Cosmic Country
genres.description: Synthesizes various American musical influences and the exploratory ethoses of Psychedelia and Progressive Country to create an ethereal and more experimental sound still rooted in traditional Country.

genres.name: Country
genres.description: American genre derived from Southern and Appalachian forms of American Folk Music and later Rock and Pop influences, with a focus on the life and culture of rural America.

genres.name: Country & Irish
genres.description: Developed in Ireland; combines North American Country with Irish Folk Music influences, often in the form of traditional Irish songs that have been adapted into country numbers.

genres.name: Country Blues
genres.description: Various styles of Blues originating in the rural US South, typically relying on expressive vocal delivery and featuring simple, usually acoustic instrumentation.

genres.name: Country Boogie
genres.description: Uptempo style built around the Boogie Woogie rhythm, with strong beats and prominent electric guitar leads, made popular in the 1940s.

genres.name: Country Folk
genres.description: Emphasises Traditional Country instrumentation as well as influences from contemporary Singer-Songwriter traditions, such as a gentler disposition and prominent lyrical storytelling focus.

genres.name: Country Gospel
genres.description: Incorporates the harmonies and Christian themes of Gospel.

genres.name: Country Pop
genres.description: Combination of Country with Pop to appeal to a larger audience.

genres.name: Country Rap
genres.description: Combines the flow, production-emphasis, and demeanor of Hip Hop with the lyrical content and general approach of Country.

genres.name: Country Rock
genres.description: Combination of contemporary Rock with more traditional American Country.

genres.name: Country Soul
genres.description: Combining the gritty horn-driven sound of Southern Soul with the textures and aesthetics of Country.

genres.name: Country Yodeling
genres.description: Vocal technique of Yodeling, brought to the United States by German settlers, sung over the instrumentation of Traditional Country.

genres.name: Countrypolitan
genres.description: Emphasizes Pop-oriented orchestration and songwriting while reducing the role of Country instrumentation and rhythms; often featuring lush string arrangements and group backing vocals.

genres.name: Coupé-décalé
genres.description: Bass-heavy and minimal style of Ivorian popular dance music, drawing heavily from Zouglou and Congolese rhythms.

genres.name: Cowboy Poetry
genres.description: Descended from the oral traditions of cowboys and ranchers, written with traditional use of rhyme and meter, using humor and slang, and primarily concerning the cowboy profession, lifestyle, and legacy.

genres.name: Cowpunk
genres.description: Mixes together Country Rock, Rockabilly, and Contemporary Folk with the familiar punk sound.

genres.name: Crack Rock Steady
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Crust Punk and sometimes Metal, coupled with anti-establishment lyrics.

genres.name: Cretan Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Greek island Crete.

genres.name: Crime Jazz
genres.description: Gritty, moody style that emerged in the mid-1950s to accompany film noir movies and hard-boiled detective/crime-themed TV shows.

genres.name: Crimean Tatar Music
genres.description: Music of the Crimean Tatar people, a Turkic ethnic group indigenous to the Crimean Peninsula, located in southern Ukraine.

genres.name: Croatian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Croats.

genres.name: Crossbreed
genres.description: Harsh and dense mixture of Darkstep with Hardcore [EDM] developed in the late 2000s.

genres.name: Crossover Thrash
genres.description: Mixes the metallic instrumentation of Thrash Metal with the ethos and approach of Hardcore Punk.

genres.name: Cruise
genres.description: Fast-paced Nigerian dance music, utilising chopped, often humorous, samples.

genres.name: Crunk
genres.description: Originating from the southern United States and reliant on drum machines and synthesizer stabs to create an energetic, often dance-oriented sound.

genres.name: Crunkcore
genres.description: Combines rapping, screaming and autotune with synthesizers and Hip Hop beats often influenced by Crunk.

genres.name: Crust Punk
genres.description: Metallic outgrowth of Anarcho-Punk featuring a down-tuned, high-gain guitar sound, frequent D-Beat drum patterns, guttural vocals, and politically-charged lyrics often featuring apocalyptic imagery.

genres.name: Csango Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Csango, an ethnic minority group with Hungarian origins living primarily in the Romanian Moldavia region, but who are also found in the Transylvania, Dobruja, Moldova, the Ukrainian Chernivtsi region, and the Tolna region of Hungary.

genres.name: Csárdás
genres.description: Traditional Hungarian dance and music form characterized by tempo variations.

genres.name: Cuarteto
genres.description: Originated in the Argentinian province of Córdoba, usually with an upbeat rhythm and originally performed with a four-piece band.

genres.name: Cuban Charanga
genres.description: Played by traditional Cuban ensembles, influenced by Son cubano but performed on European instruments such as piano, bass, violins, and flutes.

genres.name: Cuban Music
genres.description: Encompasses the wide variety of traditions from the island of Cuba.

genres.name: Cubaton
genres.description: Rhythmically and vocally inspired by major elements of Cuban Music.

genres.name: Cuddlecore
genres.description: Rawer and more Punk informed, downplaying jangly guitars in favor of heavier yet still light-hearted tones; often features influence from the contemporary Riot Grrrl movement.

genres.name: Cueca
genres.description: Popular in Chile, Argentina, and Bolivia, accompanied by a 6/8 or 3/4 time signature and usually structured into 14 verses.

genres.name: Cumbia
genres.description: Danceable folk genre formed during the 19th century in Colombia and eastern Panama.

genres.name: Cumbia amazónica
genres.description: Mixes Cumbia peruana with selvatic dances, Afro-Latin rhythms, Surf Rock, and Psychedelic Rock between the 1960s and 1980s.

genres.name: Cumbia argentina
genres.description: Almost always features synthesizer keyboards and electronic percussion with an upbeat rhythm.

genres.name: Cumbia chilena
genres.description: Incorporates Chilean Music into the traditional sound of Cumbia.

genres.name: Cumbia colombiana
genres.description: Style that incorporates elements of Colombian traditional music, which includes and keeps influences from Spanish, African, and Indigenous cultures.

genres.name: Cumbia mexicana
genres.description: Incorporation of Rock & Roll, Mexican popular music, and Cuban influences, often adopting electric instruments, brass ensembles, accordion, and Cuban timbales, while retaining a beat-driven sound and traditional Colombian features.

genres.name: Cumbia norteña peruana
genres.description: Developed on the Peruvian coast, with influences from Cumbia colombiana and cumbia ecuatoriana and lyrics mostly about love and heartbreak.

genres.name: Cumbia peruana
genres.description: Developed in Peru and diversified into various subgenres, each with its own regional influences.

genres.name: Cumbia pop
genres.description: Developed in the Río de la Plata region in the mid-2010s, featuring Latin Pop influences and lyrics related to romance, youth, and fun.

genres.name: Cumbia salvadoreña
genres.description: Takes influence from local Salvadoran music and traditionally features a distinctive ensemble.

genres.name: Cumbia santafesina
genres.description: Originated in the Argentinian province of Santa Fe, particularly in its capital city Santa Fe de la Vera Cruz, with lyrics that tend to be romantic and relatively clean compared to later Cumbia argentina.

genres.name: Cumbia turra
genres.description: Cumbia argentina heavily influenced by Reggaetón and characterized by hard-hitting bass and heavy use of samples and Auto-Tune.

genres.name: Cumbia villera
genres.description: Developed in the villa miserias (shanty towns) by the lower classes of Argentina in the early 2000s, featuring basic rhythms and low budget productions combined with lyrics that can be openly sexual or touch on sociopolitical issues.

genres.name: Cumbiatón
genres.description: Combining Reggaetón  with Cumbia mexicana, and less frequently with other forms of traditional Mexican Music.

genres.name: Cuplé
genres.description: Originally developed in the 19th century as a blend of old theatre Spanish styles based in short monologues (jácara and tonadilla) and French Couplet.

genres.name: Currulao
genres.description: Pacific coast Afro-Colombian music and folk dance performed by a marimba/percussion ensemble with heavy use of call-and-response vocals.

genres.name: Cyber Metal
genres.description: Originated around 1999, influenced by EBM and Aggrotech with more melodic and less repetitive riffs as well as harsh vocals.

genres.name: Cybergrind
genres.description: Standard conventions of Grindcore taken to an even more discordant and rapid-fire extreme, with added Electronic dimensions of computer-generated noises and drum machines.

genres.name: Czech Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Czech people in central Europe.

genres.name: Cải lương
genres.description: Blends classical Vietnamese Opera with southern Vietnamese Folk Music and colonial French spoken melodrama.

genres.name: D-Beat
genres.description: Emerged in the early 1980s, features Metal influences, shouted vocals, and a distinct drum style known as the D-beat.

genres.name: Dabke
genres.description: Fast-paced dance and music style, most commonly performed in the Levant.

genres.name: Dagestani Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Dagestani people.

genres.name: Dagomba Music
genres.description: Music of the Dagomba people of northern Ghana.

genres.name: Dance
genres.description: Rooted in Disco and developed largely within Electronic Dance Music; emphasizes rhythm and is generally produced for play by DJs at clubs, parties, or festivals.

genres.name: Dance-Pop
genres.description: Simple, yet catchy melodies and throbbing beats inspired initially by Disco and later various House styles.

genres.name: Dance-Punk
genres.description: Mixes the energy of Punk Rock with the danceable rhythms of Funk and Disco.

genres.name: Dance-Punk Revival
genres.description: Punchy and danceable variant of Post-Punk Revival that features Electronic instrumentation and influence from Alternative Dance.

genres.name: Dancefloor Drum and Bass
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2000s as a more accessible and polished style with melodic, prominent synth leads derived from Jump-Up and punchy, often synthesized drums.

genres.name: Dancehall
genres.description: Developed from Reggae in the late 1970s, when Roots Reggae became more stripped-down, with an increased emphasis on pure rhythm.

genres.name: Dang-ak
genres.description: Korean Classical Music that dates back to the Later Silla period of 668–935.

genres.name: Dangdut
genres.description: Indonesian popular music distinguished by a rhythmic blend of Indian, Arabic, Western, Malay, Sundanese, and Javanese influences within Indonesian Music, characterized by a unique rhythmic pattern from kendang.

genres.name: Dangdut koplo
genres.description: Development of Javanese Dangdut which originated in Indonesia in the 1990s, featuring a faster tempo and influences from international styles like Pop, Rock, and Reggae.

genres.name: Danish Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Danish people.

genres.name: Danmono
genres.description: Sōkyoku composed for koto, a thirteen-string traditional instrument.

genres.name: Dansbandsmusik
genres.description: Nordic Pop style originating from 1960s Pop Rock, incorporating Swing, Schlager, Nordic Old Time Dance Music and Country influences.

genres.name: Dansktop
genres.description: Danish equivalent to Dansbandsmusik with Schlager and Country influences and Contemporary Folk and Pop elements.

genres.name: Danzón
genres.description: Development on Habanera in 2/4 time, featuring African influence through complex cross-rhythms, that would become the most popular style of dance music in Cuba during the late 19th century and early 20th century.

genres.name: Dariacore
genres.description: SoundCloud-based scene developed in the early 2020s, combining prominent vocal samples and distorted, dense production with influences from a wide range of Electronic Dance Music genres, often incorporating musical and visual references to popular media and internet culture.

genres.name: Dark Ambient
genres.description: Emphasizes an ominous, gloomy, and dissonant atmosphere.

genres.name: Dark Cabaret
genres.description: Dark, moody style incorporating elements of Cabaret in a modern context, with varied instrumentation.

genres.name: Dark Electro
genres.description: Emerged in the early 1990s in Europe, incorporating the abrasiveness of old school Industrial but with a greater focus on a horror-inspired atmosphere and harsh, distorted vocals.

genres.name: Dark Folk
genres.description: Minimalistic and melancholic sound with influence from Nordic Folk Music and even Ambient.

genres.name: Dark Jazz
genres.description: Melancholic and gloomy Film noir-inspired atmosphere and influence from Crime Jazz and Dark Ambient.

genres.name: Dark Plugg
genres.description: Ominous, sinister synth pads and lead melodies, skittering hi-hats, and fast percussion and snare rolls.

genres.name: Dark Psytrance
genres.description: Uses more complex sound design based on dark atmospheres and fast tempos.

genres.name: Darkcore
genres.description: Aggressive, dark, and often midtempo with influences from Doomcore, Industrial Hardcore, and Nu Style Gabber.

genres.name: Darkside
genres.description: Dark atmosphere and fast rhythms; served as a forerunner of Drum and Bass.

genres.name: Darkstep
genres.description: Hard, uptempo and uses heavy breakbeats, Post-Industrial-influenced sound design, and horror movie samples to create a sinister, claustrophobic atmosphere.

genres.name: Darksynth
genres.description: Incorporates atmospheric Horror Synth and faster tempos into a much heavier and darker sound.

genres.name: Darkwave
genres.description: Expands on the dark, introspective and sorrowful atmosphere of Gothic Rock; borrowing aspects from Electronic and other non-Rock influences.

genres.name: Darmstadt School
genres.description: Circle of post-World War II Western European composers of avant-garde Modern Classical, exploring Serialism and other innovations.

genres.name: Data Sonification
genres.description: Usage of data to create sound, soundscapes and music mostly as a way to illustrate its information.

genres.name: Death 'n' Roll
genres.description: Incorporates a groove-oriented, Hard Rock-influenced approach while retaining heavily distorted rhythm guitars and gruff or occasionally growled vocals.

genres.name: Death Doom Metal
genres.description: Fuses down-tuned guitars, growled vocals, and aggressive, often double-kick drumming with a mournful, somber atmosphere and plodding tempos.

genres.name: Death Industrial
genres.description: Combines the abrasive textures of Noise and Industrial music with dark, brooding drones and atmospheres.

genres.name: Death Metal
genres.description: Heavily distorted, down-tuned guitars, palm-muted, tremolo-picked riffs, double-kick and blast beat percussion, chromatic chord progressions, minor keys, abrupt changes in tempo, and guttural vocals.

genres.name: Deathchant Hardcore
genres.description: Took shape in the UK in the late 1990s and early 2000s, characterized by rapid rhythms with Gabber-influenced kicks, frequent use of breakbeats and Hip Hop-inspired sampling.

genres.name: Deathcore
genres.description: Integrates brutal palm-muted and tremolo-picked riffing, blast beat-focused drumming, and guttural vocals of Death Metal with groovy breakdown sections.

genres.name: Deathgrind
genres.description: Combines the intensity and high-pitched screams of Grindcore with the technicality and low guttural vocals of Death Metal.

genres.name: Deathrock
genres.description: More Punk-oriented offshoot of Gothic Rock that emphasizes energy and an effect-laden sound over pure atmosphere.

genres.name: Deathstep
genres.description: Darker, heavier form of Brostep that uses "machine gun" basses, atonal synths, and elements from genres like Death Metal and Metalcore.

genres.name: Dechovka
genres.description: Brass band genre popular in Czechia and Slovakia, characterized by lively brass instrumentation, infectious rhythms, and vibrant melodies.

genres.name: Deconstructed Club
genres.description: Emerged in the 2010s as the hybridization of diverse Electronic Dance Music genres with an abrasive Post-Industrial sound.

genres.name: Deejay
genres.description: Reggae in which a deejay (similar to an MC in Hip Hop) talks or chants lyrics over a pre-recorded reggae rhythm.

genres.name: Deep Drum and Bass
genres.description: Sub-bass-rich, repetitive, minimalist, and rhythm-focused production.

genres.name: Deep Funk
genres.description: Focuses more on grooves and rhythm than songwriting.

genres.name: Deep House
genres.description: Emerged in the United States during the mid-1980s, featuring a relaxed tempo and influences from Jazz, Funk, and Soul.

genres.name: Deep Soul
genres.description: Draws on the typical Southern Soul groove and accentuates the Gospel and Blues influence, particularly Chicago Blues.

genres.name: Deep Tech
genres.description: Incorporates UK Garage rhythms and synths stabs, influences from British rave music, UK Bass and UK Deep House, resulting in an urban, subdued, but danceable sound with deep, muted basslines.

genres.name: Dek Bass
genres.description: Prominent heavy, sustained bass tones, percussion derived from South Asian Music, and often high-pitched sound effects or samples; commonly played at extreme volumes in DJ/sound system competitions.

genres.name: Delta Blues
genres.description: One of the earliest forms of Blues, named for the Mississippi Delta region of the United States where it developed, with a highly rhythmic style and a typical 12-bar structure.

genres.name: Dembow
genres.description: Originated in the Dominican Republic during the early 1990s, featuring rapping indebted to Hip Hop and a style drawing on Dancehall, particularly the "Dem Bow" riddim.

genres.name: Demoscene
genres.description: Computer art subculture originating in the 1980s based on the creation of demos and overcoming technical limitations.

genres.name: Demostyle
genres.description: Traditional eclectic style of the Demoscene with a special emphasis on tracker techniques and samples, and combining numerous elements of completely different genres - from Italo-Disco, Progressive Electronic and Funk to Belgian Techno, Ambient and Drum and Bass.

genres.name: Dennery Segment
genres.description: Developed in Saint Lucia in the early 2010s; heavily influenced by Angolan Kuduro, as well as incorporating elements of Zouk and Lucian drums alongside suggestive lyrics usually sung in Kwéyòl (Saint Lucian Creole).

genres.name: Denpa
genres.description: Underground style aiming to be bizarre yet catchy, using off-key and high-pitched vocals, strange or nonsensical lyrics, repetitive chants, onomatopoeia, frantic and "off-kilter" production, and "moe" aesthetics.

genres.name: Descarga
genres.description: Cuban genre consisting of improvised jam sessions incorporating elements of Jazz and Afro-Cuban music.

genres.name: Desgarrada
genres.description: Improvisational tradition from Northern Portugal where two vocalists address and respond to each other, usually in a joking manner.

genres.name: Desi Hip Hop
genres.description: Hip hop music created on the Indian subcontinent and the South Asian diaspora, especially India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.

genres.name: Detroit Sound
genres.description: Upbeat 808 percussion; simple, funky mallet instruments, keys, strings, and synth bass; and street-centric, often punched-in rapping.

genres.name: Detroit Techno
genres.description: Features a signature mechanical, detached sound that echoed the atmosphere of Detroit's nightlife and incorporated influences from Electro, Chicago House, as well as Synthpop and Electro-Disco.

genres.name: Deutschpunk
genres.description: Partly a reaction to the commercialization of the German movement Neue Deutsche Welle; characterized by extreme speed, consciously basic songwriting, crude musicianship, and radical leftism.

genres.name: Deutschrock
genres.description: Lyrics address German life, culture, and identity wrapped in upbeat songs, anthemic ballads, and a strong focus on the personality of the lead singer.

genres.name: Dhaanto
genres.description: Song and dance that originally featured no instruments, but later transformed into a style featuring prominent rhythms and slow grooves.

genres.name: Dhol tasha
genres.description: Energetic, dense rhythms played on the dhol and tasha drums, which the genre is named after.

genres.name: Dhrupad
genres.description: Ancient style of classical Hindustani vocal and instrumental music.

genres.name: Digicore
genres.description: Developed in the late 2010s and characterized by frantic, bombastic, and glamourous production, usually derived from Trap, that serves to accompany highly melodious, auto-tuned, and hi-pitched vocal performances, often done with breathy voice singing and sing-rapping.

genres.name: Digital Cumbia
genres.description: Mixes an Electronic sound into traditional Cumbia through influences from House, Dancehall, Hyphy, and Dubstep.

genres.name: Digital Dancehall
genres.description: First, pre-Ragga style of Dancehall to popularize Electronic rhythms that arose in the mid-1980s.

genres.name: Digital Fusion
genres.description: Incorporates the hardware-limited sounds of Chiptune and other Bit Music into compositions drawing on Jazz, Cinematic Classical, progressive music, and other Electronic styles, sometimes augmented with live instrumentation.

genres.name: Digital Hardcore
genres.description: High-tempo fusion of Hardcore Punk and Electronic, combining harsh vocals and electric guitars of the former with electronic instruments.

genres.name: Dikir barat
genres.description: Vocal Malay Music that revolves around group singing, often for the purpose of competitions.

genres.name: Dimotika
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Greek mainland, often using clarinet, guitar, tambourine, and violin as accompaniment, while also incorporating various forms of Greek dance and vocal music.

genres.name: Dinka Music
genres.description: Music of the Dinka people, the most populous ethnic group of South Sudan.

genres.name: Dirty South
genres.description: Originated in the Southern US during the mid-1990s, defined by a bouncy rhythm, fast-tempo snares, 808s, heavy bass, and often rapped in a rhythmic delivery consisting of explicit lyrics.

genres.name: Disco
genres.description: Combines the lush orchestration of Philly Soul and bass grooves of Funk with a four-on-the-floor rhythm.

genres.name: Disco polo
genres.description: Polish Dance-Pop, originally established from contemporary wedding / feast songs and Italo-Disco.

genres.name: Disco Rap
genres.description: Most prevalent from 1979 to 1982, featuring MCs rapping over popular Disco breaks.

genres.name: Dissonant Black Metal
genres.description: Dissonant atonal riffing, cleaner production style, and complex song structures.

genres.name: Dissonant Death Metal
genres.description: Emphasizes discordant, dense songwriting and utilizes pinch harmonics, scratchy guitar leads, and atonality.

genres.name: Diva House
genres.description: Dominant, anthemic female vocals, common use of piano stabs, and energetic, driving four-on-the-floor rhythms.

genres.name: Divertissement
genres.description: Straightforward tuneful music historically written to serve as light entertainment for events or as interstitial movements within larger theatrical works.

genres.name: Dixieland
genres.description: Developed in New Orleans in the 1910s, incorporating influences from Ragtime and Blues into cacophonous, polyphonic arrangements with instruments trading places between accompaniment and soloist.

genres.name: Djanba
genres.description: Sung and composed in the Murrinh-Patha language and consisting of a mixed group of men and women accompanied by bilma and handclaps, typically without didgeridoo.

genres.name: Djent
genres.description: Groovy polymeters, syncopated power chord chugs, palm-muted, distorted guitars, and significant focus on production and tone.

genres.name: Doble paso
genres.description: Frenetic and intense high tempo variant in comparison to the standard drum patterns, often used to accompany the dance of the same name.

genres.name: Dobrado
genres.description: Brazilian musical genre, played by military bands with wooden, brass and also percussive instruments.

genres.name: Doină
genres.description: Melancholic, lyrical folk song characterised by its free rhythm.

genres.name: Dolewave
genres.description: Loose, low-key, and sardonic with erudite lyrics and considerable influence from the Dunedin Sound and Slacker Rock; came to prominence in Melbourne in the early 2010s.

genres.name: Dondang sayang
genres.description: Typically performed by two vocalists of opposite gender, featuring a musical dialogue of Malay vocal poetry on topics of love and romance.

genres.name: Dongjing
genres.description: Rooted in Chinese Taoist Ritual Music from the Nakhi (Naxi) people, historically performed around Yunnan and Sichuan.

genres.name: Donosti Sound
genres.description: Sentimental and melancholic scene, influenced by Twee Pop, that emerged in the late 1980s in Donostia / San Sebastián, Spain.

genres.name: Doo-Wop
genres.description: Heavy emphasis on male four-part harmonies and light instrumentation; peaked in popularity in the 1950s.

genres.name: Doom Metal
genres.description: Plodding tempos, repeated chords, and thick, distorted, down-tuned guitars in a style focused on foreboding, atmosphere, and tension.

genres.name: Doomcore
genres.description: Often somber and contemplative in mood, a feature achieved by the common use of long-stretched ambient pads, and sometimes even samples of screaming and other "spooky" sounds.

genres.name: Doomgaze
genres.description: Gloomy and sombre atmosphere, amplified by the slow tempo and melancholy of Doom Metal, combined with the effects, washes of sound, and vocals found within Shoegaze.

genres.name: Doujin Music
genres.description: Independently-released music derived from the wider doujin movement in Japan, largely released at events such as Comiket and M3, and primarily focused on otaku interests.

genres.name: Downtempo
genres.description: Atmospheric and groove-based with relaxed tempos and mellow beats.

genres.name: Downtempo Deathcore
genres.description: Slow and minimal songs emphasizing breakdowns, atmosphere, and dissonance with downtuned guitars.

genres.name: Dream Pop
genres.description: Reverberated guitars, effects-laden vocals, and dense productions, creating a psychedelic, spacious, and dreamlike sound.

genres.name: Dream Trance
genres.description: Slow tempo (about 130 BPM) with strong roots in Progressive House, using beats typical of Eurodance and Dance-Pop; emphasizes a laid-back, carefree, and dreamlike sound.

genres.name: Dreampunk
genres.description: Accentuates ambiance and a dreamy, futuristic atmosphere, taking influence from Progressive Electronic, as well as Cyberpunk and Dystopian movies.

genres.name: Drift Phonk
genres.description: Busy, noisy production inspired by lo-fi Memphis Rap; frequently features 808 cowbell melodies and chopped, compressed samples.

genres.name: Drill
genres.description: Originated in Chicago in the early 2010s; broadly characterized by complex, energetic rhythms coupled with gang-oriented, street-conscious, and violent lyrics.

genres.name: Drill and Bass
genres.description: Frenzied, intricate beat programming inspired by Drum and Bass.

genres.name: Drone
genres.description: Focuses on long, sustained tones and tone clusters, or repetition of single notes.

genres.name: Drone Metal
genres.description: Extremely slow tempos, highly sustained, repetitive guitar notes, and minimalist song structures often omitting a traditional rhythm section and vocals.

genres.name: Drum and Bass
genres.description: Fast, syncopated breakbeat patterns (often sampled or programmed) with prominent basslines, commonly within the 160-180 BPM range.

genres.name: Drum and Bugle Corps
genres.description: Primarily uses drums and bugles, developed from North American military music.

genres.name: Drumfunk
genres.description: Focuses on complex drum beats made to emulate live recordings.

genres.name: Drumless
genres.description: Stripped-down production style pioneered in the early 2010s and identified by a lack of drums or minimal, subtle percussion left untouched from the original sample or filtered out.

genres.name: Drumline
genres.description: Solely percussion based Marching Band.

genres.name: Drumstep
genres.description: Dancefloor-friendly, loud, and heavy combination of the drum programming and tempo of Jump-Up with the half-time rhythm and midrange LFO wobble of Brostep.

genres.name: Druze Music
genres.description: Musical traditions of the Druze people.

genres.name: DSBM
genres.description: Lethargic, melancholic, and repetitive sound; depressive and misanthropic themes; vocals ranging from high-pitched wails and screams to strained cleans; often featuring non-distorted sections.

genres.name: Dub
genres.description: Primarily instrumental Reggae which developed from the extensive use of studio techniques and effects like reverb and delay.

genres.name: Dub Poetry
genres.description: Poetry with Dub and Reggae backing rhythms, originating in Jamaica in the 1970s.

genres.name: Dub Techno
genres.description: Fuses elements of Minimal Techno with characteristics of Dub.

genres.name: Dubstep
genres.description: Half-time syncopated and sparse beats set around 140 BPM with heavy sub-basses; emerged in South London in the early 2000s.

genres.name: Dubstyle
genres.description: Characterized by the incorporation of the half-time rhythms and wobbly basslines of Dubstep.

genres.name: Dubwise Drum and Bass
genres.description: Implementing Reggae and Dub influences, usually vocal dubs, delay effects, and reggae instrumentation, with the clean production and rhythms of post-2000s styles.

genres.name: Dunedin Sound
genres.description: Emerged in Dunedin, New Zealand in the early 1980s, featuring a murky, lo-fi sound that overlaps with contemporaneous Jangle Pop and Slacker Rock styles.

genres.name: Dungeon Rap
genres.description: Combines the dark production of Memphis Rap with the fantasy aesthetics and sound design of Dungeon Synth.

genres.name: Dungeon Sound
genres.description: Commonly features dark textures, spatial production, and midrange basses.

genres.name: Dungeon Synth
genres.description: Focuses on evoking epic and atmospheric soundscapes primarily associated with fantasy and medieval settings through the usage of synthesizers, keyboards, lo-fi production, and drum machines.

genres.name: Dutch Cabaret
genres.description: Popular comedy form in the Netherlands which evolved out of traditional Cabaret in the 1890s.

genres.name: Dutch Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music from the Netherlands.

genres.name: Dutch House
genres.description: High-pitched wonky synth melodies and heavy influence from Fidget House which developed in the Netherlands around 2007-08.

genres.name: Düsseldorf School
genres.description: Krautrock scene which developed alongside Berlin School music in the early 1970s; known for its characteristic ‘motorik beat,’ as well as for playing a major role in the evolution of Electronic music.

genres.name: EAI
genres.description: Slow paced, physical, textured aesthetic - often created using unconventional instruments processed through a computer.

genres.name: Early Hardstyle
genres.description: Forerunner subgenre that emerged around the turn of the 2000s from Hard Trance and Gabber, distinguished by the signature reverse bass groove, slower tempo around 140 BPM and straightforward, repetitive sound.

genres.name: East African Music
genres.description: Traditions which originate from the eastern subregion of the African continent, encompassing a wide variety of cultures and styles.

genres.name: East Asian Classical Music
genres.description: Covers all the forms of pan-East Asian Classical Music sharing origins in Chinese Classical Music.

genres.name: East Asian Folk Music
genres.description: All the forms of Traditional Folk Music from East Asia, including Japanese Folk Music, Chinese Folk Music, and Korean Folk Music.

genres.name: East Asian Music
genres.description: Covers the different forms of music with origins in Japan, Korea, China, Taiwan, and Vietnam.

genres.name: East Coast Club
genres.description: Group of club styles from the US East Coast that combines Miami Bass rhythms with influence from Breakbeat and Ghetto House.

genres.name: East Coast Hip Hop
genres.description: Highly influential Hip Hop scene that developed in New York City, particularly in the South Bronx, during the 1970s.

genres.name: Eastern-Style Polka
genres.description: Fast, urban Polish-American style performed by a Big Band-like ensemble.

genres.name: Easy Listening
genres.description: Typically instrumental, including lush arrangements and melodies played by orchestras or big bands aiming for light entertainment.

genres.name: Easycore
genres.description: Combines the radio-friendly stylings of second-wave Pop Punk with Metalcore-inspired breakdowns, lower guitar tunings, and occasional unclean vocals.

genres.name: EBM
genres.description: Melodic and dancefloor-friendly take on Post-Industrial music that developed in the early 1980s.

genres.name: Eccojams
genres.description: Simple, prototypical Vaporwave style, heavily influenced by Chopped and Screwed and Glitch, that features short, slowed-down, lyric focused, sampled loops smothered in reverb and continuously repeated, usually taken from late 20th century music.

genres.name: ECM Style Jazz
genres.description: Primarily associated with ECM Records, combining elements of Jazz Fusion with the subdued atmosphere of Cool Jazz and the Western Classical Music bent of Third Stream.

genres.name: Egg Punk
genres.description: Originated in the early 2010s; features lo-fi production, eccentric lyrics, quick tempos, nasally vocals, and cheap keyboard sounds.

genres.name: Egyptian Music
genres.description: Music of the people of Egypt.

genres.name: Electric Blues
genres.description: Major development in sound and reach of Blues when it became possible to amplify the instruments of small combos.

genres.name: Electric Texas Blues
genres.description: Originating in (but not limited to) Texas; includes Jazz influences like Swing rhythms and sometimes the addition of a horn section.

genres.name: Electro
genres.description: Syncopated rhythms programmed on the Roland TR-808 drum machine, often resembling Funk breaks, along with simple funky basslines.

genres.name: Electro Hop
genres.description: Emerged in the mid 2000s featuring upbeat rap verses and catchy hooks over four-on-the-floor Electropop and  Electro House-inspired production.

genres.name: Electro House
genres.description: Warm analog basslines, punchy percussion, crisp high-pitched synthesizer leads, and clipped vocal samples.

genres.name: Electro latino
genres.description: Mixes elements of Merengue and Reggaetón with polished production from mainstream House subgenres; often shares traits with Latin Pop, having anthemic melodies and verse-chorus structures.

genres.name: Electro Swing
genres.description: Upbeat, energetic style that splices Swing with Electronic Dance Music, looking to recapture the atmosphere of late 1920s to mid-1940s Jazz within a more updated club-friendly medium.

genres.name: Electro-Disco
genres.description: Disco instrumentation is largely - if not entirely - replaced by synthesizers and augmented with futuristic elements such as the vocoder.

genres.name: Electro-Industrial
genres.description: Formed in the late 1980s and early 1990s; grew out of a combination of EBM and Industrial.

genres.name: Electroacoustic
genres.description: Manipulation and processing of sound sources to create atmospheric pieces.

genres.name: Electroclash
genres.description: Draws from 1980s styles such as Electro, New Wave, and Electro-Disco combined with Techno, resulting in minimal, throbbing beats and basslines, buzzing synthesizer parts, vocoders and often monotone, half-spoken, half-sung vocals.

genres.name: Electronic
genres.description: Uses non-traditional electronic instrumentation and sound manipulation technology as the primary backbone of a composition.

genres.name: Electronic Dance Music
genres.description: Broad category for subgenres mainly derived from Disco, featuring Electronic sounds, synthesizers, drum machines and varying BPM ranges.

genres.name: Electronicore
genres.description: Hybrid of Metalcore and/or Post-Hardcore with various Electronic Dance Music styles, utilizing Electronic instrumentation and occasional Dance beats.

genres.name: Electropop
genres.description: Dense, layered, and compressed production, usually coupled with a distinct fuzzy and "warm" low-frequency synthesizer style.

genres.name: Electrotango
genres.description: Combines Tango rhythms and melodies with Electronic music.

genres.name: Eleki
genres.description: Japanese Surf Rock that emerged during the early to mid-1960s, incorporating elements of Japanese Folk Music.

genres.name: Eletrofunk
genres.description: Blends Funk brasileiro vocals with production from popular late 2000s and early 2010s House.

genres.name: Elizabethan Song
genres.description: Monophonic style developed in Renaissance England that is typically composed in strophic form for one to several vocalists with instrumental accompaniment ranging from solo lute to chamber ensemble.

genres.name: Emo
genres.description: Focuses on emotional lyrics, expressive vocals, melodic songwriting, and dynamic song structures.

genres.name: Emo Rap
genres.description: Moody, melancholic production combining atmospheric Cloud Rap, and Trap's typical drum programming, with sampling from Alternative Rock, Midwest Emo, Emo-Pop, and Pop Punk.

genres.name: Emo Revival
genres.description: Movement beginning in the late 2000s inspired by the styles of 1990s Midwest Emo, often associated with Math Rock-inflected "twinkly" style.

genres.name: Emo-Pop
genres.description: Mainstream derivative of Emo, puts more emphasis on the poppy sensibilities of Alternative Rock and Pop Punk.

genres.name: Emocore
genres.description: Emerged primarily in Washington D.C. in 1985 as a reaction to the stagnant Hardcore Punk scene, with a less aggressive style that was more melodic and often featured emotional, introspective lyrics.

genres.name: Emoviolence
genres.description: Shorter length and volatile song structures, while borrowing techniques from Powerviolence such as blast beats, unconventional screaming and noisier sounds.

genres.name: English Folk Music
genres.description: Musical traditions of the English people, primarily divided into dance music and folksongs.

genres.name: English Pastoral School
genres.description: Early 20th-century English classical composers turning to English folk and pastoral influences.

genres.name: English Underground
genres.description: Countercultural scene in the United Kingdom, centred around London clubs like UFO and Middle Earth, which peaked in 1966 and 1967.

genres.name: Enka
genres.description: Evolved from Ryūkōka in the mid-1950s, based around the pentatonic scale and with a lyrical focus on expressive and emotional topics such as love, loss, loneliness, and death.

genres.name: Entechna
genres.description: First appeared in Greece in the late 1950s, featuring orchestrated arrangements with influence from Greek Folk Music and the popular Laika style.

genres.name: Entechna laika
genres.description: Artistic side of Laika played mainly but not always with the basic instruments of it, the bouzouki, Greek baglama, and the jouras, sometimes with the accompaniment of orchestras.

genres.name: Epadunk
genres.description: Swedish party-oriented scene emerging in the early 2020s, featuring Electronic Dance Music-leaning sound and vulgar lyrics.

genres.name: Epic Collage
genres.description: Cinematic, dense digital collage; frequently utilizes a Deconstructed Club sonic palette and decontextualized novel samples.

genres.name: Epic Doom Metal
genres.description: Emphasizes Heavy Metal influence and theatrical vocals.

genres.name: Epic Music
genres.description: Often associated with Electronic production, heavy percussion such as taiko drums, Choral vocals, and orchestral instrumentation to create a bombastic style commonly linked to movie trailers.

genres.name: Estonian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Estonian people.

genres.name: Ethereal Wave
genres.description: Atmospheric guitar and synthesizer soundscapes, effects like reverb and delay, and commonly soprano female vocals to create a surreal, otherworldly effect.

genres.name: Ethio-Jazz
genres.description: Unique blend of traditional Ethiopic Music and Jazz.

genres.name: Ethiopian Church Music
genres.description: Sacred tradition of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, sung in an ancient Semitic language called Ge'ez and credited with assembling the current Ethiopian notation system.

genres.name: Ethiopic Music
genres.description: Music made by people who speak Ethiopian Semitic languages.

genres.name: Euphoric Hardstyle
genres.description: Melodic, more lighthearted, and accessible Hardstyle.

genres.name: Euro House
genres.description: Vocal-focused style emerging in the late 1980s in Europe, developing in parallel with Eurodance.

genres.name: Euro Trance
genres.description: Emerged as a fusion with Eurodance, features fast tempos, more accessible grooves and structures, and simple, catchy melodies with vocals and saw synth leads.

genres.name: Euro-Disco
genres.description: European style that moved away from the genre's Rhythm & Blues and Soul roots, speeding up the tempo and adding Electronic instruments like synthesizers and drum machines as a backing for more melodic Europop-influenced vocals.

genres.name: Eurobeat
genres.description: Fast-paced with roots in Hi-NRG and Italo-Disco; became mainly popular in Japan in the 1990s.

genres.name: Eurodance
genres.description: Takes elements of Euro-Disco, House, Techno, and Hi-NRG while featuring on-beat kick, hi-hat and snare sounds at around 110 to 150 bpm.

genres.name: European Folk Music
genres.description: Encompasses numerous folk traditions found in Europe.

genres.name: European Free Jazz
genres.description: Arose in Europe in the late 1960s and early 1970s, moving even further from the Jazz tradition by often dropping the swinging rhythm, taking liberties with the use of atonality and noise.

genres.name: European Music
genres.description: Regional styles with roots in the European continent and surrounding islands.

genres.name: Europop
genres.description: Emerged throughout mainland Europe in the early 1970s, referring to slick, highly commercial Pop songs that emphasize sugary melodies and light, bouncy instrumentation.

genres.name: Euskal kantagintza berria
genres.description: Basque genre born during the 1960s inspired by Nova cançó and Chanson.

genres.name: Ewe Music
genres.description: Music of the Ewe people, found in southern Togo, southeastern Ghana and southwestern Benin.

genres.name: Exotica
genres.description: Emerged in the early 1950s as the United States developed a fascination with Polynesia and the South Pacific, incorporates traditional instruments and rhythms from these cultures into a Western Pop context.

genres.name: Experimental
genres.description: Most radical approaches throughout history, featuring non-traditional production methods resulting in sounds and styles that go largely beyond traditional boundaries.

genres.name: Experimental Big Band
genres.description: Dispensing with traditional Jazz structures and Swing sounds, instead performing Avant-Garde Jazz and pushing the boundaries of the medium.

genres.name: Experimental Hip Hop
genres.description: Incorporates experimental and eccentric elements considered unconventional or unorthodox compared to more traditional hip hop.

genres.name: Experimental Rock
genres.description: Eschews accessibility and convention, experimenting with song structures, time signatures, rhythm, dissonance, instrumentation, noise, electronics, studio manipulation, and other techniques not traditionally associated with Rock.

genres.name: Expressionism
genres.description: Originating between the abandonment of tonality at the conclusion of the period of Romanticism and the creation of twelve-tone composition.

genres.name: Extratone
genres.description: At and above the threshold of 1000 BPM where sequences of kick drums begin to form a continuous pitch.

genres.name: Fado
genres.description: Tradition from Portugal originating in the first half of the 19th century, mainly consisting of melancholic songs accompanied by Portuguese guitars or classical guitars.

genres.name: Fairy Tales
genres.description: Recorded for children with or without background music.

genres.name: Falak
genres.description: Songs that reflect the state of living for those indigenous to the Pamir mountains ranges, often sung in high registers.

genres.name: Famo
genres.description: Popular and danceable style from Lesotho and the surrounding Sotho-speaking region of South Africa, often featuring the accordion as the lead instrument.

genres.name: Fandango caiçara
genres.description: Style of fandango born in coastal Southern Brazil amidst the Caiçara people.

genres.name: Fanfare
genres.description: Brass-led tradition originating in Western Europe, commonly performed during important public events, typically featuring a ceremonious, triumphant, or uplifting sound.

genres.name: Fantasia
genres.description: Free-form, improvisational, and with contrasting sectional writing, sometimes based on preexisting melodies and generally meant to evoke a sense of imaginative exploration.

genres.name: Fantezi
genres.description: Incorporates influences from Turkish Classical Music and Turkish Folk Music within a more accessible, commercial, and unorthodox context.

genres.name: Faroese Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Faroe Islands.

genres.name: Festejo
genres.description: Happy and danceable Afro-Peruvian rhythm originating in the 17th century.

genres.name: Festival Progressive House
genres.description: Uplifting, melodic, energetic but clean drops, featuring modern supersaws and pianos, taking influences from Progressive House, Uplifting Trance, but applying them to a form structurally closer to Big Room House and Electro House.

genres.name: Festival Trap
genres.description: Massive, sub-bass-heavy drops with simple melodies, synth leads and production influenced by Big Room House; highly popular from 2013 to 2015.

genres.name: Fidget House
genres.description: Makes heavy use of Breakbeat Hardcore-esque synth stabs, pitch bending of basslines, and cut-up vocal samples, as well as glitchy, or "choppy", 4/4 rhythms.

genres.name: Field Hollers
genres.description: Created by African-American slaves working on cotton plantations, featuring expressive vocals to no strict rhythm.

genres.name: Field Recordings
genres.description: Material recorded outside of a recording studio for the purpose of capturing the audible illustration of an environment.

genres.name: Fife and Drum Blues
genres.description: Rooted in martial Fife and Drum Corps music, originated among Afro-American communities in Mississippi.

genres.name: Fife and Drum Corps
genres.description: Derived from military field music, primarily uses fifes and drums.

genres.name: Fijian Music
genres.description: Music of the Fijian people.

genres.name: Fijiri
genres.description: Deeply rooted in the Persian Gulf pearl diving culture, and sung during weekly gatherings combining solo and choral sections with minimal percussion.

genres.name: Filin
genres.description: Emotional style that appeared in La Habana during the late 1940s, deeply influenced by the melodic and expressive style of Vocal Jazz.

genres.name: Filk
genres.description: Broad fandom-focused movement that emerged from Science Fiction conventions in the 1950s, based around original lyrics about fannish interests set to popular melodies or original compositions in an eclectic range of genres.

genres.name: Filmi
genres.description: Music of films in the Indian subcontinent, representing the shared styles of the linguistically segregated industries in India, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Nepal.

genres.name: Finnish Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Finnish people.

genres.name: Finnish Tango
genres.description: Melancholic style developed in Finland in the 1930s and 1940s, influenced by traditional minor-key Finnish Folk Music melodies and the rhythms of German marches.

genres.name: First Wave of Detroit Techno
genres.description: Influential 1980s scene that invented Detroit Techno and was active in Electro, House, and Synthpop.

genres.name: Flamenco
genres.description: Traditional Spanish style based around fiery acoustic guitar rhythms, emotional vocals, and accompaniment from traditional percussion and dance.

genres.name: Flamenco Jazz
genres.description: Combination of Jazz with Flamenco nuevo, the contemporary style of Flamenco, which was pioneered in the late 1960s.

genres.name: Flamenco nuevo
genres.description: Contemporary style of Flamenco which departs from tradition by incorporating influences from other genres like Jazz, Blues, and Rock.

genres.name: Flamenco Pop
genres.description: Incorporates Flamenco sub-styles into a more commercial Pop form; particularly through the vocal style and rhythms.

genres.name: Flashcore
genres.description: Fast-paced short sounds, complex structures with erratic progression, and often dense and atmospheric abstract sound design, featuring recontextualized elements from IDM, Speedcore, Industrial Hardcore, and Breakcore.

genres.name: Flemish Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Flanders region in northern Belgium, typically sung in the local Flemish dialect.

genres.name: Flex Dance Music
genres.description: Largely instrumental; infused with Electronic Dance Music elements.

genres.name: Flint Sound
genres.description: Uptempo and repetitive, featuring simple melodies, pitched-up snares, and humorous, punchline-heavy lyrics.

genres.name: Florida Breaks
genres.description: Developed during the mid-1990s, combining major influences of Hip Hop derivatives such as Miami Bass and Electro along with elements of 1990s Electronic Dance Music genres like House or Techno.

genres.name: Florida Fast Music
genres.description: DJing and production technique originally developed in South Florida, that primarily involves speeding up Hip Hop, Contemporary R&B, and East Coast Club records.

genres.name: FM Synthesis
genres.description: Sound synthesis that combines the simple waveforms of Chiptune with modulating oscillators to create a bouncier synthesizer sound that would be used in arcade cabinets and home video game consoles like the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis in the late 1980s.

genres.name: Folk
genres.description: Rooted in mostly oral traditions of the peoples of the world, encompassing international Traditional Folk Music as well as Western Contemporary Folk which arose in the 1940s.

genres.name: Folk Baroque
genres.description: Originated in England in the early 1960s, featuring a distinctive guitar fingerpicking style of the same name and the DADGAD guitar tuning.

genres.name: Folk Metal
genres.description: Features influences from various types of Traditional Folk Music expressed through melodies and/or traditional instrumentation, notably having a large scene in Europe.

genres.name: Folk Pop
genres.description: Blends Contemporary Folk with a Pop sensibility, most popular in the late 1960s and early 1970s and featuring influence from the contemporary Folk Rock style.

genres.name: Folk Punk
genres.description: Influenced by various forms of Folk, including Traditional Folk Music as well as Contemporary Folk and Folk Rock.

genres.name: Folk Rock
genres.description: Influenced by Folk, particularly in the use of acoustic instrumentation and relatively simple arrangements; has its origins in the American Contemporary Folk movement of the 1960s.

genres.name: Folkhop
genres.description: Influenced by Hip Hop, including looped beats with Bhangra instrumentation and rapped vocals.

genres.name: Folklor miejski
genres.description: Urban folk street band traditions of Polish cities.

genres.name: Folktales
genres.description: Traditional stories passed down throughout many generations.

genres.name: Folktronica
genres.description: Combines sound design techniques from IDM and Glitch with acoustic instrumentation inspired by Contemporary Folk.

genres.name: Fon leb
genres.description: Traditional performance music originating in northern Thailand consist of an ensemble with Piphat instruments and a pair of female choreographers.

genres.name: Fon Music
genres.description: The traditions of the Fon people, originating in central and southeastern Benin as well as the southwestern region of Nigeria.

genres.name: Football Chant
genres.description: Sung by large crowds at association football (soccer) games to celebrate or insult teams.

genres.name: Footwork
genres.description: Extensive use of drum fills, tom drums, handclaps, and snares within fast-paced, highly syncopated beats not bound to a 4/4 kick rhythm.

genres.name: Footwork Jungle
genres.description: Combining Footwork's archetypal percussion, skittering drum fills, handclaps, and syncopated rhythms, with Drum and Bass drum programming and breakbeats, merging the two into unconventional, frantic drumming and dense, off-kilter rhythms.

genres.name: Forest Psytrance
genres.description: Mimicks the ambience of a forest by using swarming and teeming effects as well as natural samples; features straightforward song structures.

genres.name: Forró
genres.description: Developed from Baião and the dance rhythms quadrilha and xaxado, along with influences of European Folk Music like chula and schottische (Xote).

genres.name: Fort Thunder Scene
genres.description: Late '90s – early 2000s Noise and Noise Rock scene that formed around an art commune in Providence, Rhode Island.

genres.name: Foxtrot
genres.description: Lightly syncopated ballroom dance form in 4/4, most popular in the 1930s and closely associated with early Big Band Jazz.

genres.name: Franco-Flemish School
genres.description: Musical movement centered in the Low Countries, known for its intricate polyphony, emotional expression, and influence on European sacred and secular music from the 1440s to 1550.

genres.name: Frapcore
genres.description: Emerged in France in the mid-2010s, uses French rapping with 4-on-the-floor Hardcore [EDM] and especially Gabber instrumentals.

genres.name: Frat Rap
genres.description: Light-hearted and laid-back with lyrical focuses on subjects such as partying and college life.

genres.name: Frat Rock
genres.description: Early form of Garage Rock with hard Rhythm & Blues grooves, catchy melodies, and a "fratty" focus on partying and girls.

genres.name: Freak Folk
genres.description: Loosely defined 2000s Psychedelic Folk revival closely associated with the New Weird America movement, sometimes also a shorthand for certain leftfield styles of psychedelic and Indie Folk.

genres.name: Freakbeat
genres.description: Outgrowth of the Mod movement which combines elements of British Rhythm & Blues and Beat with studio effects common in Psychedelia such as fuzztones, flanging and chorus; often seen as a British relative of the American Garage Psych scene.

genres.name: Free Car Music
genres.description: Chaotic and metallic percussion with clanging rides, rapid hi hat rolls, and tense kick buildups typically coupled with staggered, punched-in rapping.

genres.name: Free Folk
genres.description: Incorporates improvisation, repetition and extended song lengths.

genres.name: Free Improvisation
genres.description: Improvised music which, in descending from Free Jazz and classical Indeterminacy, further abandons the prescriptions of harmonic or rhythmic structures which characterized those genres.

genres.name: Free Jazz
genres.description: Attempts to break free from the conventions and patterns of earlier Jazz subgenres through the use of elements such as dissonance, atonality, and free-flowing rhythmic structures.

genres.name: Free Noise
genres.description: 1990s New Zealand scene consisting of Rock-based groups with a focus on Free Improvisation, Drone, and Noise music.

genres.name: Freeform Hardcore
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1990s, combining fast and hard-hitting rhythms with heavy influence from the synthesizers of Trance.

genres.name: Freestyle
genres.description: Electro-influenced; developed in Latino communities in New York and Miami in the 1980s, especially dominated by Latin Freestyle and its Latin influences.

genres.name: Freetekno
genres.description: Originated in the early 1990s, commonly played at free parties in Europe, and features a repetitive pounding kick drum at tempos of 170 BPM or above.

genres.name: French Caribbean Music
genres.description: Music from the French Antilles (Martinique, Guadeloupe, Dominica, Saint Lucia) and from Haiti.

genres.name: French Electro
genres.description: Mixes Electro House with major elements of genres such as Electroclash, Nu-Disco, Synth Funk, and even Electro-Industrial, resulting in a harsh, punchy, and funky midtempo sound.

genres.name: French Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of metropolitan France, including that of its regional cultures.

genres.name: French Hip Hop
genres.description: Hip Hop originating from France, typically performed in the French language.

genres.name: French House
genres.description: Originated in France in the mid-1990s, characterized by the use of filtered (low-pass, phaser, etc.) samples of Funk and Disco.

genres.name: French Pop
genres.description: Pop originating from France.

genres.name: French-Canadian Folk Music
genres.description: Brought by French colonists to their Nouvelle-France settlements, primarily based around French Folk Music with influences from English Folk Music and Celtic Folk Music, typically played during gatherings and holidays.

genres.name: Frenchcore
genres.description: Off-beat, bouncy rhythmic patterns and tempos around the 200 BPM range.

genres.name: Frevo
genres.description: Played in a very fast, binary tempo; originated in 1910 on the streets of the northeastern Brazilian city of Recife.

genres.name: Friese bries
genres.description: New Wave and Punk inspired music scene located in the province of Friesland in the Netherlands in the mid-1980s.

genres.name: Fugue
genres.description: Contrapuntal composition and technique for a fixed numbers of musical voices; following the imitations of one main theme.

genres.name: Fuji
genres.description: Combines the ajisaari/wéré tradition of improvisational music performed during Ramadan with other Islamic styles like Apala and sakara.

genres.name: Fula Music
genres.description: Music of the Fula, Fulani, or Fulɓe people, one of the largest ethnic groups in the Sahel region, present from the far West African countries of Senegal and Mauritania to Central African Cameroon with the biggest population located in Nigeria.

genres.name: Full-On Psytrance
genres.description: Faster and more intense, usually set around 145-150 BPM and featuring harder rolling basslines, vocal samples and "spacey" effects.

genres.name: Funaná
genres.description: Upbeat Cape Verdean style which developed on the island of Santiago, based around the diatonic accordion and rhythm provided by the ferrinho.

genres.name: Funeral Doom Metal
genres.description: Features exceptionally slow, funeral dirge-like tempos; crushing, sluggish guitars; mournful, melancholic atmosphere; and distant, hushed growls and grunts.

genres.name: Funeral March
genres.description: Slow, solemn marches usually in a minor key; meant to invoke the feeling of a funeral procession.

genres.name: Fungi
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music native to the Virgin Islands, named after a local dish which features a "mixed-up" flavor that can be compared to the style that combines Western instruments with local ones.

genres.name: Funk
genres.description: Danceable, syncopated grooves carried by bass and drums alongside percussive guitar, keyboard, and/or horn parts, with rhythmic emphasis on the downbeat.

genres.name: Funk 150 bpm
genres.description: Fast tempos, typically reaching 150 bpm and sometimes beyond it, heightened energy and typically faster flows as well.

genres.name: Funk automotivo
genres.description: Catchy, repetitive synths accompanied by a strong four-on-the-floor kick and loud, reverberated vocals.

genres.name: Funk brasileiro
genres.description: Hip Hop-influenced dance style originating from the favelas of Rio de Janeiro and known primarily as "funk" in Brazil.

genres.name: Funk carioca
genres.description: Early scene of Funk brasileiro that began in Rio de Janeiro, developed from a local take on American Miami Bass.

genres.name: Funk de BH
genres.description: Atmospheric, mellow and minimalistic production with sparse percussion, often featuring sound effects or filtered samples.

genres.name: Funk mandelão
genres.description: Simple lyricism, raw and minimalistic production, and distinct drops with bursting bass.

genres.name: Funk melody
genres.description: Light and melodic take on Funk brasileiro, developed alongside Funk carioca.

genres.name: Funk Metal
genres.description: Melds Funk Rock grooves with slap basslines and metallic guitarwork.

genres.name: Funk ostentação
genres.description: Late 2000s take on Funk brasileiro from São Paulo state, featuring Pop Rap influences, having a more accessible sound.

genres.name: Funk Rock
genres.description: Incorporates prominent Funk grooves.

genres.name: Funknejo
genres.description: Incorporates the rhythms, production, and idioms of Funk brasileiro into the universitário genre.

genres.name: Funkot
genres.description: Fast-paced Indonesian form of Electronic Dance Music that combines Eurodance and Trance synths with the syncopated rhythm from Dangdut koplo.

genres.name: Funktronica
genres.description: Originated in eastern North America around the turn of the 21st century, combining trends of Synth Funk and Italo-Disco.

genres.name: Funky Breaks
genres.description: Merging popular 1990s breaks styles like Big Beat with major Funk and Soul elements.

genres.name: Funky House
genres.description: Funky, warm, catchy basslines on top of looped Funk or Disco samples, resulting in an upbeat, bouncy, and pacy groove.

genres.name: Furry Music
genres.description: Created by and for the furry fandom/subculture, an independent art movement focused on anthropomorphic characters.

genres.name: Fusion Gugak
genres.description: Traditional Korean Folk Music and Korean Classical Music combined with elements taken from contemporary styles of popular music and Western music.

genres.name: Future Bass
genres.description: Woozy, detuned synthesizers, 7th chords, harsh basslines, syncopated percussion with fast-paced hi-hats and a melodic, carefree atmosphere.

genres.name: Future Bounce
genres.description: Fusion of Melbourne Bounce and Future House that combines the former's basslines and bouncy, upbeat drops with the latter's metallic, pronounced synth leads.

genres.name: Future Core
genres.description: Blends the speed, basslines, and rhythms of UK Hardcore (mostly coming from the J-core sphere) with euphoric, woozy synths, 7th chords and arpeggios, and vocal chops of Future Bass, particularly Kawaii Future Bass.

genres.name: Future Funk
genres.description: Sample-based form of House which formed out of Vaporwave in the early 2010s.

genres.name: Future Garage
genres.description: Combines the rhythms of late 1990s and early 2000s 2-Step with novel moods and production approaches, commonly featuring jittery, broken rhythms, vocal chops, and warm synth pads and plucks.

genres.name: Future House
genres.description: Features distinctive metallic-sounding drops and frequency-modulated basslines at around 120-130 BPM.

genres.name: Future Rave
