genres.description: Emerged in the late 2010s by combining the mainstage EDM approach with influences from then-popular forms of Techno and old-school Trance/rave-inspired grooves and atmospheres.

genres.name: Future Riddim
genres.description: Melodic and futuristic style inspired by Future Bass, and to a lesser extent Colour Bass and Melodic Dubstep.

genres.name: Futurepop
genres.description: Derivative of EBM, retaining its apocalyptic worldview but incorporating heavy influence from the melodic style of Synthpop.

genres.name: Futurism
genres.description: Radical and militant attitude, rejection of Western Classical Music and traditional criteria of craft, non-conformity, and a fascination with machines.

genres.name: Futuristic Swag
genres.description: Playful, Snap-influenced and party-oriented.

genres.name: G-Funk
genres.description: Relaxed and organic sound featuring live instrumentation, use of P-Funk samples, and high-pitched synth lines.

genres.name: G-House
genres.description: Deep, dark form of House music that primarily incorporates rap samples or original rapping on top of minimal, bassy beats.

genres.name: Gaana
genres.description: Style of Tamil music originating in northern Chennai's working-class communities, defined by fast-paced delivery and introspective lyrics often offering social commentary on everyday life.

genres.name: Gabber
genres.description: Fast-paced and energetic, often in the 160-220 BPM range, with a hallmark of a distinctive distorted kick sound.

genres.name: Gagaku
genres.description: One of the oldest forms of Japanese Classical Music, based on the pentatonic Yo scale, characterized by an elegant sound that is typically solemn, slow-paced, and resonant.

genres.name: Gagauz Folk Music
genres.description: Gagauz people are a Turkic group living mostly in the southern Gagauzia region of Moldova, but also nearby areas like southwestern Ukraine and southeastern Romania.

genres.name: Gagok
genres.description: Vocal songs derived from Korean Classical Music backed by a small orchestra of Jeong-ak ("aristocratic or proper music").

genres.name: Gaita zuliana
genres.description: Emerged in the state of Zulia in the 1950s, merging Spanish Folk Music and Venezuelan Christmas carols.

genres.name: Galician Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional music of the Galician people.

genres.name: Gallican Chant
genres.description: Extinct plainchant tradition originating from the region of Gaul (now modern-day France).

genres.name: Gambang kromong
genres.description: Betawi traditional music which combines elements of Gamelan, Western music and a Chinese-derived pentatonic scale.

genres.name: Gamelan
genres.description: Originated in the island of Java; played by an ensemble typically consisting of metallophones and gongs, sometimes augmented with drums, flutes, and human voices.

genres.name: Gamelan angklung
genres.description: Takes its name from the angklung, an instrument made of bamboo tubes.

genres.name: Gamelan beleganjur
genres.description: Loud, chaotic, highly percussive, and with heavy tempo changes.

genres.name: Gamelan degung
genres.description: Sundanese Gamelan performed by a small orchestra of bronze gongs and metallophones.

genres.name: Gamelan gender wayang
genres.description: Performed with two/four metallophones made out of bronze keys with suspended bamboo tube resonators connected to them.

genres.name: Gamelan gong gede
genres.description: Ceremonial style characterized by a simpler and more melodic approach with clearer and more stable progressions compared to other Balinese orchestras.

genres.name: Gamelan gong kebyar
genres.description: Free compositional techniques and rapidly changing dynamics.

genres.name: Gamelan jegog
genres.description: Played entirely on marimba-like instruments made from bamboo which widely differ in size.

genres.name: Gamelan sekaten
genres.description: Javanese ceremonial Gamelan played with large instruments, strictly unaccompanied by vocals.

genres.name: Gamelan selonding
genres.description: Ensemble consists of four to six musicians playing metallophones made out of iron in a seven-tone scale.

genres.name: Gamelan semar pegulingan
genres.description: Originated in the 16th-17th centuries; features a soft, delicate, and ethereal sound.

genres.name: Ganga
genres.description: Dissonant form of polyphonic singing from the regions of Herzegovina and Dalmatia.

genres.name: Gangsta Rap
genres.description: Lyrics from a gangster's perspective.

genres.name: Garage House
genres.description: Disco-influenced style of House that developed in the 1980s, incorporating elements of Gospel, Soul, and Dub, before evolving into a more upbeat style that prominently features crisp syncopated hi-hats and synth stabs.

genres.name: Garage Psych
genres.description: Emerged from mid-1960s US Garage Rock; characterised by fuzz guitars, cheap organs, experimentation with psychedelic effects and surreal lyricism, and a retained emphasis on raw energy and the pop song format.

genres.name: Garage Punk
genres.description: Combination of the raw fuzztones of the original Garage Rock bands of the 1960s with the tempo and attitude of Punk Rock.

genres.name: Garage Rock
genres.description: Raw and energetic, generally employing simple, sloppy, and fuzzbox-distorted guitar melodies in addition to frequent shouting or screaming.

genres.name: Garage Rock Revival
genres.description: Incorporated the raucous spirit of '60s Garage Rock into the sensibilities of Alternative Rock and Indie Rock; predominant in the '00s.

genres.name: Garba
genres.description: Swinging rhythms and use of clapping/stomping; traditionally performed with the instruments dhol, dholak, tabla, harmonium, and naal, though newer productions can contain Electronic elements.

genres.name: Garifuna Music
genres.description: Music of the Garifuna, an Afro-Indigenous people from Central America and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

genres.name: Geek Rock
genres.description: Emphasizes a nerdy aesthetic, incorporating synthesizers and other instrumentation less common in Alternative Rock alongside quirky Pop-oriented songwriting and dense, witty lyricism on unconventional topics.

genres.name: Genge
genres.description: Combines elements of Dancehall with various traditions of Kenya.

genres.name: Gengetone
genres.description: Takes strong influence from Reggaetón and modern Dancehall, featuring more explicit lyrics and harder beats.

genres.name: Georgian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Georgian people, who mostly live in Georgia.

genres.name: German Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Germany.

genres.name: German Music
genres.description: Music of the German-speaking people, spanning predominately central Europe, primarily Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, among others.

genres.name: Ghazal
genres.description: Developed in Arabia with further evolutions in Persia and the Indian subcontinent; based on rhyming couplets with intricate schemes and deal with romance, loss, and religion.

genres.name: Ghetto Funk
genres.description: Rich sampling, drawing from classic Hip Hop as well as from Funk and Soul, and strong midtempo break grooves.

genres.name: Ghetto House
genres.description: Rough sound based around minimal drum machine-driven tracks and heavy usage of vocal samples.

genres.name: Ghettotech
genres.description: Fuses the syncopation and synthesized sounds of Electro and Detroit Techno with the cut-up samples of Ghetto House and fast rhythms of Miami Bass.

genres.name: Gilaki Music
genres.description: Music of the Gilak people of northern Iran.

genres.name: Ginan
genres.description: Form of musical recitation sacred to Nizari Ismaili Muslims.

genres.name: Girl Group
genres.description: Combines elements of Rhythm & Blues, Rock & Roll, and Traditional Pop; typically performed by trios or quartets of female vocalists.

genres.name: Glam Metal
genres.description: Very catchy hooks and guitar riffs, sing-along choruses, and lyrics often glamorizing the "sex, drugs and rock & roll" lifestyle.

genres.name: Glam Punk
genres.description: Contrasts a snotty, nihilistic, and combative attitude of punk with theatrics and flamboyance.

genres.name: Glam Rock
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Rock & Roll and Blues Rock into catchy Pop Rock melodies, usually accompanied with a strong sense of theatricality.

genres.name: Glitch
genres.description: Uses abstract sound design and malfunctioning electronics—CD skips, data corruption, and hardware noise—as main compositional elements.

genres.name: Glitch Hop
genres.description: Incorporation of IDM-derived production into drum patterns inspired by Hip Hop beats.

genres.name: Glitch Hop [EDM]
genres.description: Tempos around 100-110 BPM, swung, bouncy drum patterns, and a focus on upbeat, danceable drops and buildups.

genres.name: Glitch Pop
genres.description: Incorporates elements of more experimental Electronic styles like IDM and Glitch.

genres.name: Gnawa
genres.description: A mystical musical tradition centred around the qraqab castanets and guembri bass lute, named after its originators, the Afro-Maghrebi Gnawa people.

genres.name: Go-Go
genres.description: Dominated by drums and percussion (primarily congas) with heavily syncopated rhythms, bursts of horns, and call-and-response vocals.

genres.name: Goa Trance
genres.description: Forerunner of Psytrance styles that emerged in the early 1990s, distinguished by old-school, organic sound with rapid, oriental-inspired melodies.

genres.name: Goan Music
genres.description: Music of Goa, a former Portuguese colony on the west coast of India, rooted in the traditions of its inhabitants.

genres.name: Gogo Music
genres.description: Music of the Gogo People (Wagogo), who inhabit Central Tanzania.

genres.name: Gommance
genres.description: Emerged in Réunion, mixing Caribbean, African and Afro-Dutch influences.

genres.name: Gondang
genres.description: Traditional ensemble in Bataknese traditional music of North Sumatra, taking its name from its leading instrument - a unique set of toned drums.

genres.name: Goombay
genres.description: Bahamian music centered around the drum known as the goombay, a sort of membranophone.

genres.name: Goral Music
genres.description: Music of highlanders occupying Northern Carpathians (Gorals).

genres.name: Goregrind
genres.description: Death Metal-influenced riffs with rhythms ranging from very fast to slower mid-tempos correlated with pitch-shifted vocals, sloppy playing and production, and gore-themed aesthetics.

genres.name: Gorenoise
genres.description: Combines and subverts Goregrind and Grindcore with brash Noise and even faster drum tempos.

genres.name: Gospel
genres.description: Arising from vocal Christian tradition often featuring emotive performances, layered accompaniments, and themes of faith and salvation.

genres.name: Gospel House
genres.description: Incorporates heavy Gospel elements and singing borrowed from classic and contemporary gospel, usually in the form of choir vocals and call-and-response chants.

genres.name: Gothenburg Sound
genres.description: Pioneering Melodic Death Metal scene of Gothenburg, Sweden.

genres.name: Gothic Country
genres.description: Evokes the Southern Gothic literary genre through morbid lyrical themes and melancholic sounds that emphasize its American Folk Music and Post-Punk influences.

genres.name: Gothic Metal
genres.description: Features heavy, low-mid tempo riffs, somber, gloomy atmosphere accentuated by ethereal keyboards and synthesizer layers, and vocal styles ranging from raspy growls to female operatic singing.

genres.name: Gothic Rock
genres.description: Combines drama and a dark atmosphere with effects-laden guitars, prominent basslines, propulsive drums, and occasional keyboards and drum machines.

genres.name: Gqom
genres.description: Evolved from South African House, specifically Kwaito; often described as a more minimal and raw version.

genres.name: Grand opéra
genres.description: French style characterized by its enlarged scope and sense of grandeur, with bigger orchestras and casts, and ornate sceneries and costumes.

genres.name: Graphical Sound
genres.description: Compositional technique in which markings are manually applied to a medium, then processed by a machine to produce synthetic sound from the markings in real time.

genres.name: Grebo
genres.description: Short-lived English subculture and associated music; raw, futuristic, sample-heavy form of Alternative Dance with a dirty guitar sound.

genres.name: Greek Folk Music
genres.description: Greek folk traditions.

genres.name: Greek Music
genres.description: Music of the Greek people.

genres.name: Greenlandic Music
genres.description: Majorly from Inuit ethnic groups in Greenland, a large island between the Atlantic and Arctic Oceans.

genres.name: Greenwich Village Scene
genres.description: Collective of folk singers who mainly performed in small venues (basements, bars, and coffee houses) throughout Greenwich Village from the late 1950s to mid-1960s.

genres.name: Gregorian Chant
genres.description: Liturgical, monophonic chant that accompanied Mass and other rituals in Western Christianity.

genres.name: Grime
genres.description: UK Garage-derived production style characterized by dark, fast-paced, often aggressive beats that commonly features fast-paced MCing.

genres.name: Grindcore
genres.description: Brief and intense song structures featuring a plethora of blast beats, down-tuned and tremolo-picked guitars, and abrasive, usually raw production.

genres.name: Griot Music
genres.description: Type of hereditary professional caste in West African Music culture that preserves tradition.

genres.name: Groove Metal
genres.description: Midtempo riffs influenced by Thrash Metal but with a greater focus on rhythmic syncopation and heaviness over speed.

genres.name: Group Sounds
genres.description: Japanese bands in the mid-to-late 1960s who began performing a style of Beat primarily in English.

genres.name: Grunge
genres.description: Mixes Punk and Metal sensibilities into a mid-tempo approach featuring a heavy, "sludgy" guitar sound, "raspy" vocals and angsty lyricism.

genres.name: Gstanzl
genres.description: Short improvised traditional song form the larger Bavarian region (Southeastern Germany and Austria), satirical and often being accompanied with dances.

genres.name: Guaguancó
genres.description: Emerged after the abolition of slavery in Cuba in 1886; usually features a lead singer, accompanied by three large drums, known as tumbadoras or congas, and a call-and-response chorus.

genres.name: Guajira
genres.description: Originally developed in Cuba between the 18th and 19th Century as a narrative style influenced by Tonada chilena.

genres.name: Guaracha
genres.description: Humorous song with short notes and a fast tempo that commonly alternates a short fourth line verse with a repeated fourth line chorus.

genres.name: Guaracha [EDM]
genres.description: Originated in Colombia, featuring "fluttering" trumpets, accordion, and tambora drums.

genres.name: Guaracha santiagueña
genres.description: Fast, upbeat and danceable rhythm originated in the province of Santiago del Estero, Argentina as a fusion of Chacarera and Chamamé.

genres.name: Guarania
genres.description: Slow and melancholic rhythms, primarily performed on the Paraguayan harp.

genres.name: Gufeng
genres.description: Emphasizes Chineseness and an "ancient" atmosphere, and often features semi-classical lyrics.

genres.name: Guggenmusik
genres.description: Alemannic type of Marching Band played at carnival events, featuring a cacophonous, seemingly "out of tune" sound.

genres.name: Guided Meditation
genres.description: Practice wherein an instructor guides the listener through the process of meditation throughout a session.

genres.name: Gujarati Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Gujarati people, who primarily live in the western Indian state of Gujarat.

genres.name: Gumbe
genres.description: Vocal and percussive tradition from Guinea-Bissau developed in the 1970s as a fusion of various traditional genres in the country; sometimes used as a catch-all term for the music of Guinea-Bissau in general.

genres.name: Gurage Music
genres.description: Music of the Gurage people of Central Ethiopia.

genres.name: Gwo ka
genres.description: Developed in the island of Guadeloupe; driven by a group of gwo ka drums.

genres.name: Gypsy Punk
genres.description: Strong Eastern European influences, especially various kinds of Romani Folk Music and Balkan Folk Music as well as Klezmer.

genres.name: Género chico
genres.description: Light, small-scale musical comedy with mild social commentary, populist themes, and catchy melodies.

genres.name: Għana
genres.description: Indigenous Maltese folk which consists of quatrains, ideally improvised, following a rhyme scheme of a-b-c-b, and sung to traditional tunes, usually accompanied by guitars.

genres.name: H8000
genres.description: Belgian Hardcore [Punk] scene centered in West Flanders, famed for its Vegan Straight Edge Metalcore.

genres.name: Habanera
genres.description: Based around the Habanera rhythm, where the most typical instruments used are guitars, lutes, and bandurrias.

genres.name: Haight-Ashbury Scene
genres.description: Influential Psychedelic Rock scene which emerged by summer 1966 in the Haight-Ashbury district of San Francisco and peaked in terms of notoriety by summer 1967, coinciding with a massive influx of visitors, media interest, and ensuing commercialisation.

genres.name: Haitian Music
genres.description: Encompasses the styles of music developed by the Haitian people.

genres.name: Haitian Vodou Drumming
genres.description: Form of rhythmic performance by Haitian Vodou practitioners, played at associated ceremonies.

genres.name: Halftime
genres.description: Offshoot of Drum and Bass (mainly Neurofunk) characterized by off-kilter rhythms playing at around 80-85 BPM (half of normal DnB pace), influenced by Dubstep, Wonky, Trap [EDM], and Hip Hop.

genres.name: Hamburger Schule
genres.description: Combines traditions of the Neue Deutsche Welle based on Grunge with Pop hooks and elements of Punk Rock.

genres.name: Han Folk Music
genres.description: Chinese folk form often played at weddings and funerals, using the Suona (a form of oboe) and Chuigushou (a specific type of percussive ensemble), together with heterophony.

genres.name: Hands Up
genres.description: Prominent, melodic supersaw leads, Dance-Pop derived hooks, and a strong reliance on sidechained basslines and hard, powerful drums.

genres.name: Hanmai
genres.description: Chinese performance style featuring a performer shouting lyrics over an upbeat backing track.

genres.name: Haozi
genres.description: Chinese Work Song that originated from collective manual labor and usually follows a call-and-response structure, aiming to coordinate work.

genres.name: Hapa haole
genres.description: Hawaiian musical traditions adapted to popular American Jazz and Pop styles.

genres.name: Happy Hardcore
genres.description: Emerged in the 1990s from the UK Breakbeat Hardcore scene; characterized by saccharine vocals, uplifting piano riffs and spacey effects, gradually developing to emphasize extremely fast-paced four-on-the-floor beats.

genres.name: Happy Rock
genres.description: Late 2000s Brazilian movement made as a response against Emo with a bright aesthetic, heavy use of electronic instruments and distorted vocals.

genres.name: Harana
genres.description: Hispanic-influenced lyrical courtship music traditionally sung by men, accompanied by guitar based on the danza rhythm.

genres.name: Harawi
genres.description: Repeating phrases of sung poetry dealing with emotional topics.

genres.name: Hard Beat
genres.description: Short-lived, harder, harsh form of New Beat with Industrial, Acid House and EBM-influenced arrangement.

genres.name: Hard Bop
genres.description: A continuation of Bebop that reintroduces more traditional African-American musical features, such as bluesy melodies, slow to medium tempos, and a more groove-oriented sound, while retaining the expressive improvisation.

genres.name: Hard Dance
genres.description: Umbrella term for EDM mainly developed out of Hard Trance and UK Hard House; usually characterized by fast tempos, hard kick drums and a "bouncy" syncopated groove.

genres.name: Hard Drum
genres.description: Highly percussive, syncopated rhythms, influences from global contemporary genres, and lack of melodic elements, with a tempo lingering around 130 BPM.

genres.name: Hard Rock
genres.description: Originated in the mid-to-late 1960s from Psychedelic Rock and Blues Rock with a heavy sound characterized by distorted guitars and power chords.

genres.name: Hard Techno
genres.description: Typically rave-oriented form characterized by hard, prominent kick drums, pounding rhythms, fast tempos around 140-160 BPM, and aggressive, often distorted sounds.

genres.name: Hard Trance
genres.description: Rave-oriented form of Trance infusing its atmospheres with faster, thumping rhythms and strong melodic / bassline sections, initially spawning out of the first wave in early-1990s Western Europe.

genres.name: Hard Trap
genres.description: Often abrasive subgenre of Trap [EDM] with heavy influence from Hardstyle.

genres.name: Hardbag
genres.description: Development of handbag / Diva House characterized by heavier, hard hitting percussion, more pronounced rave and early Hard Dance elements, and fewer vocals.

genres.name: Hardcore [EDM]
genres.description: Umbrella term for a wide variety of fast-paced and energetic Electronic Dance Music styles that have been developed since the early 1990s.

genres.name: Hardcore [Punk]
genres.description: Broad genre which encompasses the first wave of Hardcore Punk beginning in the 1970s, as well as its derivative styles that incorporate diverse musical influences and stray away from the core Punk Rock sound.

genres.name: Hardcore Breaks
genres.description: Revival of Breakbeat Hardcore which emerged in the 2000s, bringing in modern influences and production techniques.

genres.name: Hardcore Hip Hop
genres.description: Confrontation and aggression, whether in the lyricism, vocal delivery, hard beats, heavy production, or any combination thereof.

genres.name: Hardcore Punk
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1970s, often featuring extensive use of yelling or screaming, a stripped-down production style, and very short songs.

genres.name: Hardgroove Techno
genres.description: Features shuffling grooves with heavy emphasis on layered percussive elements; often includes a mix of samples and drum machines played at a range of 135-140 BPM.

genres.name: Hardline
genres.description: Militant outgrowth of Vegan Straight Edge influenced by deep ecology.

genres.name: Hardstep
genres.description: Very compressed and sparse drumming, extensive use of kick drums and gritty, minimalistic production style with emphasis on simple, deep, modulated bass patterns.

genres.name: Hardstyle
genres.description: Hard, four-on-the-floor kick drums, fast tempo around 150 BPM, reverse bass and harsh, distorted synths.

genres.name: Hardtek
genres.description: Modern version of the "tribecore" sound featuring deep alternating basses and festival EDM-influenced drops.

genres.name: Hardvapour
genres.description: Influenced by Hardcore [EDM] and Techno and made in response to the Vaporwave movement.

genres.name: Hardwave
genres.description: Harder, festival-oriented offshoot of Wave, combining its "reese" basses and icy synths with Trap [EDM] drum patterns, build-up-drop structures, and fuller sound influenced by Trance and Hardstyle.

genres.name: Harlem Renaissance
genres.description: Influential 1920s and '30s cultural movement centered on the African American community in Harlem, New York.

genres.name: Harsh Noise
genres.description: Highly aggressive walls of sound that assault the listener.

genres.name: Harsh Noise Wall
genres.description: Harsh, distorted walls of sound that feature few dynamic variations and often take the form of long compositions with little to no change or progression over time.

genres.name: Hasidic Music
genres.description: Covers the music of Hasidic Jews, primarily characterized by spiritual, intense, and devotional, singing and melodies.

genres.name: Hauntology
genres.description: Movement that, through techniques found within Ambient and Sound Collage, aims to warp musical styles and broadcast media from the mid-20th century post-war era into an uncanny, lost, "haunted" atmosphere.

genres.name: Hausa Music
genres.description: Hausa are one of the largest ethnic groups in Africa, living mainly in northern Nigeria and southern Niger in west Africa.

genres.name: Hawaiian Music
genres.description: Includes a variety of syncopated rhythms, percussion and vocal styles, including chanting (mele) and falsetto.

genres.name: Hazara Folk Music
genres.description: Folk music of the Hazara people, mainly native to central Afghanistan.

genres.name: Heartland Rock
genres.description: Borrows elements from Folk Rock, Roots Rock, and 1950s-60s Rock & Roll; often characterized by its conscious, communal lyrical concerns and working-class appeal.

genres.name: Heaven Trap
genres.description: Blends Trap [EDM]’s signature percussion and sub-basses with euphoric, uplifting, melodious drops prominently derived from Festival Progressive House, contrary to the gritty, "dirty" nature of other EDM trap styles.

genres.name: Heavy Metal
genres.description: Heavier outgrowth of Hard Rock featuring greater distortion and intensity along with lesser Blues influences.

genres.name: Heavy Psych
genres.description: Developed in the late 1960s with influence from Blues Rock, such as heavy dependence on riffs and willingness to improvise, adding crushing levels of heaviness with thick fuzzy guitars to create a doomy and morose atmosphere.

genres.name: Heikyoku
genres.description: Semi-classical bardic tradition in Japan analogous to the troubadour music of medieval Europe.

genres.name: Hellenic Black Metal
genres.description: Black metal scene in Greece with more mid-tempo songwriting and pronounced Heavy Metal influence.

genres.name: HexD
genres.description: Heavily bit-crushed vocals, sometimes sped-up and pitched-up, and highly compressed and distorted production, typically made from existing material of other genres.

genres.name: Hi-NRG
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1970s and quickly became the most popular form of Electronic Dance Music in the LGBT club scenes of San Francisco and New York, characterized by its uptempo, high-energy sound.

genres.name: Hi-Tech Full-On
genres.description: Largely Japanese genre with an energetic and glitchy sound derived from Full-On Psytrance and Complextro.

genres.name: High Quality Rip
genres.description: Community based on bait-and-switch remixes of music, localized online.

genres.name: Highlife
genres.description: Originally began along the Ghanaian coast in the 1920s as a blend of western brass band instrumentation and rhythms with traditional Akan Music and Dagomba Music.

genres.name: Hill Country Blues
genres.description: Emphasizes a steady hypnotic groove, sparse percussive and highly energetic guitar riffs, and often features meandering structures with unconventional and usually fewer chord changes compared to Delta Blues.

genres.name: Hill Tribe Music
genres.description: Music of the various ethnic groups residing in the hills of Mainland Southeast Asia and Southwest China, also known as the region of Zomia.

genres.name: Himene tarava
genres.description: Protestant choral songs in Tahiti and other southern Polynesian islands.

genres.name: Hindustani Classical Music
genres.description: North Indian traditional music (including parts of Pakistan, Afghanistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, and Bhutan) with roots reaching back to the 12th century CE.

genres.name: Hip Hop
genres.description: Emerged primarily on the United States East Coast in African-American communities in the late 1970s; emphasizes rhythmic beat patterns and a type of spoken vocal delivery known as rapping.

genres.name: Hip Hop Soul
genres.description: Hip Hop-oriented style that evolved out of New Jack Swing in the early 1990s.

genres.name: Hip House
genres.description: Incorporates production elements of early Hip Hop and usually rapping into 1980s House.

genres.name: Hip-hopolo
genres.description: 2000s Polish Hip Hop scene focused on a mainstream approach; received massive popularity and overwhelming criticism from the hip hop community.

genres.name: Hipco
genres.description: Developed in Liberia, often featuring conscious and political lyrics and influences from local dance styles.

genres.name: Hiplife
genres.description: Fusion of Ghanaian Highlife with Hip Hop.

genres.name: Hispanic American Folk Music
genres.description: Encompasses many varieties of folk traditions from Hispanic America.

genres.name: Hispanic American Music
genres.description: Includes all genres created by Hispanic Americans.

genres.name: Hispanic Music
genres.description: Music of Hispanic America and Spain, and the genres shared between them.

genres.name: Hmong Folk Music
genres.description: Folk traditions of the Hmong people, an ethnic group localized in Laos, Vietnam, China, and Thailand.

genres.name: Hmong Pop
genres.description: Popular music of the Hmong ethnicity, with roots in the Hmong Folk Music and influenced by Western and East Asian forms of Pop music.

genres.name: Hoboken Sound
genres.description: Predominantly 1980s New Jersey scene that blended contemporary Post-Punk and New Wave with Power Pop melodicism and Garage Rock directness, becoming heavily influential to early American Jangle Pop and Alternative Rock as a whole.

genres.name: Hokkien Pop
genres.description: Modern Pop music sung in Hokkien dialects, with its industry largely centered across Taiwan and Southeast Asia.

genres.name: Holy Minimalism
genres.description: Style informed by Christian Liturgical Music that emphasizes slow sustained rhythmic values, soft dynamics, and silence to produce a contemplative and reverential atmosphere.

genres.name: Holy Terror
genres.description: Offshoot of the Process Church of Final Judgement and The Abraxas Foundation sects, focused on the occult and demonology, as well as apocalyptic, misanthropic themes.

genres.name: Honky Tonk
genres.description: Upbeat style that retains much of the common instrumentation of Traditional Country, as well as featuring prominent guitars (especially the steel guitar), strong backbeats and lyrics commonly about the working-class life.

genres.name: Honky-Tonk Piano
genres.description: Nostalgic revival popularised in the 1950s which is more upbeat and whimsical, with a bright and detuned piano sound.

genres.name: Honkyoku
genres.description: Japanese Classical Music performed solo on a bamboo flute shakuhachi.

genres.name: Horror Punk
genres.description: Thematically and lyrically derived from Horror movies, typically with a nostalgic and campy attitude.

genres.name: Horror Synth
genres.description: Combines eerie and haunting synth pads and sharp, abrasive sounds to create atmospheres that accentuated the dark, unnerving, violent, or ghostly themes of horror films.

genres.name: Horrorcore
genres.description: Lyrical and aesthetic focus on the macabre and morbid, with production generally of a darker nature than is typically found in other Hip Hop.

genres.name: Hot Rod Music
genres.description: Features prominent lyrics about hot rods and car culture and incorporates Sound Effects and guitar textures to mimic sounds made by automobiles.

genres.name: House
genres.description: Generally features a four-on-the-floor beat within 110-140 BPM, a groove built on swing and syncopation, synthesized basslines, repetitive melodic elements, and an upbeat mood.

genres.name: Houston Sound
genres.description: Features slow to medium tempos, heavy bass, prominent organs and horns, and live instruments such as keyboards, bass guitar and wah-wah pedal.

genres.name: Huaylarsh
genres.description: Festive Andean music with vibrant rhythm featuring saxophones and violins, typical of the central Peruvian region.

genres.name: Huayno
genres.description: Andean dance music that incorporates both pre-Hispanic and Western musical elements.

genres.name: Humppa
genres.description: Finnish music related to Jazz and the Foxtrot.

genres.name: Hungarian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Hungarians.

genres.name: Hyang-ak
genres.description: One of the most common and oldest surviving forms of Korean court music.

genres.name: Hybrid Trap
genres.description: Blending Trap [EDM]'s typical percussion and sub-basses with major influences from heavy bass music genres, and in particular, metallic, gritty, and off-kilter sound design, originally derived from Brostep.

genres.name: Hymns
genres.description: Performed and written with the purpose of praise, adoration, and prayer, often addressed to deities or other cultural figures.

genres.name: Hyper Techno
genres.description: Exaggerated fast form of Belgian Techno for the Japanese market, focusing mainly on synth sounds and samples typical of 1990s dance music.

genres.name: Hyperpop
genres.description: Developed and took inspiration from Bubblegum Bass and popular 2000s-2010s Electropop, characterized by eclectic, unconventional, mechanical-sounding and dense production; and by manipulated, usually auto-tuned vocals.

genres.name: Hypertechno
genres.description: Emerged in the 2020s by mixing fast tempos, prominent basslines, and hard-hitting drums derived from popular Techno with simplistic, catchy melodies and vocals, often influenced by 2000s Hard Dance, Eurodance and Electropop.

genres.name: Hyphy
genres.description: Party-focused style with upbeat tempos, heavy bass and prominent synths, all underpinned by a distinctive West Coast-style rhythm, claps on beats 2 and 4, and a strong kick drum on beats 1, 2, and either 3 or 4.

genres.name: Hypnagogic Pop
genres.description: 21st century style that refracts the pop culture of past decades through surreal, low-fidelity production and emulation of outdated media formats or equipment.

genres.name: Hát lô tô
genres.description: Short songs performed in the Vietnamese lô tô game to reveal drawn numbers.

genres.name: Hưng ca
genres.description: Diasporic Vietnamese movement originating in the United States during the 1980s; characterised by nationalistic and socio-political lyrics.

genres.name: Iberian Music
genres.description: Music of the Iberian peninsula.

genres.name: Ibiza Trance
genres.description: Builds on the relaxing island atmosphere of Balearic Beat, though with a slightly faster tempo of around 130 BPM.

genres.name: Icelandic Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Iceland, including a variety of styles like the rímur, the kvædaskapur and langspil instrumental music.

genres.name: IDM
genres.description: Emerged through the development of Electronic Dance Music idioms into a less club-oriented and more experimental direction, often incorporating unconventional sound design and complex rhythms.

genres.name: Idol kayō
genres.description: More Westernized and upbeat form of Kayōkyoku popular in the 1970s and 1980s which acted as a precursor to J-Pop.

genres.name: Igbo Music
genres.description: Music of the Igbo people, who live mainly in a region of southeastern Nigeria often known as "Igboland".

genres.name: Igorot Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Igorot people of the Cordillera region in the northern Philippines, known for their gong ensembles.

genres.name: Illbient
genres.description: Combines Ambient soundscapes with Hip Hop drum patterns, breaks, and samples through the busy effect layering of Dub.

genres.name: Ilocano Music
genres.description: Music by the Ilocano people, an ethnic group residing in the northwestern tip of Luzon.

genres.name: Impressionism
genres.description: Originated in late 19th to early 20th century France as a reaction to Romanticism, placing a greater focus on depicting atmosphere and mood rather than fixed concepts.

genres.name: Impromptu
genres.description: Composition written to sound like a spur-of-the-moment improvisation.

genres.name: Indeterminacy
genres.description: Leaves elements of composition, performance, or both up to chance.

genres.name: Indian Pop
genres.description: Commonly based out of India, Pakistan and Bangladesh and almost always sung in Hindi, Urdu or Bengali, implements South Asian Music in context of American and European Pop and Rock music.

genres.name: Indie Folk
genres.description: Combines the melodic sensibilities and production style of Indie Rock and Indie Pop with acoustic instrumentation and influences from Folk, Singer-Songwriter, and sometimes Country.

genres.name: Indie Pop
genres.description: Back-to-basics Rock approach combining a less mainstream and DIY ethos with melodic, lighthearted and straightforward songwriting.

genres.name: Indie Rock
genres.description: Associated with a less mainstream-oriented and a DIY approach while often dabbling in Pop-informed melodic songwriting, eclecticism, and adopting an "authentic" or raw style.

genres.name: Indie Surf
genres.description: Reverb-drenched, nostalgic, and often lo-fi, with influences from Surf Rock and Vocal Surf; rose to popularity around 2009.

genres.name: Indietronica
genres.description: Leftfield or DIY approach characterised by simpler Pop-informed melodies, often incorporating vocals or live instrumentation alongside Electronic production.

genres.name: Indigenous American Music
genres.description: Diverse styles and genres developed by the indigenous peoples of the Americas.

genres.name: Indigenous American Traditional Music
genres.description: Meta-genre encompassing traditions attributed to the indigenous peoples of the Americas.

genres.name: Indigenous Andean Music
genres.description: Diverse styles and genres developed by the indigenous peoples of the Andes.

genres.name: Indigenous Australian Traditional Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Aboriginal Australians and Torres Strait Islanders, collectively known as Indigenous Australians.

genres.name: Indigenous North American Music
genres.description: Diverse styles and genres developed by the indigenous peoples of present-day Canada, the United States and northwestern Mexico.

genres.name: Indigenous Taiwanese Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the various Austronesian people groups that make up the indigenous population of the island of Taiwan.

genres.name: Indo Jazz
genres.description: Fuses the various musical traditions of the Indian subcontinent with jazzy musical structures.

genres.name: Indo-Caribbean Music
genres.description: Music of the Indo-Caribbean diaspora.

genres.name: Indonesian Music
genres.description: Music of the Indonesian people, including those of the majority groups residing in Java, Sumatra, Kalimantan, Bali and other major native areas.

genres.name: Indorock
genres.description: Predominantly instrumental style influenced by Country, Malay Music, and Hawaiian Music; created in the late 1950s by Indo and Moluccan expatriates from Indonesia to the Netherlands.

genres.name: Industrial
genres.description: Emerged out of Punk and avant-garde art movements in the mid-1970s, often characterized by a bleak, mechanical atmosphere, the use of metallic percussion as well as other unconventional instruments, and extensive use of sampling influenced by Musique concrète.

genres.name: Industrial & Noise
genres.description: Umbrella encompassing Noise and Industrial, as well as later derivatives that combine the latter aesthetics with other styles and in more accessible directions which fall under Post-Industrial.

genres.name: Industrial Folk Song
genres.description: Details the experiences and aspirations of industrial laborers and their working conditions; frequently rooted in labor causes and often used for protest and organizational purposes.

genres.name: Industrial Hardcore
genres.description: Fuses the sonic palettes and aesthetics of Industrial with the intense rhythms of Gabber, Speedcore, Doomcore and other subsequent styles.

genres.name: Industrial Hip Hop
genres.description: Incorporates harsh elements inspired by Industrial music such as blaring, noisy synths, distorted and metallic percussion, as well as more aggressive and off-kilter rapping styles.

genres.name: Industrial Metal
genres.description: Incorporates the abrasive and heavy sound of Industrial into Metal, using elements like synthesizers and drum machines.

genres.name: Industrial Rock
genres.description: Incorporates abrasive guitars and synthesizers inspired by Industrial and various Post-Industrial styles.

genres.name: Industrial Techno
genres.description: Harder, darker style of Techno which draws parallels with factories and the rhythm of machinery.

genres.name: Inkiranya
genres.description: Influential drumming style originating in Burundi carried out by a percussion ensemble.

genres.name: Insect Sounds
genres.description: Recordings that capture the sounds produced by insects.

genres.name: Instrumental Hip Hop
genres.description: Can take the form of instrumental versions of songs that normally feature rapping, or hip hop originally released and always intended to be instrumental.

genres.name: Integral Serialism
genres.description: Application of twelve-tone technique in early Serialism to as many compositional factors as possible (in an attempt to apply total serial control).

genres.name: Interview
genres.description: Recording of a specific person/s during a formal conversation arranged for historical archiving or media broadcast, often in a question and answer format in which the interviewee shares their views and personal anecdotes with the audience.

genres.name: Inuit Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Inuit people, the aboriginal peoples inhabiting the Arctic regions of Canada, Alaska, and Greenland.

genres.name: Inuit Vocal Games
genres.description: Practiced by the Inuit of Canada, two vocalists face each other decimeters away and try to outlast each other with intense and unusual vocal techniques.

genres.name: Ionian Islands Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music from the Ionian Islands in Greece.

genres.name: Iraqi Maqam
genres.description: Highly structured but semi-improvised and rhythmically complex compositions built around set structures which consist of specific maqam modes.

genres.name: Irish Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Ireland.

genres.name: Irish Showband
genres.description: Phenomenon lasting from the mid-1950s until the early 1980s, often performed a mixture of currently popular music and skits.

genres.name: Isicathamiya
genres.description: A cappella Zulu style, which takes a softer, more melodious approach, in contrast to the powerful, loud sound of the earlier Mbube style.

genres.name: Islamic Religious Music & Recitation
genres.description: Music and melodic recitation involved in the Islamic faith, such as the reading of the Qur'an with its melodic component (qira'ah), the adhan call to prayer, and the elements often used in the practice of dhikr (particularly in Sufism).

genres.name: Israeli Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Jewish settlers of Eretz Yisra'el.

genres.name: Istrian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Istria.

genres.name: Italian Folk Music
genres.description: Folk traditions of Italy.

genres.name: Italian Music
genres.description: Music of the Italian people.

genres.name: Italo Dance
genres.description: Appeared in the 1990s after the decline of Italo-Disco, featuring rhythmic influence from that genre.

genres.name: Italo House
genres.description: Originated in Italy during the late 1980s, making use of anthemic pianos, diva vocals, and Dance-Pop song structures.

genres.name: Italo Pop
genres.description: Romantic style developed in Italy in the late 1950s including various influences such as Chanson and Schlager.

genres.name: Italo-Disco
genres.description: Produced primarily in Italy and is characterized by the use of synthesizers, drum machines, and sometimes vocoders to create a mechanical, Electronic version of Disco with futuristic atmosphere.

genres.name: Izlan
genres.description: Uses sung poetry with a focus on love themes.

genres.name: Izvorna bosanska muzika
genres.description: Polyphonic vocal music that developed in Bosnia in the 20th century, bearing connections to traditional Bosnian genres.

genres.name: J-core
genres.description: Eclectic scene of Japanese Hardcore [EDM] heavily associated with Doujin Music.

genres.name: J-Euro
genres.description: Italian-oriented Japanese scene of Eurobeat, which emerged with Japanese-language covers of Italian songs in the early-to-mid-1990s.

genres.name: J-Pop
genres.description: Commercial Pop of Japan after the advent of the Heisei era (1989), characterized by modernized production, a more eclectic sound palette, and a more westernized vocal style.

genres.name: Jackin' House
genres.description: Punchy, 'shuffly' percussion, strong grooves, funky basslines, and chopped-up samples.

genres.name: Jaipongan
genres.description: Sundanese performance music; uses instruments typical for Gamelan ensembles, but expands the drum section.

genres.name: Jam Band
genres.description: Arose in late 1960s America, usually performed in a live setting and combines diverse styles under the Rock umbrella, often influenced by genres such as Funk, Jazz, Country and Blues.

genres.name: Jamaican Music
genres.description: Regional music of Jamaica ranges from its cultural origins in traditional and religious folk of the late 19th and early 20th centuries to the international popularity of Reggae from the 1970s onwards.

genres.name: Jamaican Ska
genres.description: Originated in Jamaica with groups who combined Jazz and Rhythm & Blues with rhythms of traditional Caribbean Music like Mento and Calypso.

genres.name: James Bay Fiddling
genres.description: Fiddle playing of the James Bay Cree people, characterised by a fusion of Scottish style with Cree rhythms.

genres.name: Jamgrass
genres.description: Emphasizes instrumental jamming and extended performances with many outside influences.

genres.name: Jangle Pop
genres.description: Treble-heavy guitars with arpeggiated melodies, distinct basslines, and often propulsive, repetitive strum-rhythms; frequently influenced by Post-Punk.

genres.name: Japanese Classical Music
genres.description: Classical music of Japan.

genres.name: Japanese Folk Music
genres.description: Folk traditions of Japan.

genres.name: Japanese Hardcore
genres.description: Bands from Japan, performing styles such as Burning Spirits, Crust Punk, and Thrashcore.

genres.name: Japanese Hip Hop
genres.description: Hip Hop which is created by artists who are either based in or from Japan.

genres.name: Japanese Idol
genres.description: Contemporary Japanese singer-dancers valued mainly for their personality and charisma, often performing as groups in a cutesy and youthful style.

genres.name: Japanese Music
genres.description: Japanese meta-genre covers all forms of music, traditional or contemporary, rooted in Japanese Folk Music.

genres.name: Javanese Gamelan
genres.description: Broad classification grouping Gamelan genres native to Javanese culture.

genres.name: Javanese Music
genres.description: Music of the Javanese people.

genres.name: Jawaiian
genres.description: Hawaiian branch of Reggae, typically blends local traditional melodies, harmonies, incorporating specialty instruments such as ukulele and steel guitar.

genres.name: Jazz
genres.description: Originating in African American communities in the Southern United States around the turn of the 20th century, building on New Orleans Brass Band ensemble and influences from Ragtime and Blues to become a very popular style by the emergence of Swing in the 1930s.

genres.name: Jazz Fusion
genres.description: Near-universal usage of electric guitars and keyboards coupled with influences from genres such as Rock, Rhythm & Blues, Funk, and Traditional Folk Music, and a relative degree of harmonic simplicity.

genres.name: Jazz guachaca
genres.description: Encompasses Jazz influences with Hispanic American Music styles such as Cueca, Bolero, Tango and Corrido.

genres.name: Jazz manouche
genres.description: Combines Jazz with several aspects of Romani Folk Music.

genres.name: Jazz Mugham
genres.description: Combines Jazz with elements of Azerbaijani Mugham, featuring jazz-inspired instrumental compositions, improvisations, wind and vocal elements, as well as modal scales and ornamentation techniques for emotional depth.

genres.name: Jazz Poetry
genres.description: Emerged in the 1920s, incorporating the style and rhythms of Jazz as both art forms spread throughout African-American communities in the United States.

genres.name: Jazz Pop
genres.description: Pop that incorporates elements from Jazz.

genres.name: Jazz Rap
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Jazz through the use of samples or live instrumentation.

genres.name: Jazz-Funk
genres.description: Jazz highly influenced by Funk.

genres.name: Jazz-Rock
genres.description: Strongly influenced by Jazz in structure and/or instrumentation.

genres.name: Jazzstep
genres.description: Combines the rhythm and speed of Drum and Bass with the melodies, composition, and instrumentation of Jazz.

genres.name: Jeong-ak
genres.description: Also known as proper music; dates back to the Later Silla period of 668–935.

genres.name: Jerk
genres.description: Sparse, snare-heavy drum patterns loosely inspired by Jerk Rap, which take major elements from other prominent 2010s and 2020s underground hip hop genres like Plugg.

genres.name: Jerk Rap
genres.description: Sparse beats, simple melodies, and party-centric lyrics geared towards a style of dance called “jerkin’.”

genres.name: Jersey Club
genres.description: Emerged in Newark in the late 2000s; features fast tempos, hard kicks, and less prominent breakbeats.

genres.name: Jersey Club Rap
genres.description: Incorporates Jersey Club's distinct kick-heavy rhythms, which are modified to better suit rapping, featuring less sampling and more atmospheric production than earlier Jersey club.

genres.name: Jersey Drill
genres.description: Mixes Drill and Jersey Club production, characterized by an energetic sound and distinct syncopated rhythms.

genres.name: Jersey Shore Sound
genres.description: Stylistically correlated to Heartland Rock, with cultural origins in coastal New Jersey; characterized by its horn-heavy mixture of 1960s Rock & Roll, Rhythm & Blues, and Doo-Wop.

genres.name: Jersey Sound
genres.description: Soulful, melodic, Gospel-infused House music developed in Newark, NJ in the late 1980s and early 1990s with an emphasis on songcraft.

genres.name: Jewish Liturgical Music
genres.description: Employed for different purposes in the practices of Jewish religion, such as the Kriyat haTorah of biblical verses during synagogue services.

genres.name: Jewish Music
genres.description: Different Jewish forms coming from different regions of the world, influenced by local cultures.

genres.name: Jiangnan sizhu
genres.description: Originating from Jiangnan region and played by a varying ensemble of stringed instruments, flutes, mouth organs and small percussions.

genres.name: Jibaro
genres.description: Traditions of the mountain-dwelling jibaro people that live primarily in Puerto Rico.

genres.name: Jigg
genres.description: Club-oriented genre characterized by heavy 808-driven beats, imposing synthesized brasses and an uptempo rhythm.

genres.name: Jilala Music
genres.description: Music of the Jilala Sufi order, most notably used in healing trance rituals.

genres.name: Jingles
genres.description: Short, melodic phrases, traditionally used in advertisements, and later in ringtones and video games.

genres.name: Jit
genres.description: Guitar-driven electric pop from Zimbabwe that draws influence from Central and East African rumba, South African jive and local music.

genres.name: Jiuta
genres.description: Originally created by solo performers singing and playing shamisen, but since the late 18th century increasingly often performed by sankyoku ensembles (shamisen, koto and shakuhachi or kokyu).

genres.name: Joik
genres.description: Traditional Sami singing style found in northern Finland, Sweden, Norway and Russia.

genres.name: Jongo
genres.description: Afro-Brazilian cultural manifestation involving music and dance; composed of percussion instruments and chants.

genres.name: Jook
genres.description: Fast-paced; draws influence from Bounce, Miami Bass, Jersey Club and Dancehall.

genres.name: Joropo
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Creole music and the Venezuelan waltz.

genres.name: Jovem Guarda
genres.description: 1960s Brazilian youth-oriented Pop Rock, with romantic lyrics and influenced by Merseybeat and Rockabilly.

genres.name: Jubilee
genres.description: Rooted in African-American culture, characterized by complex rhythms and call-and-response vocals.

genres.name: Jug Band
genres.description: Usually features a jug as the bass instrument as well as other homemade (or easily affordable) instruments, such as kazoos and washboards.

genres.name: Juke
genres.description: Faster than Ghetto House, playing at 160bpm, and makes striking use of unconventional drum patterns which differ wildly from other House styles.

genres.name: Jump Blues
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1930s with influence from Jazz styles such as Swing and Big Band, featuring fast tempos and raucous performances.

genres.name: Jump-Up
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1990s, characterized by loud "wobbling" basslines, simpler drum loops, and a light-hearted and warm sound.

genres.name: Jumpstyle
genres.description: Features a heavy 909 kick drum, four-on-the-floor beat, and a tempo between 140 and 150 BPM.

genres.name: Jungle
genres.description: Developed in the early 1990s from Breakbeat Hardcore, featuring rapid, chaotic-sounding breakbeats and strong basslines; known as the forerunner of most Drum and Bass styles.

genres.name: Jungle Dutch
genres.description: Combines the high-pitched synth leads of Dutch House with the frantic "tribal" rhythms of Jungle Terror.

genres.name: Jungle Terror
genres.description: Emerging mostly from Dutch House and Big Room House, incorporates Tribal House-influenced percussion, hard kicks, and animal sounds resulting in a wild, jungle-resembling atmosphere in a festival EDM-oriented context.

genres.name: Junkanoo
genres.description: Highly rhythmic Bahamian style which traditionally accompanies the arts festival and street parade of the same name.

genres.name: Jùjú
genres.description: Yoruba Music that emerged during the 1920s in urban settings across Nigeria, especially in Lagos.

genres.name: Jōruri
genres.description: Consists of a singing narrator (tayū) with shamisen accompaniment.

genres.name: K-Pop
genres.description: Contemporary style from South Korea, based on multiple mainstream influences such as Contemporary R&B, Dance-Pop, and Hip Hop.

genres.name: Kabarett
genres.description: Theatrical entertainment consisting of mixed elements of music, sketches, monologues, dialogues, lyric poetry and/or ballads.

genres.name: Kabye Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Kabye people of northern Togo, including some of the most singular styles that can be found in West Africa.

genres.name: Kabyle Music
genres.description: Music of the Kabyle Amazigh people.

genres.name: Kacapi suling
genres.description: Sundanese music played by an ensemble consisting of one or two kacapis (zithers), one suling (flute), and occasionally a set of kendangs (drums).

genres.name: Kadongo kamu
genres.description: Oldest form of mainstream music in Uganda, dating back to the early 1950s, translating to “one little guitar” from the Luganda language.

genres.name: Kafi
genres.description: Sufi vocal style popular in Pakistan, differentiated from Qawwali by its small ensemble size and simple arrangements.

genres.name: Kagura
genres.description: Performed at Shinto shrines for ceremonies and rituals.

genres.name: Kai
genres.description: Prevalent in the Altai-Sayan region and rooted in Shamanic traditions, it is renowned for its emphasis on the low vocal register and is revered as a sacred medium for communicating with all nature and the spirits.

genres.name: Kaiso
genres.description: Trinidadian folk considered to be the precursor of Calypso, led by "griot" storytellers who sing derogatory lyrics to the sound of drums and guitars in a call-and-response manner in order to rebel against slaveowners.

genres.name: Kakawin
genres.description: Form of Indonesian poetry written in Kawi, performed melodically using a structured pattern of long and short syllables.

genres.name: Kalattut
genres.description: Distinctive Folk tradition shaped by European cultural exchanges and indigenous Greenlandic heritage.

genres.name: Kalindula
genres.description: Features multiple rumba-like lead guitars and quick steady basslines, while mixing together elements of other percussion-heavy Zambian styles.

genres.name: Kalmyk Music
genres.description: Music of the Kalmyks, a Mongol Buddhist ethnic group inhabiting the Republic of Kalmykia, a federal subject of the Russian Federation.

genres.name: Kalon'ny fahiny
genres.description: Fusion of music from the highlands of Madagascar and western Operetta.

genres.name: Kaneka
genres.description: New Caledonian style of popular music that draws influence from traditional Melanesian music.

genres.name: Kannada Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Kannada people, a large ethnolinguistic group who mainly inhabit the state of Karnataka in southwestern India.

genres.name: Kansai No Wave
genres.description: Late '70s to early '80s scene from the Kansai region of Japan, sharing the brash oppositional, anti-music attitude of New York City No Wave.

genres.name: Kantan Chamorrita
genres.description: Improvised verse singing performed in the Chamorro language, traditional of the Marianas islands.

genres.name: Kanto
genres.description: Songs performed at the Tuluat Theaters of İstanbul in the late 19th century.

genres.name: Kantruem
genres.description: Form of fast-paced dance music played by the Khmer people of northeast Thailand.

genres.name: Kapuka
genres.description: Includes elements from Hip Hop and Reggae, as well as Kenyan traditions.

genres.name: Karachay-Balkarian Music
genres.description: Music of the Karachay and Balkar peoples of the Northwestern Caucasus, who reside in the republics of Karachay-Cherkessia and Kabardino-Balkaria.

genres.name: Karakalpak Traditional Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Karakalpak people, located in northwestern Uzbekistan.

genres.name: Karelian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Karelian people.

genres.name: Kaseko
genres.description: Surinamese popular music with roots in Surinamese Creole music, which was influenced by folk traditions of Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

genres.name: Kashubian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Kashubian people of northwestern Poland.

genres.name: Kawaii Future Bass
genres.description: "Cute" style of Future Bass rooted in anime and video game culture; emerged in Japan in the mid-2010s.

genres.name: Kawaii Metal
genres.description: Fuses various Metal substyles with J-Pop's upbeat melodicism and song structures, utilizing kawaii lyricism and an idol music aesthetic.

genres.name: Kayōkyoku
genres.description: Japanese popular music prominent during the later period of the Shōwa era (early 1950s to late 1980s).

genres.name: Kazakh Music
genres.description: Music of the Kazakhs.

genres.name: Kecak
genres.description: Balinese dance-drama and its associated musical style, with a choir performing a polyrhythmic style of vocal music somewhat similar in structure to Gamelan.

genres.name: Kef Music
genres.description: Dance-oriented Armenian American music with prominent presence of Anatolian instruments and folkloric melodies (often in the 10/8 meter) paired with novel lyrics relating to a variety of topics.

genres.name: Keroncong
genres.description: Early form of popular Indonesian Music from the 19th-20th century, inspired by Portuguese sailor songs brought to the archipelago during the colonial era.

genres.name: Kete
genres.description: Traditional percussive style played at special occasions in the courts of high ranking Asante chieftains.

genres.name: Ketuk tilu
genres.description: Traditional village dance and its accompanying music, which is played by a small gong-chime ensemble and accompanied by a Sundanese singer.

genres.name: Khakas Traditional Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Khakas Republic (part of the Russian Federation), a form of Turkic music related to the musics of neighboring Tuva, Altai and Mongolia.

genres.name: Khaliji Music
genres.description: Musical traditions of Eastern Arabia and the Persian Gulf region, roughly covering the Arabic-speaking people of the modern countries of the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Iraq, and Iran.

genres.name: Khayal
genres.description: Predominant vocal style, often with a significant amount of improvisation.

genres.name: Khmer Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Khmer people, who mainly reside in Cambodia.

genres.name: Khmer Music
genres.description: Music of the Khmer people, the majority ethnic group of Cambodia.

genres.name: Khoisan Folk Music
genres.description: Encompasses traditions of the Khoisan ethnic family groups.

genres.name: Khrueang sai
genres.description: Thai Classical Music emphasizing string instruments while also incorporating other kinds of instruments to enrich the sound.

genres.name: Kidandali
genres.description: Popular form of Ugandan music, originally derived from Kadongo kamu and Soukous.

genres.name: Kidumbak

genres.description: Earliest, most stripped-down form of Merengue.

genres.name: Merenhouse
genres.description: Popularized by Dominican-American artists of the 1990s, blending modern Merengue with electronic instrumentation and the combination of rapping/singing vocals.

genres.name: Merseybeat
genres.description: Light, highly melodic style of Beat popular in the UK during the early 1960s, named due to the abundance of bands from Liverpool beside the River Mersey.

genres.name: Mesoamerican Music
genres.description: Diverse styles and genres developed by the Indigenous peoples of Mesoamerica, a cultural region extending from central and southern Mexico through parts of Central America.

genres.name: Mesopotamian Music
genres.description: Music of Mesopotamia, a historical region situated in West Asia within the Tigris–Euphrates river system, comprises the heritage of Sumerians and Akkadians.

genres.name: Metal
genres.description: Driving and distorted riffs, aggressive drumming, vigorous vocals, and an all-around show of brute force in its early days, since branching into dozens of subgenres.

genres.name: Metalcore
genres.description: Drop-tuned guitar riffs, constant double kick drumming with varying tempos and techniques, breakdown sections, and screaming or shouting vocals.

genres.name: Mexican Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Mexican people.

genres.name: Mexican Music
genres.description: Music of Mexico and those deeply rooted in Mexican traditions.

genres.name: Meyxana
genres.description: Azerbaijani folk recitative genre.

genres.name: Miami Bass
genres.description: Sustained Roland TR-808 kick drums and faster tempos, along with a distinct Electro influence.

genres.name: Microfunk
genres.description: Minimal, glitchy, and "bleep"-y sound inspired by IDM.

genres.name: Microhouse
genres.description: Stripped-down, minimal form of House, originating in the late 90s, which takes influence from Minimal Techno, Glitch and IDM.

genres.name: Micromontage
genres.description: Arrangement of microsounds on an incredibly small time scale.

genres.name: Micronesian Music
genres.description: Music of the Micronesian peoples.

genres.name: Microtonal Classical
genres.description: Eschews the traditional twelve-tone scale of Western Classical Music, utilizing intervals outside of its bounds.

genres.name: Mid-School Hip Hop
genres.description: Based around heavy, stripped-down drum machine beats.

genres.name: MIDI Music
genres.description: Intended for real-time sequenced playback via MIDI protocol on MIDI devices and used primarily in 1990s PC Video Game Music, arranger keyboards and karaoke.

genres.name: Midtempo Bass
genres.description: Harsh synth leads and a usual tempo of around 90-110 BPM.

genres.name: Midwest Emo
genres.description: Characterized by shifts between loud and soft dynamics, off-key, strained and emotional vocals, sometimes with intricate instrumental arrangements and layered arpeggiated guitar parts.

genres.name: Miejski folk
genres.description: Alternative and Punk music influenced by Folklor miejski and Contemporary Folk.

genres.name: Milonga
genres.description: Characterized by a slow rhythm usually performed on a guitar; generally considered a precursor to Tango.

genres.name: Min'yō
genres.description: Form of Japanese Folk Music which literally translates to "folk song".

genres.name: Minangkabau Music
genres.description: Music of the Minangkabau people.

genres.name: Mincecore
genres.description: Raw and simplistic with heavy reliance on Punk structures while including political and socially aware themes.

genres.name: Minimal Drum and Bass
genres.description: Minimalist, sparse sound; emerged in two main 2000s strains, one Dubstep-inspired and one IDM-inspired, which crossed paths in the 2010s.

genres.name: Minimal Synth
genres.description: Minimal and distinctly DIY take on Synthpop with a bleak and naive aesthetic.

genres.name: Minimal Techno
genres.description: Stripped-down and sparse, often featuring a dark sound and a slow, steady development through the track.

genres.name: Minimal Wave
genres.description: Retrospective term for more Electronic and minimal forms of New Wave, Post-Punk, Synthpop, and related styles, tending towards a more sparse and lo-fi sound.

genres.name: Minimalism
genres.description: Developed in the United States in the 1960s; recognized for its repetitive nature and use of static harmony.

genres.name: Minneapolis Sound
genres.description: Emerged in late 1970s Minneapolis, characterized by glossy Contemporary R&B-influenced production techniques, angular New Wave-inspired rhythms, and a larger emphasis on electric guitar layers.

genres.name: Minstrelsy
genres.description: Popular song and entertainment tradition from the U.S. engendered in variety shows employing racist caricature and blackface.

genres.name: Minyue
genres.description: Modernized composition for Chinese instruments on the basis of Chinese Folk Music, incorporating aspects of Western Classical Music.

genres.name: Mittelalter-Metal
genres.description: Emerged as a metallic style in the mid-to-late 1990s from the German Neo-Medieval movement.

genres.name: Mittelalter-Rock
genres.description: Emerged in the 1990s from the German Neo-Medieval movement, incorporating medieval instruments with Rock music.

genres.name: Mobb Music
genres.description: San Francisco Bay Area production style building on slowed down Funk (often utilizing live elements).

genres.name: Mod
genres.description: 1960s youth subculture in the United Kingdom, drawing from British Rhythm & Blues, Beat, Garage Rock, and Pop sensibilities alongside a distinctive fashion style.

genres.name: Mod Revival
genres.description: Late 1970s and early 1980s revival of Mod fashion and music, featuring influence from the nascent Punk Rock scene.

genres.name: Moda de viola
genres.description: Style of Sertanejo de raiz predominant in southeast, south, and west-central Brazil.

genres.name: Modal Jazz
genres.description: Utilizes musical modes as harmonic framework over traditionally used chord progressions.

genres.name: Modern Classical
genres.description: Multitude of different compositional approaches beginning in the 20th century that deviate significantly from the previously-held tenets.

genres.name: Modern Creative
genres.description: Style of semi-improvisation that derives heavily from both the composition of Modern Classical and the techniques of Avant-Garde Jazz.

genres.name: Modern Laika
genres.description: Laiki music mixed with popular Western music, most notably pop and dance.

genres.name: Modinha
genres.description: Popular during the 18th and 19th centuries in Brazil; characterized by sentimental works with amorous themes, poetic lyrics, acoustic instrumentation and operatic vocals.

genres.name: Molam
genres.description: Native to Laos and the Isan region, wherein a singer is accompanied traditionally by a bamboo mouth organ called the khaen, nowadays mostly by larger ensembles.

genres.name: Molam sing
genres.description: Modernized form featuring a faster pace and mostly electric instrumentation.

genres.name: Mongolian Music
genres.description: Music of the Mongols.

genres.name: Mongolian Throat Singing
genres.description: Traditional music from Mongolia characterized by many throat singing techniques.

genres.name: Mono
genres.description: Employs Burmese melodies and modes of singing accompanied by Western instrumentation.

genres.name: Monodrama
genres.description: Mostly modern style written for a single virtuoso singer with accompaniment, often shorter in length and with a more philosophically introspective or abstract libretto.

genres.name: Montenegrin Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional folk music of Montenegro.

genres.name: Mood kayō
genres.description: Early form of Kayōkyoku dominant in the 1950s and 1960s, prominently influenced by American Jazz, Hispanic American Music, and Hawaiian Music.

genres.name: Moogsploitation
genres.description: Moog synthesizer-led music often associated with a wave of Novelty records in the 1960s and 1970s.

genres.name: Moombahcore
genres.description: High-pitched synth leads, gritty percussion, a kick-snare pattern, aggressive bass drops, and around 110 BPM while often paralleling Complextro or Brostep.

genres.name: Moombahton
genres.description: Offshoot of Dutch House characterized by tempos in the 100-110 BPM range, Reggaetón-influenced rhythms, bass-heavy kicks and high-pitched synths.

genres.name: Moorish Music
genres.description: Music of the Moors, the largest ethnic group in Mauritania.

genres.name: Moravian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Moravian people.

genres.name: Mordvin Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Mordvin people.

genres.name: Morenada
genres.description: Vibrant and culturally significant music originating in Bolivia and characterized by the sound of the matraca and a marked and rigid duple meter with a slow march-like tempo.

genres.name: Morna
genres.description: Slow tempo, monotonality, and the use of the violão, the Cape Verdean classical guitar, as the main instrumental accompaniment.

genres.name: Moroccan Chaabi
genres.description: Upbeat style of Moroccan popular music played in streets, cafés, weddings, and festivals.

genres.name: Moscow School
genres.description: School of Russian Western Classical Music composers centered on Moscow in the mid-to-late 19th century.

genres.name: Mossi Music
genres.description: Music of the Mossi people of Burkina Faso.

genres.name: Motet
genres.description: Extremely diverse form of vocal music, usually written as a style of Polyphonic Chant for A cappella soloists or choir.

genres.name: Motown Sound
genres.description: Succinct, catchy song structures; complex arrangements; Gospel-influenced vocals; highly melodic and rhythmic bass lines; 4-4 drum patterns; often syncopated piano parts; regular use of horn and string sections; and historically a distinctive reverb and treble-heavy production.

genres.name: Motswako
genres.description: Mainly rapped in a mixture of Setswana and English, incorporating additional languages and local South African and Botswanan influences, particularly Kwaito.

genres.name: Moutya
genres.description: Tradition that originated in Seychelles among Creole slaves, similar to Séga, although rawer and played only on large flat drums made from goatskin.

genres.name: Movida madrileña
genres.description: Countercultural scene developed in Madrid, Spain, in the late 1970s as a reflection of the newfound freedom after the end of the Franco’s dictatorship; mainly playing New Wave, Synthpop and Post-Punk.

genres.name: Mozambique
genres.description: Cuban genre featuring energetic, African-influenced percussion.

genres.name: MPB
genres.description: Short for música popular brasileira; formed in the mid-1960s as a modernized version of Bossa nova and Samba-canção.

genres.name: Muak
genres.description: Korean shamanistic music that accompanies the ritual of gut as performed in all regions of Korea.

genres.name: Mulatós
genres.description: Upbeat, danceable Hungarian Pop that takes strong influence from Hungarian Folk Music and Romani Folk Music.

genres.name: Muliza
genres.description: Mestizo folk genre popular in the central Peruvian Andes, characterized by a pronounced, though sedate, rhythm; traces of Andean melody; and octosyllabic verses.

genres.name: Murga
genres.description: Popular carnival music traditional in some cities of Spain and Hispanic America.

genres.name: Murga uruguaya
genres.description: Variant originated in Montevideo that stands out for its rhythms, nasal vocals and choral arrangements.

genres.name: Musette
genres.description: French popular music which arose in 1880s Paris, performed with the traditional instruments musette, grelottière, and accordion.

genres.name: Music Hall
genres.description: British theatrical entertainment popular in the 19th and 20th centuries, featuring light and comedic popular songs.

genres.name: Musical Comedy
genres.description: Heavily utilizes music in its delivery of humor.

genres.name: Musical Theatre and Entertainment
genres.description: Range of styles of theatre individually popular in the United States or in various countries in Europe, mostly from the 19th century to the mid-20th century.

genres.name: Musika popullore
genres.description: Tradition in Albania consisting of light, commercial, amplified Albanian Folk Music usually professionally arranged and manufactured in recording studios alongside video clips.

genres.name: Musique concrète
genres.description: Manipulation of recorded sounds, mostly Field Recordings, natural sounds, and real-world noises, as a process of abstracting "concrete" sounds, or "sound objects", from their acoustic origins.

genres.name: Musique concrète instrumentale
genres.description: Acoustic, through-composed Classical Music that relies heavily on unconventional instrumental techniques.

genres.name: Mutant Disco
genres.description: Danceable basslines, syncopated grooves, and angular guitar riffs, characterized by a spirit of experimentation and integration of disparate sounds.

genres.name: Muzică de mahala
genres.description: Appeared in the 1980s, incorporating modern instruments and based on the model of Balkan Pop-Folk in neighboring countries.

genres.name: Muzică lăutărească
genres.description: Strongly influenced by folk from Turkey, Russia, and Western Europe, and even by Byzantine Church music.

genres.name: Muzika mizrahit
genres.description: Middle Eastern-flavored Israeli popular music, usually performed by Mizrahi Jews, and combining aspects of the music of the North African, Middle Eastern, and Central Asian countries from which they descended.

genres.name: Muzika yehudit mekorit
genres.description: Rooted in traditional Jewish Music, especially Hasidic Music; incorporates modern influences, typically written on subjects of devotion and religion.

genres.name: Muzikat dika'on
genres.description: Depressing, somber lyrics and dramatic deliveries, more influenced by Turkish Music and Arabic Music in comparison to the lighthearted, playful, later varieties of Muzika mizrahit.

genres.name: Muziki wa dansi
genres.description: Popular in Tanzania with strong connections to Soukous and often associated with Jazz, whose name means "dance music" in Swahili.

genres.name: Mélodie
genres.description: French form typically with a greater emphasis on emotional restraint, refinement, subtlety, and concision.

genres.name: Méringue
genres.description: Haitian genre that dates back to the early 19th century; the roots of Compas.

genres.name: Métis Fiddling
genres.description: Canadian style blending First Nations and European musical influences into an up-tempo style of fiddling characterized by the use of syncopation and indigenous rhythms.

genres.name: Métis Music
genres.description: Music of the indigenous Métis people of Canada and the United States.

genres.name: Música cebolla
genres.description: Chilean offshoot of Canción melódica that expresses a much more melancholic or nostalgic side.

genres.name: Música criolla peruana
genres.description: Combination of African, Spanish, and Andean influences that originated after the time of the arrival of Spanish colonists and African slaves to Peru.

genres.name: Música de intervenção
genres.description: Wave of Portuguese singer-songwriters in the 1960s and 1970s who agitated against the Estado Novo regime and the colonial war waged by Portugal against national liberation fronts.

genres.name: Música gaúcha
genres.description: Popular music style of southern Brazil, based on the traditional Polka and other European rhythms.

genres.name: Música llanera
genres.description: Traditional music originating from the Llanos region of Colombia and Venezuela.

genres.name: Música típica chilena
genres.description: Incorporation of rural folklore music to urban fields, adding vocal groups accompanied mainly by guitar and a "huaso" symbolism.

genres.name: Māori Music
genres.description: Music of the indigenous Māori people of New Zealand.

genres.name: Młoda Polska
genres.description: Neoromantic composers attempting to create a new Polish national style.

genres.name: Mūsīqā lubnāniyya
genres.description: Lebanese pop genre that emerged post-independence as a nationalist tradition distinct from Egyptian and Levantine music, blending local influences with western orchestration, peaking in Lebanon's 1957–1975 golden age through radio, cinema, and stage.

genres.name: Nagauta
genres.description: Japanese Classical Music used in Kabuki, a form of theatre oriented to dance-drama.

genres.name: Nagoya kei
genres.description: Nagoya-based scene lasting though the 1990s and early 2000s; characterized by a simpler and gloomier visual presentation along with a darker, heavy sound inspired by Post-Punk, Gothic Rock and Heavy Metal.

genres.name: Nahua Music
genres.description: Musical traditions of the Nahuas, a major grouping of indigenous peoples inhabiting various regions in Mesoamerica, most notably Mexico.

genres.name: Nardcore
