genres.description: Hardcore Punk scene originating in Oxnard, California, in the early 1980s which often emphasizes speed, aggression, and technicality, and is heavily associated with the local southern California skateboarding culture and a D.I.Y. ethos.

genres.name: Narodno zabavna glasba
genres.description: Modernised form of Slovenian Folk Music from the Alpine region of Upper Carniola (Oberkrain).

genres.name: Nasheed
genres.description: Vocal songs popular throughout the Islamic world, mostly performed A cappella though sometimes featuring light instrumentation.

genres.name: Nashville Sound
genres.description: Production style characterized by smooth vocals over a relaxed ensemble of guitars and rhythm section, and variously incorporating elements from other styles of Country and Pop.

genres.name: Native American New Age
genres.description: Takes heavy influence from Indigenous North American Music, emphasizing a peaceful and harmonious atmosphere and utilizing chants, drumming, and flutes.

genres.name: Nature Recordings
genres.description: Recordings of natural phenomena such as waterfalls, ocean waves, and storms, as well as Animal Sounds.

genres.name: Naturjodel
genres.description: Originated in Toggenburg and Appenzell in Switzerland; deep vocal range, relaxed voice, free tempo, polyphony, elongated notes, improvisation, glissando, and use of syllabic sounds.

genres.name: Naxi Music
genres.description: Musical traditions of the Naxi peoples, fusing Chinese Music with local Naxi influences.

genres.name: Nederbeat
genres.description: Dutch answer to the British Beat boom of the 1960s.

genres.name: Nederpop
genres.description: Dutch language Pop which originally arose in the 1970s to describe the style of the 1950s and 1960s, but would also later be used for 1980s artists who incorporated elements of Ska and Reggae.

genres.name: Neo Kyma
genres.description: First appeared in the middle of the 1960s, rooted in Entechna, taking major inspiration from French Chanson.

genres.name: Neo-Acoustic
genres.description: Cross-section of Indie Pop and Jangle Pop with more prominent acoustic instrumentation and songwriting/arrangements that draw from Sophisti-Pop.

genres.name: Neo-Canterbury
genres.description: Movement reviving the signature style of the Canterbury Scene, often updating it with modern influences.

genres.name: Neo-City Pop
genres.description: 2010s style blending emerging genres like Acid Jazz and Neo-Soul with the Western-inspired Japanese Pop styles of the 1970s and 1980s.

genres.name: Neo-Grime
genres.description: Mixes Wave with Grime and other forms of UK Electronic music.

genres.name: Neo-Medieval Folk
genres.description: Emulates European Folk Music from the Middle Ages, originating in Germany in the 1980s.

genres.name: Neo-Pagan Folk
genres.description: Emulates music played by pagan people, particularly from pre-Christian Europe.

genres.name: Neo-Prog
genres.description: Emerged in the early 1980s in the United Kingdom from the influence of Symphonic Prog, utilizing a synth-driven sound that focuses on Pop-informed melodicism while de-emphasizing guitar riffing.

genres.name: Neo-Psychedelia
genres.description: Developments in Psychedelia since the early 1980s, building on the drug-inspired styles developed in the 1960s.

genres.name: Neo-Soul
genres.description: Emerged during the mid-to-late 1990s; defined by a combination of Soul with the rhythmic percussion and groove of Hip Hop.

genres.name: Neo-Traditionalist Country
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1980s as a reaction to the increased dominance of Country Pop, moving instead towards a Honky Tonk-rooted sound that centered the Singer-Songwriter.

genres.name: Neoclassical Darkwave
genres.description: Combines dark and melancholic atmosphere with Western Classical Music.

genres.name: Neoclassical Metal
genres.description: Greatly influenced by Western Classical Music in its style of playing and composing.

genres.name: Neoclassical New Age
genres.description: Strongly influenced by and sometimes also based upon early music and the Baroque Music or Classical Period.

genres.name: Neoclassicism
genres.description: Return to the more formal and less expansive structures and forms, beginning shortly after World War I as a reaction to what some composers perceived as excesses of Romanticism.

genres.name: Neocrust
genres.description: Melodic, dark, and atmospheric style that often incorporates influences from Sludge Metal, Post-Metal, Black Metal, and Screamo.

genres.name: Neofolk
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1980s from the Post-Industrial scene, with a dark, often martial atmosphere.

genres.name: Neofolklore
genres.description: Short-lived movement that reincorporated traditional Chilean folklore into modern production and styling inspired by foreign musicians.

genres.name: Neoperreo
genres.description: Heavy emphasis on rhythm, influence from global trends in club music, and generally progressive lyrics.

genres.name: Nerdcore Hip Hop
genres.description: Themes touch on such nerd mainstays as science, computers, and science fiction.

genres.name: Nerdcore Techno
genres.description: Stylistically diverse form of underground Japanese Electronic Dance Music utilizing energetic beats built around samples from pop and/or nerd culture.

genres.name: Nervous Music
genres.description: Dark, sinister and menacing sound, heavy sub-basses, simple melodies and slow, sparse and slamming drums.

genres.name: Neue Deutsche Härte
genres.description: Alternative Metal and Industrial Metal that incorporates various aspects of electronic music, specifically Electronic Dance Music.

genres.name: Neue Deutsche Todeskunst
genres.description: Dark themes inspired by German philosophy and poetry, typically combining Electronic instrumentation with neoclassical influences and an eccentric, theatrical style.

genres.name: Neue Deutsche Welle
genres.description: Eclectic German scene influenced by Synthpop and various styles of Punk, sometimes associated with Industrial.

genres.name: Neue Volksmusik
genres.description: Emerged in the Southern German region from  in the 1980s onwards as a reaction to the conservatism of Alpine Folk Music scenes, combining the genre with outside sources and paired with a strong sense of irony and progressive political views.

genres.name: Neurofunk
genres.description: Focuses on technical songwriting with warped, complex bass sounds, distorted and modulated synths (often with repeated stabs over the basslines), and dark but clean production.

genres.name: Neurohop
genres.description: Features the complex bass of Neurofunk and a frantic and mechanical sound design.

genres.name: New Age
genres.description: Broad genre centered on peaceful, meditative melodies, using a wide variety of instrumentation.

genres.name: New Age Kirtan
genres.description: American development of Kirtan, fusing it with New Age and Western music.

genres.name: New Beat
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1980s in Belgium; characterized by dark basslines, hard-hitting grooves and a slow tempo.

genres.name: New Brunswick Basement Scene
genres.description: Underground Punk Rock, Emo, and Indie Rock scene centred around Rutgers University in New Brunswick, New Jersey.

genres.name: New Complexity
genres.description: Dense, difficult, and rigorously academic approach to Modern Classical composition which emerged in the 1980s.

genres.name: New German School
genres.description: Mid-19th-century Romantic movement experimenting in harmonics and form and engaged in social issues.

genres.name: New Jack Swing
genres.description: Mixes light Hip Hop & Funk production techniques with Contemporary R&B vocals and melodies as well as swinging and danceable drum grooves.

genres.name: New Jazz
genres.description: Colorful, repetitive synths and synthetic instruments, playful vocal chops, and wonky bass selections set to bouncy Trap drums.

genres.name: New London Jazz
genres.description: Contemporary and eclectic Jazz scene based in London, UK, that pulls from a variety of styles, including Spiritual Jazz, Afro-Jazz, and Jazz Fusion, and is often influenced by other genres such as Electronic, Dub, and Hip Hop.

genres.name: New Mexico Music
genres.description: Derived from the Traditional Folk Music of New Mexico mixed with influences from Western, Country and Norteño, particularly associated with Spanish-speaking Nuevomexicanos.

genres.name: New Music
genres.description: Developed when Japanese Singer-Songwriters incorporated elements of Contemporary Folk and Pop Rock with Kayōkyoku songwriting.

genres.name: New Orleans Blues
genres.description: Diverse scene in New Orleans since the beginning of the 20th century, commonly associated with a sound led by rollicking pianos with syncopated beats and backed by horns.

genres.name: New Orleans Brass Band
genres.description: New Orleans' unique combination of European-styled military bands with African folklore.

genres.name: New Orleans R&B
genres.description: Increased rhythmic complexity with added focus on piano and horns.

genres.name: New Partisans
genres.description: Short-lived movement in the mid-to-late 1980s in Sarajevo which attempted to synthesise Pop Rock with elements of Yugoslav Folk music and the ideals of the 1940s Yugoslav partisan movement.

genres.name: New Pop
genres.description: British-centric movement of 1980s acts utilising Post-Punk ideals in a mainstream Pop context, characterised by cross-style experimentation and a strong focus on visual aesthetics.

genres.name: New Primitivism
genres.description: Cross-media movement in Sarajevo, active primarily in the 1980s and inspired by Yugoslav New Wave and Yugoslav Punk.

genres.name: New Rave
genres.description: High energy mid-2000s style combining the tight and punchy grooves of Dance-Punk Revival with synths and four-on-the-floor rhythms from genres like Electroclash and Electro House.

genres.name: New Romantic
genres.description: UK cultural movement associated with the early 1980s and defined by a distinct, flamboyant fashion sense.

genres.name: New Tone
genres.description: Musically and socio-politically progressive movement noted for combatting prejudices and mixing together different styles of music, such as Electronic, Hip Hop, or Emo.

genres.name: New Wave
genres.description: Broad term referring to a variety of styles that saw popularity in the wake of the Punk Rock explosion of 1976-77, initially strongly associated with more accessible and stylish offshoots of punk; developed alongside Post-Punk, similarly emphasising freshness and daring.

genres.name: New Wave of New Wave
genres.description: Short-lived British New Wave and Punk Rock revival scene, active primarily around 1993-94 before being pushed out by the mass popularity of Britpop; often derided as a media construct.

genres.name: New Way of Danish Fuck You
genres.description: Copenhagen underground scene active in the late 2000s and early 2010s, drawing on Post-Punk, Industrial, Noise, Hardcore Punk, and Black Metal and embracing a raw, lo-fi, cassette-based recording style and DIY ethos.

genres.name: New Weird America
genres.description: Diverse movement that originated in the Northeastern United States during the late 1990s and 2000s which reshaped mid-20th century Contemporary Folk influences through a psychedelic and avant-garde approach.

genres.name: New Weird Finland
genres.description: Rose to prominence in the early 2000s, based around a collective of musicians living primarily in the Finnish cities of Tampere, Turku and Helsinki and with a sound primarily rooted in Psychedelia, particularly Psychedelic Folk and its subgenres Free Folk and Freak Folk.

genres.name: New York Drill
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2010s, characterized by energetic, bouncy tresillo rhythms, creating a warmer, more booming tone than UK Drill, which prominently inspired it.

genres.name: New York Hardcore
genres.description: Hardcore Punk bands from New York City from the 1980s and onwards.

genres.name: New York School
genres.description: Circle of avant-garde composers based in 1950s New York, most well known for pioneering the use of chance as a method of composition.

genres.name: Newa Folk Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Newa people, who live in Nepal, performed with mostly percussive instruments and some wind instruments.

genres.name: Newfoundland Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province.

genres.name: Ngoma
genres.description: Played in Swahili-speaking African countries; primarily focused on rhythm.

genres.name: Nguni Folk Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Nguni ethnic family groups, a southern Bantu ethnicity.

genres.name: Ngâm thơ
genres.description: Vietnamese Poetry recitation backed by traditional instruments.

genres.name: Nhạc tiền chiến
genres.description: Popular music with romantic and poetic lyrics largely written between 1930s and 1940s.

genres.name: Nhạc vàng
genres.description: Made largely from the 1950s until the 1970s; introspective and sentimental lyrical themes.

genres.name: Nhạc đỏ
genres.description: Vietnamese revolutionary music, which may contain elements of Western Classical Music, Bolero Việt Nam, and Vietnamese Folk Music, and usually political and war-themed lyrics.

genres.name: Nightcore
genres.description: Based around the technique of speeding and pitching up pre-existing songs.

genres.name: Nigun
genres.description: Form of spiritual, repetitive and immersive tunes that developed in Hasidic Jewish communities, typically vocal-led.

genres.name: Nintendocore
genres.description: Fuses Post-Hardcore and Metalcore influences with Chiptune instrumentation.

genres.name: Nivkh Music
genres.description: Music of the Nivkh people inhabiting northern Sakhalin, the adjacent coast of the Russian Far East, and regions around the Amur River.

genres.name: No Melody
genres.description: Usage of minimalistic, repetitive midtempo drum patterns, and simple, prominent 808s.

genres.name: No Wave
genres.description: Underground, avant-garde, anti-art movement and music scene based in New York City around 1976-1980; commonly incorporates elements like dissonance, atonality, and stream-of-consciousness lyrics into various genres.

genres.name: Nocturne
genres.description: Intimate piece meant to evoke associations with the night.

genres.name: Noh
genres.description: Played by an hayashi ensemble, consisting of a fue (flute), a kotsuzumi (shoulder drum), a ōtsuzumi (hip drum), and a taiko (stick drum).

genres.name: Noiadance
genres.description: Blends Dutch House production with Funk brasileiro vocals and drumming on top of Moombahton rhythms.

genres.name: Noise
genres.description: Strays away from conventional structure, tonality, and composition and consists predominantly of noise.

genres.name: Noise Pop
genres.description: Arose in the mid-1980s; blend of poppier Rock songwriting and melodies with the dissonant, noisy timbres of distorted guitars and frequent use of guitar feedback.

genres.name: Noise Rock
genres.description: Explores dissonance and distortion through unconventional playing and guitar effects, commonly augmented by lo-fi production and bursts of feedback.

genres.name: Noisecore
genres.description: Short blasts of riff-less, Noise-driven music accompanied with chaotic drums and screamed vocals.

genres.name: Noisegrind
genres.description: Noise-driven, defined by its rawness, feedback usage, and very brief song structures.

genres.name: NOLA Sludge
genres.description: New Orleans–based Louisiana Metal scene, commonly cited as the birthplace of Sludge Metal.

genres.name: Nordic Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of Nordic countries of Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden.

genres.name: Nordic Folk Rock
genres.description: Fusion of Nordic Folk Music and Rock.

genres.name: Nordic Music
genres.description: Music from the Nordic countries, including Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, and Finland.

genres.name: Nordic Old Time Dance Music
genres.description: Meta-genre strongly related to Nordic Folk Music having less complex structures, easy rhythms, and melodic lines.

genres.name: Nortec
genres.description: Samples and synthesizes Mexican styles like Banda sinaloense and Norteño into a sound related to IDM and House.

genres.name: Norteño
genres.description: More traditional, rural version of Tejano Music whose name translates to "northern".

genres.name: North African Music
genres.description: Music of North Africa.

genres.name: North Asian Music
genres.description: Music of the indigenous peoples of Siberia, the Russian Far East, and outlying islands.

genres.name: Northeastern African Music
genres.description: Music of Northeastern Africa.

genres.name: Northeastern Brazilian Music
genres.description: Regional styles that combines elements of indigenous, African and European traditions, historically with a focus on life of the northeastern people, such as drought, migration, the struggle for survival, love and nostalgia, and often danced in intense and accelerated movements.

genres.name: Northern American Music
genres.description: Regional styles with roots in Northern America (America north of Mexico, including Canada, United States, Greenland, Saint-Pierre and Miquelon, and Bermuda), typically drawing from European Folk Music and Classical Music as well as West African Music and Indigenous American Music influences.

genres.name: Northern Brazilian Music
genres.description: Regional styles rooted in Northern Brazil, often influenced by Caribbean rhythms and instrumentations, usually with focus on romance, celebrations, the relationship between the man and the Amazon rainforest, and danced in fast and sensual movements.

genres.name: Northern Gothic
genres.description: Modern recontexualisation of Gothic music, influenced by the regional politics, culture and geography of post-industrial 21st-century Northern England.

genres.name: Northern Soul
genres.description: Soul popular in northern England in the late 1960s and early 1970s, consisting primarily of lesser-known American artists in the mid-1960s copying the Motown Sound.

genres.name: Northumbrian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional folk of Northumbria, a region of Northern England consisting of Northumberland and County Durham.

genres.name: Norwegian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Norway, primarily intended as accompaniment for dancing and coming in two main varieties, instrumental and vocal music.

genres.name: Nouveau zydeco
genres.description: Adds new elements into contemporary Zydeco, most importantly the incorporation of Funk, Contemporary R&B and Hip Hop characteristics.

genres.name: Nouvelle chanson française
genres.description: Both a subgenre of Chanson and a specific scene from the 1990s incorporating alternative trends from this period and new and unusual ways within Chanson tradition.

genres.name: Nova cançó
genres.description: Arose in Catalonia during the Franco dictatorship, sung in Catalan as a way to resist restrictions placed on regional languages in Spain and retain a regional identity.

genres.name: Nova srpska scena
genres.description: Serbian Alternative Rock scene subject to media interest in the '00s and early '10s; influenced by the Yugoslav New Wave and contemporary Indie Rock.

genres.name: Nova vanguarda paulistana
genres.description: Southeastern Brazilian scene that emerged in the late 2000s based on experimentation with Samba and MPB styles.

genres.name: Novaya scena
genres.description: Diverse Ukrainian avant-garde scene which emerged in the late 1980s.

genres.name: Novelty Piano
genres.description: Popular in the 1920s; originated in Chicago and took influence from Jazz.

genres.name: Novo Dub
genres.description: Alternative Electronic scene incorporating various influences, predominant in France.

genres.name: NRG
genres.description: Derived from UK Hard House; featuring darker, more anthemic Trance beats and a tempo of 155-165 BPM.

genres.name: Nu Jazz
genres.description: Electronic styles which feature aesthetics and occasionally instrumentation inspired by Jazz.

genres.name: Nu Metal
genres.description: Emphasizes bouncy, drop-tuned riffs, alternating vocal styles, and genre-bending, often incorporating Hip Hop and Funk Metal elements.

genres.name: Nu Skool Breaks
genres.description: Developed in the late 1990s and early 2000s; takes elements from Drum and Bass, UK Garage, and Techno.

genres.name: Nu Style Gabber
genres.description: Emerged near the end of the 1990s; deeper, more harmonic bassdrums with constant use of supersaw melodies, breakdown sections and slower tempos closer to the 150-180 BPM range.

genres.name: Nu-Disco
genres.description: 21st-century trend mixing modern, polished Electronic production with the aesthetics, structures, and lively, organic beats of 1970s and 1980s Disco.

genres.name: Nuban
genres.description: Traditional Afro-Emirati Folk performance of Nuban origin most commonly performed in the emirate of Dubai.

genres.name: Nubian Music
genres.description: Music of Nubia, a region centered along the Nile River in northern Sudan and southern Egypt.

genres.name: Nuer Music
genres.description: Music of the Nuer people of Eastern South Sudan and Western Ethiopia.

genres.name: Nueva canción
genres.description: Latin American (Nueva canción latinoamericana) and Spanish (Nueva canción española) movement during the 1960s and 1970s.

genres.name: Nueva canción chilena
genres.description: Socially conscious style that sought to recover traditional Chilean folk music and fuse it with the broader musical trends of Latin America.

genres.name: Nueva canción española
genres.description: Arose in Spain in the 1960s, inspired in part by Nova cançó's reclaiming of Catalan regional identity, that spread across the country in regional variations.

genres.name: Nueva canción latinoamericana
genres.description: Politically-charged messages associated with the rise of leftist social movements; striving for a renewal of traditional Latin and Hispanic American Folk Music expressions.

genres.name: Nueva cumbia chilena
genres.description: Rock-infused instrumentation, incorporating an eclectic repertoire of influences, such as Ska, Salsa, Indigenous Andean Music, Reggae, and Bolero.

genres.name: Nueva ola
genres.description: Latin American movement in the late 1950s and the 1960s incorporating assorted styles of Western popular music, primarily Rock & Roll and Pop.

genres.name: Nueva trova
genres.description: Found inspiration in the 1950s Cuban Revolution and had the intention of introducing new musical ideas to the original Trova.

genres.name: Nuevo Cancionero
genres.description: Musical-literary movement in Argentina that aimed to reevaluate and reinvigorate "la música popular nativa" (native popular music) and to be the voice of poor and marginalized Argentines.

genres.name: Nursery Rhymes
genres.description: Short, mostly traditional children's songs or poems with simple melodies, rhythms and words.

genres.name: Nustyle
genres.description: Developed out of Early Hardstyle from the mid-to-late 2000s, by incorporating distorted, crunchy, pitched kicks, faster tempo around 150 BPM, and detuned supersaw/square synth leads playing stompy, dramatic melodies.

genres.name: NWOBHM
genres.description: Acronym for new wave of British Heavy Metal, which occurred in the late 1970s, taking some influence from Punk Rock.

genres.name: Nyahbinghi
genres.description: Performed at Rastafari religious ceremonies, consisting of tripartite hand-drumming and often accompanied by vocal chants.

genres.name: Nòva cançon
genres.description: Arose in the Occitania region of southern France, sung in the Occitan language as a way to preserve their culture and resist forced usage of French.

genres.name: Ob-Ugric Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Ob-Ugric people of West Siberia Plain.

genres.name: Oberek
genres.description: Fastest triple-time national dance of Poland.

genres.name: Occitan Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional music of Occitania, sung mainly in Occitan and sometimes in French.

genres.name: Occult Rock
genres.description: Dark and psychedelic atmosphere with lyrical references to esoteric subjects such as occultism, Satanism, fantasy, and horror; closely associated sonically and culturally with Heavy Metal and its offshoots.

genres.name: Oceanian Music
genres.description: Rooted in the traditions of the geographic region of Oceania.

genres.name: Odia Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Odia, a large ethnic group who mainly inhabit the state of Odisha in eastern India.

genres.name: Odissi Classical Music
genres.description: Traditional dance and classical music from the Odisha region of Eastern India.

genres.name: Ogene Music
genres.description: Traditional acoustic music performed by Igbo groups in southeastern Nigeria centered on call-and-response vocals alongside instrumentation from iron bells, wooden whistles, and jug drums.

genres.name: Oi!
genres.description: Rejection of perceived intellectualism and elitism in Post-Punk and Art Punk, characterized by a return to a straightforward, melodic Punk Rock sound, sing-along choruses, and a lyrical focus on working class youth culture.

genres.name: Okinawan Music
genres.description: Music of the Okinawa Islands in Japan.

genres.name: Old Roman Chant
genres.description: Plainchant tradition of Medieval Rome that was closely related to Gregorian Chant, though often more musically ornate.

genres.name: Old-Time
genres.description: Pre-Bluegrass North American string band styles, particularly those rooted in Appalachian Folk Music.

genres.name: Omutibo
genres.description: Mid-20th century Kenyan popular music which centres around a fingerpicked acoustic guitar.

genres.name: Onda nueva
genres.description: Based on Joropo, it incorporates elements of Bossa nova and Jazz.

genres.name: Ondō
genres.description: Originally referred to the type of call-and-response form of Gagaku, but later became to be known for and distinguished by a swung 2/2 rhythm and storytelling.

genres.name: Onkyo
genres.description: Exploration of the physical traits of sound rather than music as expression.

genres.name: Opera
genres.description: European tradition which combines drama and distinctive vocal style in the context of Western Classical Music, usually performed as a theatrical work on stage.

genres.name: Opera buffa
genres.description: Lighthearted and amusing counterpart to Opera seria; developed in Naples in the first half of the 18th century.

genres.name: Opera semiseria
genres.description: Popular in the early and middle 19th century, containing appeals to emotion of Opera seria as well as some comedy elements present in Opera buffa.

genres.name: Opera seria
genres.description: Italian Opera popular among European nobility and royalty throughout most of the 18th century, typified by its exaggerated dramatic flair and interspersed with dry recitative.

genres.name: Operetta
genres.description: Light opera interspersed with spoken dialogues, being usually satirical and/or humorous in nature and centered around romantic plots and dancing scenes.

genres.name: OPM
genres.description: Filipino ballads prominent in the 1970s to early 1980s, combining the sentimentality, lush arrangements and vocal techniques of Kundiman with the instrumentations and rhythms of Manila Sound and Soft Rock.

genres.name: Opéra-ballet
genres.description: Principally French style of musical drama that combines operatic singing with classical dance, usually with small Orchestral Music accompaniment.

genres.name: Opéra-comique
genres.description: French style of Opera characterized by the use of some spoken dialogues to connect major arias and sung parts, as well as a more restrained approach to recitatives.

genres.name: Oratorio
genres.description: Composition for vocal soloists, choir, and orchestra, often making use of a comprehensive textbook of contemplative nature.

genres.name: Orchestral Music
genres.description: Western Classical Music performed by an orchestra.

genres.name: Orchestral Song
genres.description: Classical song for solo voice or voices with orchestral accompaniment.

genres.name: Organic House
genres.description: Subtle drums and grooves, slow tempos, and acoustic, traditional instrumentation, resulting in an organic, warm sound and spiritual atmosphere.

genres.name: Ori deck
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Moombahton and Dubstep to create a style characterized by sluggish, kick-heavy dembow rhythms.

genres.name: Oriental Ballad
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1990s in South Korea, taking influence from more traditional forms of Korean Music.

genres.name: Oriental Jewish Music
genres.description: Comprises the many traditions and styles of the various groups of Jews from the cultural East, loosely covering the Jewish groups of the Middle East, North Africa, and Central Asia.

genres.name: Orkes gambus
genres.description: Indonesian songs based on Arabic hits, adapted for a small ensemble featuring the gambus lute, percussion, and electric instruments.

genres.name: Oromo Music
genres.description: Music of the Oromo people, a Cushitic ethnolinguistic group, who primarily live in the Oromia region of Ethiopia and Northern Kenya.

genres.name: Orthodox Pop
genres.description: Combines Orthodox Jewish themes and prayer with Pop songwriting, usually sung in Hebrew.

genres.name: Ossetian Folk Music
genres.description: Folk music of Ossetians, an ethnic group that mainly inhabits a region located on both sides of the Greater Caucasus Mountains.

genres.name: OtoMAD
genres.description: Music-driven remixes that take heavy inspiration from Japanese internet culture.

genres.name: Ottoman Military Music
genres.description: Considered the oldest military marching band in the world; instruments used are cymbals, trumpet, kös drum, kettle drum, naqareh, bells, and cevgen.

genres.name: Outlaw Country
genres.description: Rock-influenced reaction to mainstream Country Pop trends, featuring rebellious personas, darker lyrics, and Western-inspired outlaw imagery.

genres.name: Outsider House
genres.description: Mostly derived from Deep House; intentional use of rough, lo-fi production, often utilizing a mix of analog/analog-like and digital instrumentation.

genres.name: Overture
genres.description: Typically single-movement form akin to the Tone Poem written as the prelude to a larger work or in association with a programmatic concept.

genres.name: P-Funk
genres.description: Features a "fat", monotonic drum sound, spaced-out synthesizers, "squelchy" basslines, tight, syncopated horns, and sometimes heavy guitars.

genres.name: P-Pop
genres.description: Commercialized style from the Philippines, which served as the successor of Manila Sound and OPM, featuring various contemporary Western influences and primarily sung in Tagalog and English.

genres.name: Pachanga
genres.description: Combination of Merengue, Conga, Rumba cubana, and Cumbia; fast, festive, and playful.

genres.name: Pacific Reggae
genres.description: Developed in Pacific island communities, incorporating elements from local Oceanian Music styles.

genres.name: Pagan Black Metal
genres.description: Incorporates acoustic guitar and traditional instrument passages, cleanly sung vocals, folk songs' melodies, and paganistic themes.

genres.name: Paghjella
genres.description: Traditional Polyphonic Chant from Corsica consisting of three registers of vocalists singing in a semicircle.

genres.name: Pagode
genres.description: Used for Samba groups whose music was performed in the suburban Cariocas parties, with romantic lyrical content and improvisation.

genres.name: Paisley Underground
genres.description: Emerged in Los Angeles in the early 1980s, featuring the energy of Power Pop and New Wave adorned with retro Psychedelia.

genres.name: Pakacaping Music
genres.description: Traditional genres of music found among the ethnicities of Indonesian archipelago, particularly on South Sulawesi, Borneo and North Sumatra.

genres.name: Palingsound
genres.description: Originating from Volendam in the Netherlands; harmonizing vocals and orchestrated arrangements.

genres.name: Palm Desert Scene
genres.description: Originated during the 1990s in Palm Desert, California, based in classic Hard Rock, Psychedelic Rock and the Alternative Rock sounds of the era.

genres.name: Palm Wine Music
genres.description: Fusion of the African Folk Music of the region with imported Caribbean Calypso.

genres.name: Palo de mayo
genres.description: Upbeat music accompanying maypole dancing from the Caribbean coast of Central America.

genres.name: Pamiri Music
genres.description: Music of the Pamiri people native to the Badakhshan region in the Pamir Mountains.

genres.name: Pansori
genres.description: Korean style of storytelling characterized by over-the-top, passionate singing from a solo vocalist accompanied by minimal drumming.

genres.name: Pansy Craze
genres.description: Period of popularity and visibility of LGBT+ and drag performers in US cities from the late 1920s to mid-1930s.

genres.name: Papuan Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Papuan people of New Guinea.

genres.name: Parang
genres.description: Latin-Caribbean genre central to Trinidad and Tobago and Venezuela traditionally used for nighttime celebrations in Trinidadian towns.

genres.name: Parlour Music
genres.description: Early form of light, sentimental popular music; popular in USA and Europe from the late 1700s to the 1870s.

genres.name: Partido alto
genres.description: Originating from the early roots of Samba primarily in Rio de Janeiro in the beginning of the 20th century, initially as a more danceable style with little or no vocals.

genres.name: Pashto Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Pashtun people of southern Afghanistan and north-western Pakistan.

genres.name: Pasillo
genres.description: Traditional dance popular in Ecuador and Colombia; based on European Waltz and often performed with guitar and mandolin.

genres.name: Pasodoble
genres.description: Mainly instrumental Spanish style primarily associated with bullfighting and popular celebrations, believed to originate from a double-time military march from France in the 18th century.

genres.name: Passion
genres.description: Musical re-enactment of the suffering and crucifixion of Christ, typically based on one of the four canonical Gospels.

genres.name: Payada
genres.description: Improvised poetry accompanied by a guitar that is tied to gaucho culture, usually performed in duo as a verse duel.

genres.name: Peak Time Techno
genres.description: Hard, dynamic, energetic and accessible subgenre featuring strong kicks, massive dirty synths, tempos around 130 BPM, more suspenseful structures with breaks and build-ups, and big, modern, festival-oriented sound; rose to high popularity in the late 2010s.

genres.name: Pep Band
genres.description: Performs at athletic events, and typically performs modified versions of Pop songs.

genres.name: Persian Classical Music
genres.description: Traditional art music of the Persian civilization.

genres.name: Persian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Persian people.

genres.name: Persian Music
genres.description: Music of the Persian people.

genres.name: Persian Pop
genres.description: Hybrid of Iranian and Persian-language popular music with Western instruments such as the guitar, drum kit, and synthesizer.

genres.name: Peruvian Music
genres.description: Music developed by the Peruvian people.

genres.name: Philippine Music
genres.description: Music of the Philippines.

genres.name: Philippine Rondalla
genres.description: Ensemble of plucked string instruments typically performed for traditional Filipino folk dances; known for its distinct sparkling and tinkling tremolo sound.

genres.name: Philly Club
genres.description: Builds on Baltimore Club with a faster tempo and sometimes influences from more modern genres like Trap [EDM].

genres.name: Philly Club Rap
genres.description: Mixes the fast and energetic production of Philly Club with similarly frantic and fast rapping.

genres.name: Philly Drill
genres.description: Apocalyptic and haunting choirs, keys, and strings with gruesome narratives and slow, sparse drums.

genres.name: Philly Soul
genres.description: Defined by lush arrangements, often borrowing upon the orchestral instrumentation seen on productions from the 1960s, with the commercial atmosphere exemplified by Pop Soul and the Motown Sound.

genres.name: Phleng phuea chiwit
genres.description: Political Thai Folk Rock born out of the 1973 student uprising, with a name translating to "songs for life".

genres.name: Phonk
genres.description: Modernized, eclectic take on classic Memphis Rap production, featuring various influences from other Hip Hop genres, especially drum programming inspired by other Southern Hip Hop as well as frequent jazzy, funky elements somewhat akin to West Coast Hip Hop and from Electronic music.

genres.name: Phonk House
genres.description: Merges Drift Phonk's nocturnal atmospheres, cowbell melodies, vocal samples, and energetic production, with House rhythms and tempos, characterized by a banging and upbeat sound.

genres.name: Piano Blues
genres.description: Features the piano as a lead instrument performed solo or with a small ensemble, ranging from mid-tempo ballads to fast-paced dance styles.

genres.name: Piano Rock
genres.description: Primarily based around piano riffs and melodies, rather than having guitar as the focal instrument.

genres.name: Picopop
genres.description: Originated in the early 2000s as an offshoot of the Japanese Shibuya-kei movement when artists introduced more prominent "bleepy" electronic elements and faster tempos.

genres.name: Piedmont Blues
genres.description: Developed in the early 20th century in the southern Appalachian foothills and characterized by a syncopated but melodic Ragtime-based finger-picking acoustic guitar style.

genres.name: Pigfuck
genres.description: Sloppy, abrasive and feedback-laden riffing with vulgar and edgy lyricism, informed by Post-Hardcore's aggression and Post-Punk's rhythm section.

genres.name: Pilón
genres.description: Featuring rhythms described as mimicking those created while pounding sugarcane with African baton-like tools.

genres.name: Pimba
genres.description: Humorous lyrics and a basic harmonic structure.

genres.name: Pinoy Folk Rock
genres.description: Typically sung in Tagalog and pioneered in the 1970s, incorporating elements of indigenous music such as Kulintang gong music and the kubing bamboo jaw harp.

genres.name: Pinpeat
genres.description: Orchestra of wind and percussion instruments having its origins in the Khmer Empire era.

genres.name: Pipe Band
genres.description: Tradition originating in the Scottish military; standard instruments consist of 6-25 sets of Great Highland bagpipes, 3-10 military snare drums, 1-6 Scottish tenor drums, and one bass drum.

genres.name: Piphat
genres.description: Led by wind and percussion instruments, with ensembles ranging from 6 to 10 instruments.

genres.name: Pirekua
genres.description: Traditional style of the P’urhépecha people, typically slow and in 3/8 or 6/8 time.

genres.name: Piyyut
genres.description: Liturgical Jewish poems that are chanted or recited during religious occasions such as daily prayers and holidays.

genres.name: Plainsong
genres.description: Monophonic chanting in the context of Roman Catholic and modern Anglican liturgy.

genres.name: Plena
genres.description: Folk genre from Puerto Rico played with hand drums called panderetas.

genres.name: Plugg
genres.description: Use of sparse and compact drum and hi-hat patterns, subby 808s and heavy low end; commonly features piano samples, airy pads, and icy synths.

genres.name: PluggnB
genres.description: Emphasizes more melodic and layered synth leads, denser and faster drum programming, and a lesser reliance on the laid-back, minimalistic atmosphere of earlier Plugg styles.

genres.name: Plunderphonics
genres.description: Compositional technique of utilizing and manipulating one or more recognizable recordings to create a new composition.

genres.name: Poetry
genres.description: Encompasses many forms of literature that use style and rhythm to evoke ideas and emotions further than the prosaic meaning of the literature itself.

genres.name: Poezja śpiewana
genres.description: Polish sung poetry; the poem is the centerpiece of a song, often with sparse instrumental accompaniment.

genres.name: Polish Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Poles.

genres.name: Polish Goral Music
genres.description: Music of indigenous highlanders native to the Western Beskids and the Podhale regions in Southern Poland.

genres.name: Polish Music
genres.description: Music rooted in the traditions of the Poles.

genres.name: Political Hip Hop
genres.description: Features explicitly political lyrics and themes.

genres.name: Polka
genres.description: Lively style and corresponding dance originating in Central and Eastern Europe, featuring a 2/4 cut time beat and instruments which vary by region.

genres.name: Polka paraguaya
genres.description: Popular music originating in Paraguay and the Province of Corrientes (Argentina), derived from the Bohemian polka and traditional music of Hispanic-Jesuit origin.

genres.name: Polka peruana
genres.description: Peruvian adaptation of European Polka, blending Afro-Peruvian rhythms and criollo melodies.

genres.name: Polonaise
genres.description: Stately national dance with music in triple meter and moderate tempo.

genres.name: Polynesian Music
genres.description: Music of Polynesia.

genres.name: Polyphonic Chant
genres.description: Chanting that combines two or more melodic lines that are harmonically cohesive but differ in rhythm and utilize non-parallel motion.

genres.name: Pon-chak disco
genres.description: Heavily influenced by Electro-Disco, featuring cheap "electronic organ" synth leads and minimalistic, repetitive rhythms.

genres.name: Ponto de umbanda
genres.description: Afro-Brazilian religious ritualistic praise sung by priests to evoke entities; typically accompanied by claps and traditional drums known as atabaque.

genres.name: Pop
genres.description: Umbrella of popular styles closely tied to mass production and mass marketing, focusing on catchiness and accessibility through melody, rhythm, lyrics, and hooks.

genres.name: Pop Batak
genres.description: Combines Western genres of music and instrumentation with a typical Batak flair, like lyrics about Batak life and the use of some traditional Batak instruments.

genres.name: Pop Ghazal
genres.description: Employs traditional Ghazal's verse, meter, and poetic inclinations in a pop form.

genres.name: Pop Kreatif
genres.description: Scene from Indonesia made popular in the 1970s-80s; commonly features lush melodies and progressive arrangements borrowed from modern styles of Jazz, Pop Rock and R&B.

genres.name: Pop Minang
genres.description: Combines Minangkabau traditions with Pop structures and instrumentation.

genres.name: Pop Punk
genres.description: Blends the loud, fast-paced sound of Punk Rock with the melodic hooks of Pop.

genres.name: Pop Rap
genres.description: Fuses Hip Hop's rapping and production traits with Pop elements such as melodious vocals and light, catchy tunes.

genres.name: Pop Raï
genres.description: Fuses melodic sensibilities into the traditional Raï structure, with increased utilization of synthesizers, guitars, and drum machines.

genres.name: Pop Reggae
genres.description: Light, commercial form of Reggae designed to crossover and break through to a more mainstream Pop audience.

genres.name: Pop Rock
genres.description: Fuses conventional verse-chorus song structure and especially melodic songwriting with usage of guitars, drums, and propulsive rhythms.

genres.name: Pop Soul
genres.description: Fusion of Pop and Soul; originated in the 1960s as an attempt to give soul crossover success.

genres.name: Pop Sunda
genres.description: Mixes Sundanese traditions with Pop structures and instrumentation.

genres.name: Pop Yeh-Yeh
genres.description: Blends Western Beat and Psychedelia styles with asli singing and melodies drawn from Malay Folk Music.

genres.name: Pops Orchestra
genres.description: Orchestra that plays covers of popular songs as well as famous classical compositions.

genres.name: Porn Groove
genres.description: Primarily found in the soundtracks to Pornographic films of the 1970s; characterized by a wah-wah electric guitar sound, slapped basslines, and minimal drums.

genres.name: Pornogrind
genres.description: Groovy, mid-tempo style known for its exaggerated bouncy rhythm and common pornographic themes.

genres.name: Porro
genres.description: Lively Hispanic American Music and dance style native to Colombia which gained popularity in the 1940s.

genres.name: Portuguese Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music from Portugal.

genres.name: Portuguese Music
genres.description: Music of Portugal.

genres.name: Positive Punk
genres.description: Early goth scene in London that grew out of the Anarcho-Punk movement and promoted themes of virtue and mysticism; commonly features wailing vocals, screeching guitars, prominent basslines, and eclectic drum patterns.

genres.name: Post-Bop
genres.description: Grew out of Hard Bop in the early to mid-1960s incorporating certain untraditional elements inspired largely in part from Avant-Garde Jazz, Modal Jazz and eventually, Free Jazz, such as non-diatonic chord progressions, irregular rhythms and amelodic forms.

genres.name: Post-Britpop
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1990s as a Britpop expansion mainly characterized by acoustic-leaning instrumentation, lush string arrangements, and mid-tempo song structures, as well as less apparent lyrical concerns for Britain in favor of introspective, contemplative themes.

genres.name: Post-Dubstep
genres.description: Minimalistic, atmospheric sound design and eclectic drum patterns, derived from but not fitting Dubstep.

genres.name: Post-Grunge
genres.description: Streamlined derivative of Grunge mixing crunchy guitar riffs with more accessible, hook-based structures.

genres.name: Post-Hardcore
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1980s from Hardcore Punk that expanded on its aggression and dynamics through longer and more complex arrangements.

genres.name: Post-Industrial
genres.description: Umbrella group of genres that combine the dark, mechanical aesthetic of early Industrial music with more accessible genres, such as Rock and Electronic Dance Music.

genres.name: Post-Metal
genres.description: Atmospheric and dense metallic riffs, unconventional songwriting, sonic experimentation, and adoption of eclectic influences.

genres.name: Post-Minimalism
genres.description: Seeks to push Minimalism's linear composition style forward, and takes in influences from genres such as Jazz, Traditional Folk Music, and others.

genres.name: Post-Punk
genres.description: Emerged alongside the initial Punk Rock explosion in the mid-to-late 1970s, putting a greater emphasis on experimentation and atmosphere.

genres.name: Post-Punk Revival
genres.description: Incorporating the sounds and aesthetics of Post-Punk into Indie Rock, with jagged guitarwork, a dominant and danceable rhythm section, clean production, and poppy song structures.

genres.name: Post-Rock
genres.description: Emphasis on timbre, texture, and atmosphere over traditional conventions while often embracing influences from genres not usually associated with Rock.

genres.name: Power Electronics
genres.description: Waves of feedback, screeching analog synthesizers, and harsh, screamed vocals.

genres.name: Power Metal
genres.description: Developed from Heavy Metal and Speed Metal, emphasizing speed, vocal melody and harmonized lead guitars.

genres.name: Power Noise
genres.description: Combines looped samples of Noise with Electronic rhythms.

genres.name: Power Pop
genres.description: Combines 1960s Pop melodies with loud power chords; characterized by prominent, sometimes jangly electric guitars, clear vocals, crisp harmonies, and economical arrangements.

genres.name: Power Soca
genres.description: Often at a tempo of 160 BPM and incorporating hard, frantic rhythms, highly synthesized production, and call-and-response vocals.

genres.name: Powerstomp
genres.description: Prominent, "stomping", and slightly distorted kick, relentless, repetitive reverse basses on the offbeats (borrowed from Hardstyle) that drive the tracks, giving the genre its distinct energetic sound, and cacophonous, noisy riffs and synth leads.

genres.name: Powerviolence
genres.description: Originated from the West Coast California Hardcore Punk scene in the late 1980s, utilizing strong elements of Noise Rock and abrupt tempo changes.

genres.name: Powwow Music
genres.description: Drum-based traditional music of Plains region Native American tribes, traditionally played at Pow-wows.

genres.name: Praise & Worship
genres.description: Christian music with lyrics focused on the greatness of God.

genres.name: Praise Break
genres.description: High-energy, improvisational "break" for worshiping God in Black churches.

genres.name: Prank Calls
genres.description: Practical jokes performed over the telephone, typically involving a comedian putting on a persona to make the individual on the other end of the line seem foolish.

genres.name: Prehistoric Music
genres.description: Styles from the first cultural periods of the human species (Homo sapiens, as well as certain Homo neanderthalensis). From its birth in the Paleolithic and Neolithic eras to the Ancient Music era beginning around 2000–3000 BC.

genres.name: Prelude
genres.description: Brief work with an improvisatory feeling, usually for keyboard, that serves either as a standalone piece or an introduction to a complimentary work of music.

genres.name: Process Music
genres.description: Compositions centering musical processes, both audible and inaudible.

genres.name: Progg
genres.description: Swedish movement centred around left-wing politics; emerged in the late 1960s and declined by the late 1970s due to internal divisions and the changing political climate.

genres.name: Progressive Big Band
genres.description: Introduces Western Classical Music compositional techniques into Big Band.

genres.name: Progressive Bluegrass
genres.description: Modernization with varied influences including Jazz, Folk, Rock, and other forms of Country.

genres.name: Progressive Breaks
genres.description: Derivative of Progressive House that incorporates its lush, melodic synth leads and atmospheres into Breakbeat's syncopated and broken rhythms.

genres.name: Progressive Country
genres.description: Blend of traditionalist Country styles with elements of Rock, Contemporary Folk, and other countercultural genres; characterized by realistic, self-reflective lyrics and non-traditional songwriting and production elements.

genres.name: Progressive Electronic
genres.description: Synthesizer-driven genre focusing on developing, often longform compositions and drawing inspiration from various sources such as Progressive Rock, Western Classical Music, and Ambient.

genres.name: Progressive Folk
genres.description: Draws from a variety of sources to subvert traditional acoustic song forms, with diversity ranging from Jazz to Medieval music to various Regional Music traditions.

genres.name: Progressive House
genres.description: Trance-influenced strain of House that grew to prominence in the early 1990s, using polished production and gradual progressions.

genres.name: Progressive Metal
genres.description: Fuses amplified, guitar-driven sound with technical proficiency, virtuosity, complex compositions, innovative arrangements, eclecticism, and additional instrumentation.

genres.name: Progressive Pop
genres.description: Milder counterpart to Progressive Rock, emerging in the late 1960s and introducing complex songwriting and arrangements into a Pop context.

genres.name: Progressive Psytrance
genres.description: Emerged in the early 2000s, featuring a slow tempo range and clean production.

genres.name: Progressive Rock
genres.description: Complex harmonies, instrumental virtuosity, and usually multi-section song structures featuring a broad range of instrumentation.

genres.name: Progressive Soul
genres.description: Greater harmonic complexity, less conventional song structures, and conceptual, socially conscious or introspective lyrical themes, incorporating diverse influences and instrumentation from Jazz, Funk, Rock, and beyond.

genres.name: Progressive Trance
genres.description: Combination of Trance and Progressive House which emerged in Western Europe in the early to mid-1990s.

genres.name: Proto-Punk
genres.description: Used to describe what influenced or in some way resembled Punk Rock before that genre's commercial breakthrough in 1976.

genres.name: Psichedelia occulta italiana
genres.description: Psychedelic scene from Italy with a distinctly brooding, dark atmosphere indebted to the country's media and a warped approach to Italian cultural memory.

genres.name: Psybient
genres.description: Heavy influence from Psytrance and Goa Trance incorporated in an atmospheric Ambient context.

genres.name: Psybreaks
genres.description: Uses Psytrance-derived sound design, such as squelchy sounds and psychedelic effects.

genres.name: Psychedelia
genres.description: Umbrella of styles intended to replicate or enhance the altered state of consciousness brought on by the use of psychedelic drugs, originating in the 1960s.

genres.name: Psychedelic Folk
genres.description: Acoustic forms that capture an atmosphere that is at turns dream-like, 'spaced-out', whimsical, haunting, mystical, and melancholic.

genres.name: Psychedelic Pop
genres.description: Combines unconventional instrumentation with studio effects to create a psychedelic atmosphere within melodic Pop music.

genres.name: Psychedelic Rock
genres.description: Rock which emerged in the mid-1960s that often attempts to emulate or enhance the effects of psychedelic drugs.

genres.name: Psychedelic Soul
genres.description: Soul which incorporates the effects and instrumentation of Psychedelic Rock.

genres.name: Psychobilly
genres.description: Cross-pollination of Punk Rock and Rockabilly.

genres.name: Psychsploitation
genres.description: Short-lived genre seeking to capitalise on the popularity of Psychedelia in the 1960s, featuring quickly and cheaply recorded material played by session musicians and put out by budget labels.

genres.name: Psystyle
genres.description: Prominent Psytrance influences, especially the basslines and energy of mainstream psytrance.

genres.name: Psytrance
genres.description: Emphasizes a psychedelic feel and an energetic sound; based around influences from Goa Trance and Acid Trance.

genres.name: Pub Rock
genres.description: Stripped-down style developed in the United Kingdom in the early to mid-1970s, mainly as a reaction to the perceived excess and pretension of Progressive Rock and Glam Rock.

genres.name: Pueblo Music
genres.description: Rooted in the traditions of the Pueblo peoples, who are indigenous to the southwest United States.

genres.name: Pungmul
genres.description: Consists of drumming, dancing, and singing, and is a tradition deeply ingrained in South Korean culture.

genres.name: Punjabi Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Punjabi people, mostly from the Punjab regions of India and Pakistan, covering diverse styles often played with traditional instruments.

genres.name: Punk
genres.description: Musical and cultural product of Punk Rock known for its simplistic, brash playstyle and anti-establishment themes.

genres.name: Punk Blues
genres.description: Fusion of the instrumentation and scales of Blues Rock with Punk.

genres.name: Punk Poetry
genres.description: Fast and rhythmic vocal delivery of political or satirical themes; frequently backed by Post-Punk or Minimal Wave instrumentation.

genres.name: Punk Rock
genres.description: Fast tempos, loud and distorted riffs, simple songs, frequent use of power chords, and shouted vocals, originating in the mid-1970s in response to commercial, sentimental, and complex Rock.

genres.name: Punta
genres.description: Garifuna Music with influences from other Caribbean genres such as Reggae, Soca, and Zouk, as well as Hispanic American Music.

genres.name: Purple Sound
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2000s out of the Dubstep scene of the time, incorporating synth leads and basslines inspired by 1980s Synth Funk and 1990s G-Funk, and Video Game Music, into a rhythmic palette mostly derived from dubstep and Grime.

genres.name: Purísima
genres.description: Nicaraguan Hymns to the Immaculate Conception of Mary, sung during holiday celebrations and in liturgical or parochial services.

genres.name: Puxa
genres.description: Energetic dance style that combines solid bass lines with subtle melodies and harmonies of São Toméan music.

genres.name: Pásztordal
genres.description: Sung by men who guard livestock, reflecting on their occupation and social position.

genres.name: Pìobaireachd
genres.description: Art tradition which originated in the Scottish Highlands, usually associated with the Great Highland bagpipes.

genres.name: Q-Pop
genres.description: Glamorous, catchy pop scene that emerged in Kazakhstan in the 2010s, inspired by K-Pop.

genres.name: Qaraami
genres.description: Dates back to the 1940s and carries regional features such as the use of a pentatonic scale and having the oud as the primary instrument.

genres.name: Qasidah modern
genres.description: Islamic pop that emerged on the Indonesian island of Java during the 1970s, updating a form of classic Arabic Poetry known as "qasidah".

genres.name: Qawwali
genres.description: Sufi Music in India and Pakistan using the raga and tala templates of Hindustani Classical Music.

genres.name: Quan họ
genres.description: Tradition of the Northern Vietnamese provinces of Bắc Ninh and Bắc Giang, originally consisting of harmonic, a cappella singing from two competing duos.

genres.name: Queercore
genres.description: Movement mainly distinguished by its lyrical content expressing the viewpoints of the LGBTQ+ community, as well as promoting queer pride and unity.

genres.name: Quyi
genres.description: Category of traditional Chinese storytelling, featuring a narrative structure and a combination of speaking and singing.

genres.name: R&B
genres.description: Umbrella of styles covering the most popular forms of Black American music from the late 1940s, when the term Rhythm & Blues first appeared; includes the developments of Soul and Funk in the '60s and '70s, and the Contemporary R&B of the 1980s onward.

genres.name: Rabiz
genres.description: Elements of Armenian folk in its instrumentation, oftentimes incorporating influences from Arabic and other West Asian forms on a background of synthesizer arrangements.

genres.name: RABM
genres.description: Leftist movement related to Crust Punk that variably espouses Marxist, environmentalist, and anarchist views.

genres.name: Rabòday
genres.description: Fast-paced rhythm inspired by Rara, with Electronic instrumentation and humorous sexual and political lyrics.

genres.name: Radio Broadcast Recordings
genres.description: Recordings of transmissions sent by radio waves, used for sending communications to a wide audience.

genres.name: Radio Drama
genres.description: Narrative storytelling performed by voice actors and produced for radio broadcasting or published on audio media such as tapes or CDs.

genres.name: Raga Rock
genres.description: Influenced by South Asian Music, featuring a droning compositional quality and commonly incorporating instruments like sitar, tambura, and tablas.

genres.name: Rage
genres.description: Dense, buzzing synth work with repetitive chord progressions and melodic synth leads.

genres.name: Ragga
genres.description: Hardcore style with a deejay (equivalent to an MC in Hip Hop) rapping over predominantly Electronic rhythms.

genres.name: Ragga Jungle
genres.description: Developed in the early 1990s in London, combining Jungle breakbeats with heavy influence from Ragga.

genres.name: Raggacore
genres.description: Prominently incorporates samples from Ragga and Dancehall, typically through shouted vocal lines and Reggae-influenced instrumentals.

genres.name: Raggatek
genres.description: Influenced by Reggae, Ragga and Dancehall, combining half-time instrumental sections with Hardtek's fast four-on-the-floor rhythms, as well as vocal samples, clean basslines and skank rhythms.

genres.name: Ragtime
genres.description: Emerged in the 1890s; piano-led and characterized by a heavily syncopated rhythm.

genres.name: Ragtime Song
genres.description: Incorporates syncopated, "ragged" rhythms into popular song forms.

genres.name: Rain Sounds
genres.description: Naturally occurring sounds of rainfall.

genres.name: Rajasthani Folk Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Rajasthani people of Western India - who now mostly live in the eponymous Rajasthan state - originated across the various castes that inhabit the region.

genres.name: Ranchera
genres.description: Originating in rural Mexico in the 19th century and popularized in the 1930s; emphasizes passionate and emotional performances and love-focused lyrics, often performed with a Mariachi ensemble.

genres.name: Rap Metal
genres.description: Features rapped vocals, typically formed around heavy, mid-tempo, and groove-oriented playing in addition to elements of Hip Hop beats such as record scratching.

genres.name: Rap Rock
genres.description: Fusion of Hip Hop and Rock, often featuring the former’s rhythmic vocal delivery and the latter’s heavy, distorted instrumentation.

genres.name: Rapai dabõih
genres.description: Religious music meant to accompany the dabõih ceremony of the Acehnese people.

genres.name: Rapso
genres.description: Fusion of Soca and Hip Hop unique to Trinidad and Tobago.

genres.name: Raqs baladi
genres.description: Egyptian folk dance and its associated musical accompaniment, appearing in the 20th century.

genres.name: Rara
genres.description: Derived from the Haitian Vodou Drumming tradition, often played at street festivals and carnivals and usually having celebratory or political lyrics.

genres.name: Rare Phonk
genres.description: Primarily features eclectic sampling and lush, jazzy beats, usually set to Trap rhythms with prominent influences of Memphis Rap.

genres.name: Rasin
genres.description: Blends the highly rhythmic drumming of traditional Haitian Vodou music with Rock-influenced electric instrumentation such as guitar, keyboard, and bass.

genres.name: Rasqueado
genres.description: Regional dance and its accompanying music from the Brazilian midwest, predominantly the state of Mato Grosso.

genres.name: Rasteirinha
genres.description: Slow-paced, highly rhythmic with instrumentation derived from Samba and Axé, and Dancehall-inspired grooves.

genres.name: Ratchet
genres.description: Club-oriented style defined by a repeated synth melody and a sparse drum pattern often accompanied by a "hey" chant.

genres.name: Rautalanka
genres.description: Nordic guitar style mainly influenced by Rock & Roll, and traditional European Schlager.

genres.name: Rawstyle
genres.description: Incorporates earlier Hardstyle and Hardcore [EDM] influences into the sound of 2010s hardstyle, creating a distinctly harsh, simplistic, raw, and dark sound, with fast BPM.

genres.name: Raï
genres.description: Originated in Algeria in the 1920s as a form of Bedouin Music, blending influences from various rural and urban genres.

genres.name: Red Dirt
genres.description: Oklahoman and Texan acts descended from the Stillwater, Oklahoma independent Country scene of the 1980s.

genres.name: Red Disco
genres.description: Continuum of various eclectic forms, derived mainly from late Euro-Disco, but also Italo-Disco, Hi-NRG and Eurobeat, and developed in the Soviet Union in the mid-to-late 1980s.

genres.name: Reductionism
genres.description: Experimental music that centers around quiet dynamics and use of silence.

genres.name: Regalia
genres.description: Lush, sweeping string arrangements, dreamy piano passages, and other orchestral instrumentation set to cinematic Trap percussion.

genres.name: Reggae
genres.description: Developed in the 1960s; shuffling "bubble" and offbeat rhythms played on an organ, and staccato guitar and piano chords known as "skank."

genres.name: Reggae / Ska / Dancehall
genres.description: Umbrella for related forms of Jamaican Music which have grown beyond their regional roots to become global phenomena.

genres.name: Reggae Rock
genres.description: Incorporates the offbeat rhythms and staccato "skank" guitar of Reggae.

genres.name: Reggaetón
genres.description: Rooted in Dancehall and mainly characterized by its heavy emphasis on the "dembow" rhythm; developed in Puerto Rico in the early 1990s under heavy influence from Hip Hop.

genres.name: Regional Music
genres.description: Music of regional cultural traditions, that is or was predominantly played and produced in these regions.

genres.name: Rembetika
genres.description: Greek tradition originating in traditional Mikrasiatiki and Smyrnaiki music with elements of other local traditional Greek genres.

genres.name: Renaissance Music
genres.description: Encompasses Western Classical Music from the 15th to 16th centuries.

genres.name: Reparto
genres.description: Incorporating Cuban Music elements, resulting in dynamic rhythms and a sound palette that typically features  Salsa-like guitar picking.

genres.name: Repente
genres.description: Contest of fully improvised poetry sung in different stanza formats.

genres.name: Requiem
genres.description: Musical setting commemorating the deceased with text usually derived from the Roman Catholic mass of the dead.

genres.name: Revolution Summer
genres.description: Collection of bands coalesced around the goal of rejuvenating the Washington DC Hardcore Punk scene in the summer of 1985, creating the early foundations for Post-Hardcore and Emo in the process.

genres.name: Revue
genres.description: French Musical Theatre and Entertainment based on numbers and sketches inspired by the most relevant events of the year.

genres.name: Rhumba
genres.description: Commercial adaptation of various Latin American genres; developed during the 1930s as the so-called "rhumba craze" unfolded in the United States.

genres.name: Rhythm & Blues
genres.description: Predominantly African American style that retains the defined backbeats, Blues chord progressions/melodies and passionate singing/shouting of Jump Blues, while appealing more to an urban audience with smaller bands and reduced Jazz influence.

genres.name: Ricercar
genres.description: Early instrumental genre, usually for solo lute or keyboard, written either as a brief introductory work or imitative contrapuntal piece.

genres.name: Riddim
genres.description: Repetitive and relatively simplistic style inspired by mid-to-late-2000s UK Dubstep, often using robotic and/or squishy sound design along with bouncy square basses and less prominent buildups.

genres.name: Rigsar
genres.description: Dominant form of popular music in Bhutan which broke traditions to move towards a more Western and Indian approach.

genres.name: Ring Shout
genres.description: Ritual practiced by African-Americans in the US South, characterized by shouting, chanting and people dancing in a circle while praying and clapping.

genres.name: Rioplatense Music
genres.description: Music developed by the people of the Rio de la Plata region.

genres.name: Riot Grrrl
genres.description: Underground feminist Punk movement originating in the United States in the early 1990s.

genres.name: Ripsaw
genres.description: Indigenous style of the Turks and Caicos Islands, featuring a handsaw as the primary instrument.

genres.name: Ritmada
genres.description: Short, repetitive and resonant beats with more danceable, immersive grooves drawn out of Afro-Brazilian instrumentation, a cleaner, more radio-friendly sound and greater focus on lyrics.

genres.name: Ritual Ambient
genres.description: Dark, disturbing, ritualistic, and occult atmosphere, often taking inspiration from various existing ritual practices around the world.

genres.name: RKT
genres.description: Emerged in the early 2010s, characterized by minimalistic, rhythm-centric production heavily influenced by Cumbia villera and other Cumbia argentina styles.

genres.name: Road Rap
genres.description: Emerged in the mid 2000s from Brixton and Peckham featuring abrasive tones, prominent Grime influence, and lyrics depicting circumstances of street gang violence in the UK.

genres.name: Rock
genres.description: Typically uses a verse-chorus structure with a backbeat rhythm and the electric guitar at the forefront; generally heavier and/or faster than its predecessors.

genres.name: Rock & Roll
genres.description: Developed in the United States and popularized in the 1950s, featuring prominent Blues scales, poppy structures, and strong rhythms.

genres.name: Rock andaluz
genres.description: Emerged during the mid-1970s in Spain; primarily utilizes Flamenco and often Symphonic Prog elements.

genres.name: Rock andino
genres.description: Emerged in the Andean countries in the late 1960s and early 1970s, incorporating traditional instruments and harmonies from Indigenous Andean Music within a Rock format.

genres.name: Rock barrial
genres.description: Argentinian scene that started in the 1990s, inspired by Rock & Roll, Blues Rock, Roots Rock, and sometimes Hard Rock, directed to a national public and dismissing modern international trends, often featuring lyrics describing the life in low-income neighbourhoods.

genres.name: Rock in Opposition
genres.description: Short-lived, international movement of ‘uncommercial’ Progressive Rock bands with left-wing politics; began its activity in early 1978 and faded out by the end of 1980, with 'reunion' festivals taking place from 2007 onwards.

genres.name: Rock Musical
genres.description: Style of musical theatre inspired by Rock.

genres.name: Rock Opera
genres.description: Hybrid of rock and, sometimes, musical theatre stylings with heavily rock-tinged songs combining to tell a coherent story.

genres.name: Rock radical vasco
genres.description: Punk music movement developed around 1983 by Basque Country and Navarre bands with a crude and abrasive sound and a 'radical' stance against the system, religion, the police and the 'Spanish State'.

genres.name: Rock rural
genres.description: Brazilian Folk Rock that emerged in the 1970s, incorporating elements of Sertanejo, Country Rock, and MPB.

genres.name: Rock subterráneo
genres.description: Peruvian artistic and countercultural movement that emerged after the return to democracy in 1980, diversifying into various Punk styles between 1983 and 1992.

genres.name: Rock sónico
genres.description: Argentinian scene emerging in the early 1990s, influenced by Shoegaze, Noise Pop, Neo-Psychedelia, and sometimes Downtempo or Slacker Rock, defined by noisy, reverb-soaked guitars, introspective lyrics and lo-fi production.

genres.name: Rock urbano español
genres.description: Spanish scene originating in the mid-to-late 1970s that gained dominance with the end of the Francoist dictatorship and the end of censorship around lyrical topics like social issues.

genres.name: Rock urbano mexicano
genres.description: Scene born in the mid-to-late 1980s mainly in the marginal areas of Mexico City that took elements from Blues Rock, Hard Rock and Folk Rock.

genres.name: Rockabilly
genres.description: Blends the sound of Country with that of Rhythm & Blues, often accompanied by driving guitars, frantic vocals, and slap-back echo in the bass.

genres.name: Rocksteady
genres.description: Jamaican popular music that blossomed briefly between 1966 and 1968 as an evolution of Ska, being slower, more relaxed, and soulful.

genres.name: Rom kbach
genres.description: Cambodian pop with a slow melody that is similar to Luk thung.

genres.name: Roman School
genres.description: Composers of primarily Christian Liturgical Music active in Rome in the 16th and 17th centuries, developing a musically conservative compositional style seen as appropriate for church performance.

genres.name: Romance
genres.description: Form of narrative sung Poetry rooted in medieval Spanish oral tradition, characterized by octosyllabic verses and assonant rhyme. Evolving from epic Medieval Lyric Poetry, and later spread across Hispanic America.

genres.name: Romani Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Romani people, an ethnic group with origins in Northern India, but who have since the Middle Ages settled around Europe, principally Romania, Bulgaria, and Spain, and many other places.

genres.name: Romanian Etno Music
genres.description: Romanian style which emerged in the early 1990s as a revival of Romanian Folk Music, blending traditional music with dance-pop rhythms.

genres.name: Romanian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Romanians.

genres.name: Romanian Music
genres.description: Music of the Romanian people.

genres.name: Romanian Popcorn
genres.description: Emerged in the second half of the 2000s in Romania, often featuring brass melodies and "staccato" pluck grooves.

genres.name: Romantic Style
genres.description: Melodic and sentimental style characterized by emotive vocals and mellow sound with a less explicit tone, emphasizing romantic love themes, blending Contemporary R&B, Latin Pop and romantic ballad influences, popularized during early 2000s to 2010s.

genres.name: Romanticism
genres.description: Expressive and emotional qualities, especially in terms of melody.

genres.name: Romantische Oper
genres.description: Early 19th century Germanic style of Opera influenced by German Folk Music and legends with a focus on fantasy, emotivity, heroic figures, and nationalism.

genres.name: Romanţe
genres.description: Expressive and poetic Romanian style, generally sung similar to a Chanson and composed for piano and guitar orchestral arrangements.

genres.name: Rominimal
genres.description: Hypnotic, minimal, and "dubby" loops, featuring subtle and intricate synth pads, cranky, clicky percussion, and bouncy, pulsing basslines.

genres.name: Roots Reggae
genres.description: Primarily defined through the political, spiritual, and socially conscious messages of its lyrics.

genres.name: Roots Rock
genres.description: Consciously and predominantly incorporates elements of its predecessors and original roots such as Country, Blues, Rhythm & Blues, Rock & Roll, and American Folk Music, but also many other American traditions.

genres.name: Rumba catalana
genres.description: Cheerful Catalan genre that takes influences from Rumba cubana, Andalusian Rumba flamenca, and Pop.

genres.name: Rumba cubana
genres.description: Folkloric manifestation of Afro-Cuban music that encompasses dance, voice, and drums.

genres.name: Rumba flamenca
genres.description: Flamenco subgenre, derived from the exchange of influences between Spain and Latin America.

genres.name: Rune Singing
genres.description: Traditional vocal music of Baltic-Finnic peoples characterized by singing poems, performed solo or in groups.

genres.name: Russemusikk
genres.description: Norwegian music crafted for the country's graduate celebrations known as russefeiring, typically features melodic, danceable, energetic production, and party-oriented, explicit singing and rapping.

genres.name: Russian Chanson
genres.description: Divided into lyrical and criminal chanson, it is best described as narrative-driven popular music inspired by crime and prison.

genres.name: Russian Folk Music
genres.description: Eastern Slavic Folk Music native to the Russian people.

genres.name: Russian Music
genres.description: Music of the Russian people.

genres.name: Russian Orthodox Liturgical Music
genres.description: Tradition of the Russian Orthodox Church, implemented with the Christianization of Kievan Rus' in 988.

genres.name: Russian Romance
genres.description: Popular Russian genre of melancholy balladry.

genres.name: Ryukyuan Music
genres.description: Music of the Ryukyuan people of the Ryukyu Islands in the southwest of Japan.

genres.name: Ryūkōka
genres.description: Uses elements of Western Classical Music, and adopts the legato style of singing.

genres.name: Rōkyoku
genres.description: Storytelling usually accompanied by a shamisen.

genres.name: Sa'idi
genres.description: Traditional folkloric performance and form of Arabic Folk Music originating from Upper Egypt.

genres.name: Sacred Harp Singing
genres.description: Predominantly 19th-century English hymns with tunes derived from old folk melodies.

genres.name: Sacred Singing Circle
genres.description: Phenomenon that originally began in hippie gatherings, notably beginning with the counter-culture Rainbow Gatherings of the 1970s, features loose musical jams with varied and spontaneous performances.

genres.name: Sacred Steel
genres.description: Focused on instrumentals and played on the steel guitar.

genres.name: Sahrawi Music
genres.description: Music of the Sahrawi people, an ethnic group who inhabit the westernmost areas of the Sahara Desert.

genres.name: Saint Petersburg School
genres.description: Interrelated circles of 19th century Russian Western Classical Music composers focused on developing a distinctly Russian national style.

genres.name: Sakha Traditional Music
genres.description: Traditional music of Sakha (a.k.a. Yakut) people, mostly living in their homeland - Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) (part of Russian Federation).

genres.name: Salegy
genres.description: Features rich, harmonized vocals and chiming guitar lines.

genres.name: Salsa
genres.description: Often incorporating congas, timbales and bongos as well as smaller instruments, such as maracas, clave and güiro.

genres.name: Salsa choke
genres.description: Colombian style that takes heavy influence from Reggaetón, House, Hip Hop, and various Afro-Colombian and Colombian Pacific styles.

genres.name: Salsa dura
genres.description: Earlier form of Salsa, usually less rigid in structure allowing for extended jam sessions; lyrical themes revolve around the "barrio" way of life and Latin American traditions.

genres.name: Salsa romántica
genres.description: Salsa following a stronger influence from Pop, typically sharing shorter, conventional structures and romantic lyricism.

genres.name: Saluang klasik
genres.description: Played by a duo or a trio of musicians, including a saluang (a kind of end-blown bamboo flute) player and a traditional singer.

genres.name: Samba
genres.description: Originated in the 19th century from a blend of various rhythmic styles of African Music, forming a new sound, structure, and a dance of the same name.

genres.name: Samba de breque
genres.description: Development of Samba-choro characterized by sudden pauses in its syncopated rhythms.

genres.name: Samba de gafieira
genres.description: Emerged in the 1930s, with the influence of Choro, Maxixe, Lundu, and Big Band from the the United States.

genres.name: Samba de roda
