genres.description: Mixed Portuguese culture with African slave traditions, as well as sharing roots and similarities with Batuque and Jongo.

genres.name: Samba de terreiro
genres.description: Urban Samba from the samba schools of Rio de Janeiro, with short songs about everyday topics and love.

genres.name: Samba-canção
genres.description: Romantic, commercial form of Samba that was popular in Brazil between the 1930s and the 1950s.

genres.name: Samba-choro
genres.description: Emerged in the 1930s as the result of a fusion of rhythmic elements and combining Samba with Choro.

genres.name: Samba-enredo
genres.description: Developed in the 1930s in Brazilian samba schools (escola de samba) to be presented and performed at carnivals.

genres.name: Samba-exaltação
genres.description: Developed in the early forties, with lyrics mainly exalting the culture of Brazil.

genres.name: Samba-jazz
genres.description: Jazz genre from Brazil that incorporates Samba and/or Bossa nova elements.

genres.name: Samba-joia
genres.description: Emerged in the 1970s, featuring a strong influence from Bolero along with overly romantic lyrics.

genres.name: Samba-rock
genres.description: Blends Samba with influences from American genres such as Rock, Jazz and Soul.

genres.name: Sambalanço
genres.description: Popular genre in Brazil during the 1950s and 1960s, with influence of Samba and Jazz.

genres.name: Sambass
genres.description: Combines Drum and Bass tempos and drum patterns, in addition to its Funk and Soul influences, with various styles of Brazilian Music.

genres.name: Samoan Music
genres.description: Music of the Samoan people.

genres.name: Samoyedic Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Samoyedic peoples.

genres.name: Sample Drill
genres.description: Prominent, recognizable samples set to tresillo-styled Drill hi-hats and counter snares.

genres.name: Samri
genres.description: Traditional dance from Najd, Saudi Arabia, performed by two opposing rows of men who face each other, dancing and moving to the rhythm, in addition to a percussion ensemble.

genres.name: San Diego Sound
genres.description: Artistically diverse Punk and indie scene based around San Diego in the 1990s.

genres.name: San Francisco Sound
genres.description: Influential Psychedelic Rock scene that developed out of Folk Rock in the mid 1960s; often emphasized atypical chord progressions and instrumental improvisation in the form of roving basslines and “cross-talking” guitars.

genres.name: Sanjo
genres.description: Traditional instrumental Korean Folk Music that focuses on a wide variety of rhythmic changes with many different classical Korean instruments.

genres.name: Santería Music
genres.description: Afro-Cuban genre played in religious rituals, combining traditions from both the Cuban and the Yorùbá people.

genres.name: Santé engagé
genres.description: Emerged in Mauritius in the 1970s, blending the popular Séga style with outside influences.

genres.name: Sarala gee
genres.description: Blend of Hindustani Classical Music with Sinhalese Folk Music.

genres.name: Sardana
genres.description: Traditional dance dating from the 16th century performed by large ensembles called 'Cobla' and danced by people holding hands in a circle.

genres.name: Sardinian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Sardinia, an island in the Mediterranean Sea.

genres.name: Sarum Chant
genres.description: Latin Plainsong tradition of Salisbury, England, characterized by its unadorned simplicity.

genres.name: Sass
genres.description: Emerged from Post-Hardcore in the early 2000s; characterized by sassy vocal styles and chaotic, erratic instrumentals.

genres.name: Sasscore
genres.description: Emerged from Post-Hardcore in the early 2000s; characterized by sassy vocal styles and chaotic, erratic instrumentals.

genres.name: Sawt
genres.description: Poetic vocal form with complex rhythms, emotive singing, and distinctive lute-backed melodies commonly found in the Gulf region and based on a maqam system.

genres.name: Saya
genres.description: Fast-paced, percussive traditional genre created by the Afro-Bolivian people.

genres.name: Scam Rap
genres.description: Lyrics that focus on various forms of fraudulent activities.

genres.name: Scene
genres.description: Youth subculture popularized in the 2000s via MySpace, spanning Metalcore, Pop Punk, Post-Hardcore, and related genres; associated with androgynous hairstyles, mall-sourced fashion, the Warped Tour festival circuit, and varied crossover with Electronic music.

genres.name: Schlager
genres.description: Light, sentimental, melodic pop music common mainly in northern and central Europe.

genres.name: Schranz
genres.description: Characterised by fast tempos, aggressive "whooshing" beat patterns, heavy compression and straightforward song structures.

genres.name: Scots Song
genres.description: Traditional folk songs usually sung in Lowland Scots, often but not always unaccompanied.

genres.name: Scottish Country Dance Music
genres.description: Strict-tempo style played by Scottish country dance bands, led by an accordion or a fiddle and featuring piano, drums and sometimes double bass.

genres.name: Scottish Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Scottish people.

genres.name: Scottish Folk Revival
genres.description: Revival of Scottish Folk Music which began around 1950 in Scotland and stagnated in the early 1970s.

genres.name: Scouse House
genres.description: Features an upbeat and energetic sound often described as being "bouncy", influenced somewhat by Happy Hardcore.

genres.name: Screamo
genres.description: Intense, aggressive and complex approach to Emo featuring higher levels of abrasiveness and dissonance, accompanied by guitar-focused melodicism and harsh vocals.

genres.name: Scrumpy and Western
genres.description: Usually humorous music originating from England's West Country, heavily featuring traditional English folk instruments and often sung in the West Country accent.

genres.name: Sea Shanty
genres.description: Songs originally sung by sailors to coordinate work on ships.

genres.name: Seapunk
genres.description: Short-lived early 2010s internet movement associated with oceanic imagery and computer graphics, deriving into vivid fashion trends, often incorporating aquatic elements into Electronic styles and visual aesthetics as well as influences by prominent tropes of 1990s rave culture.

genres.name: Second British Folk Revival
genres.description: Revival of Folk music in the United Kingdom which began at the end of the Second World War, peaked in the early-to-mid 1970s, and lost wider relevance by the end of the decade.

genres.name: Second Viennese School
genres.description: Influential circle of composers of very late Romanticism and Modern Classical who developed Expressionism and Serialism.

genres.name: Seggae
genres.description: Fusion of Séga and Reggae, popular on Mauritius and other Mascarene Islands.

genres.name: Seinn nan salm
genres.description: Unaccompanied, rhythmically free-flowing psalm singing in Gaelic practiced by Presbyterian churches, which involves a call-and-response between the precentor and the congregation.

genres.name: Seishun Punk
genres.description: Short-lived Japanese style popular in the early 2000s, characterized by a raw and abrasive style, Folk-inspired songwriting, and youth-oriented straightforward lyrics.

genres.name: Semba
genres.description: Style from Angola featuring danceable percussion, lyrics often taking the form of a story, and sometimes accompaniment from a guitar.

genres.name: Semi-Trot
genres.description: Contemporary form of Trot which takes influences from modern K-Pop and recent Pop substyles.

genres.name: Sephardic Music
genres.description: Encompasses the various musical traditions of Sephardi Jews.

genres.name: Sequencer & Tracker
genres.description: Composed for early home computer and game consoles from the late 1980s to the late 1990s, primarily for video game soundtracks.

genres.name: Serbian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Serbian people.

genres.name: Serenade
genres.description: Light, tuneful, and relatively straightforward music historically associated with outdoor entertainment for evening gatherings.

genres.name: Serialism
genres.description: Compositional method in which pitches are grouped into sets (tone rows) to determine the order and frequency of their use.

genres.name: Sermons
genres.description: Religious oral addresses delivered with the intent to uplift or educate an audience.

genres.name: Sertanejo
genres.description: Acoustic guitar-based and originated from the rural parts of Brazilian Center-South region.

genres.name: Sertanejo de raiz
genres.description: Earliest form of Sertanejo, emerging in pre-World War II rural Brazil during the late 1920s; quickly strummed acoustic guitars, most commonly the 10-string viola caipira and classical guitar, and a highly emotive vocal style.

genres.name: Sertanejo romântico
genres.description: Electric instrumentation and romantic lyrics, made popular nationwide during the mid-to-late 1980s.

genres.name: Sertanejo universitário
genres.description: Modernized style combining rural themes and acoustic instrumentation with commercial production and Electronic instrumentation.

genres.name: Seto leelo
genres.description: Style of polyphonic singing of the Seto people.

genres.name: Sexy Drill
genres.description: Emotive and sensual melodies, samples, and basslines set to driving stomps and bouncy Drill percussion typically joined by lyrical themes of sex, love, clubbing, and heartbreak.

genres.name: Seychelles & Mascarene Islands Music
genres.description: Styles from La Réunion, Mauritius, Rodrigues, and Seychelles.

genres.name: Shaabi
genres.description: Developed in Egypt during the early 1970s, typically created by and for the urban working class with witty lyrics that reflect this.

genres.name: Shabad kirtan
genres.description: Religious Sikh Hymns backed by specially selected ragas and taal.

genres.name: Shaker Music
genres.description: Created by the United Society of Believers in Christ's Second Appearing, better known as Shakers, for worship.

genres.name: Shan'ge
genres.description: Folk songs found in upland regions of China, typically sung while working.

genres.name: Shangaan Electro
genres.description: South African genre with very fast BPM (around 180) featuring MIDI keyboard sounds and marimba.

genres.name: Shashmaqam
genres.description: Modal suite that brings together lyrical and instrumental songs, poetry, and dance shared by Tajik Music and Uzbek Music.

genres.name: Shatta
genres.description: French Caribbean Dancehall subgenre with a focus on sparse percussion, heavy basslines and lyrics revolving around partying and sensuality, often in Creole.

genres.name: Shehhi Music
genres.description: Musical traditions of the Shihuh, an Arabian tribe native to the United Arab Emirates and Oman.

genres.name: Shetland & Orkney Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Shetland and Orkney Islands.

genres.name: Shibuya-kei
genres.description: Eclectic scene emerging from the Shibuya district of Tokyo near the end of the 1980s; often borrows kitschy, retro-inspired aesthetics alongside diverse musical influences from Indie Pop, 1960s Pop and Easy Listening, Jazz, and Electronic styles.

genres.name: Shidaiqu
genres.description: Fusion of Chinese popular music and Jazz that began in the 1920s in Shanghai.

genres.name: Shilla
genres.description: Traditional style of sung Nabati poetry, prevalent across the Arabian Peninsula.

genres.name: Shilluk Music
genres.description: All musical forms of the Shilluk people of the Upper Nile region of South Sudan.

genres.name: Shimokita-kei
genres.description: Japanese style closely related to the Shimokitazawa indie scene, featuring Pop-informed songwriting, melodic guitar leads, expressive vocals, and often loud, prominent overdriven guitars.

genres.name: Shitgaze
genres.description: Blends extremely raw and lo-fi aesthetics, abrasive guitar tones, and typically, the ethos of raucous Garage Rock, to create a sonic wall of deafening distortion evocative of Shoegaze.

genres.name: Shoegaze
genres.description: Dense, noisy, and ethereal washes of sound primarily created with electric guitars and heavy use of effects pedals, such as fuzz, reverb, chorus, and delay, with vocals serving as a dreamy, usually unintelligible melodic layer.

genres.name: Shona Mbira Music
genres.description: Traditional music based on cyclical patterns played on the mbira, from which long instrumental parts are improvised.

genres.name: Shona Music
genres.description: Music of the Shona people, a Bantu ethnic group who form a majority population in Zimbabwe.

genres.name: Shoor
genres.description: Mourning eulogy characterized by an intense emotional fervor and rhythmic delivery.

genres.name: Show Tunes
genres.description: Originally composed to forward the story or enhance the characters or other plot elements of Broadway productions and other stage music.

genres.name: Shōmyō
genres.description: Japanese Buddhist chant that utilizes the yō scale.

genres.name: Siberian Punk
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1980s, often blending the noisy, abrasive sound of Garage Punk and Post-Punk with radical anti-totalitarian lyrics drawing from British Punk influences.

genres.name: Siffleur
genres.description: Professional whistlers on the Vaudeville and Music Hall circuits.

genres.name: Sigilkore
genres.description: Dark and hyperactive production, featuring rapping laced with layers of effects.

genres.name: Sinawi
genres.description: Improvisational genre traditionally serving as an accompaniment to Korean shamanic rituals.

genres.name: Sindhi Music
genres.description: Music rooted in the traditions of the Sindhi people.

genres.name: Sinfonia concertante
genres.description: Fuses symphonic compositional structure and instrumentation with parts written for concertante soloists.

genres.name: Singeli
genres.description: Developed in Tanzania in the mid-2000s; fuses incredibly rapid beats, usually between 180-300BPM, with MCing and musical influences from older Tanzanian genres.

genres.name: Singer-Songwriter
genres.description: Heavily focused on lyrics and songwriting, with musical accompaniment tending to take lower precedence.

genres.name: Singspiel
genres.description: German form of Opera distinguished by the prominent usage of spoken dialogues mixed with lyrical or folklore arias/ballads.

genres.name: Sinhalese Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Sinhalese people, the majority ethnic group of Sri Lanka.

genres.name: Sissy Bounce
genres.description: Energetic style associated with New Orleans’ LGBT culture, featuring punchy drums, hyper-repetitive vocal chops, and sexually explicit chants.

genres.name: Sitarsploitation
genres.description: Variant of Exotica capitalising on the surge of Western interest in Indian music in the late 1960s; featured melodies played on the sitar (or instruments imitating it) atop Easy Listening accompaniment.

genres.name: Sizhu Music
genres.description: Traditional string and wind instrument based chamber music ensembles, prevalent in Southern China.

genres.name: Ska
genres.description: Originated in Jamaica in the late 1950s, characterized by a signature off-beat rhythm (referred to as the ‘skank’ rhythm), chop-style guitar work, busy bass lines and a use of horn sections.

genres.name: Ska Punk
genres.description: Utilizes skank rhythms, walking basslines, and often horn instrumentation in combination with a fast-paced Punk Rock playstyle.

genres.name: Skacore
genres.description: Fuses skank rhythms and frantic blasts of horns with hardcore intensity.

genres.name: Skate Punk
genres.description: Combines the speed of Melodic Hardcore with the catchiness of Pop Punk, finding a middle ground between the two.

genres.name: Sketch Comedy
genres.description: Performers assume a dramatic setting (rather than addressing the audience directly), often as fictional characters.

genres.name: Skiffle
genres.description: Grew out of British Trad Jazz, drawing influence from 1920s Jug Bands and the strong rhythms of 1950s Honky Tonk and Rock & Roll.

genres.name: Skiladika
genres.description: Greek popular artists who used more Arabian elements; originally a derogatory term used to refer to a more decadent side of Laika.

genres.name: Skinhead Reggae
genres.description: Early subgenre prominent from 1968 to 1971; known for its high tempos and driving rhythms compared with the more languid pace of most later styles.

genres.name: Skramz
genres.description: Intense, aggressive and complex approach to Emo featuring higher levels of abrasiveness and dissonance, accompanied by guitar-focused melodicism and harsh vocals.

genres.name: Skullstep
genres.description: Repetitious, aggressive, off-beat rhythms often programmed using distorted, harsh, and noisy percussion that usually resembles clangy "pots and pans", machine gun-like snares.

genres.name: Skweee
genres.description: Mid-2000s offshoot of the Nordic Electro scene which uses simple, analogue or Chiptune-inspired synthesizer leads and basslines to create stripped-down, midtempo grooves drawing on Synth Funk and Hip Hop.

genres.name: Slack-Key Guitar
genres.description: Originated in Hawaii and typically played with one's thumb in an alternating-bass pattern on the lower two or three strings.

genres.name: Slacker Rock
genres.description: Raw, noisy, and melodic, with a loose, blasé approach to performances and typically low-fidelity production.

genres.name: Slam Death Metal
genres.description: Focuses on slow or midtempo (as well as breakdown-style) sections built on chromatic, palm-muted riffs - so-called "slams".

genres.name: Slam Poetry
genres.description: Developed in the US during the late 1980s and early 1990s with the growing popularity of poetry slams, a form of poetry competition in which competing performers recite poems in front of a crowd.

genres.name: Slap House
genres.description: Taking influences from Brazilian Bass and Future House, characterized by prominent, "bouncy" bassline and simple, upbeat melodies.

genres.name: Slavic Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music native to Slavic peoples.

genres.name: Sleaze Rock
genres.description: Raw and lurid form of Glam Metal with influences from Glam Punk and Blues Rock and back-to-basics songwriting; emerged to counter Pop influences in Hard Rock in the mid-to-late 1980s.

genres.name: Slimepunk
genres.description: Loud synth leads with a distorted, gritty, and "slimy" sound design, usually laid on top of production inspired by or taken directly from genres such as Halftime, Trap [EDM], Brostep, and other forms of 2010s EDM.

genres.name: Slovak Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Slovaks.

genres.name: Slovenian Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Slovenian people.

genres.name: Slowcore
genres.description: Characterized by its subdued, often sombre songwriting and slow tempos, while taking primarily from genres like Dream Pop and Folk Rock.

genres.name: Sludge Metal
genres.description: Mixes Doom Metal's slow pacing, down-tuned riffing style and dark atmosphere with Hardcore Punk's aggression, abrasiveness and harsh vocals.

genres.name: Slushwave
genres.description: Utilizes a distinct form of sample manipulation to create a “slushy” sound, usually sequenced in soft Ambient-based soundscapes.

genres.name: Smooth Jazz
genres.description: Simple melodies and slick production influenced by Pop and R&B.

genres.name: Smooth Soul
genres.description: Slow tempo ballads with silky, often sensual, vocals and light, polished arrangements, creating an intimate, romantic atmosphere.

genres.name: Snap
genres.description: Sparse production, pounding 808 bass, occasional use of third-beat finger snaps, and simple melodies reminiscent of ringtones.

genres.name: Soca
genres.description: Upbeat, poppy and danceable style rooted in Calypso and Indo-Caribbean Music; developed in the late 1960s and early 1970s in Trinidad and Tobago.

genres.name: Soft Rock
genres.description: Clean production and light instrumentation paired with harmonious, radio-friendly songwriting; gained huge commercial success in the 1970s.

genres.name: Soft Visual
genres.description: Starting in the 1990s, featuring more toned-down "classy" and "casual"-style outfits with a natural style of makeup, along with more pop-oriented songwriting, contrasting the darkness of contemporary styles of Visual kei.

genres.name: Soga Music
genres.description: Music of the Soga people, a Bantu ethnic group residing in Eastern Uganda.

genres.name: Solonese Gamelan
genres.description: Style originating from Surakarta; known for its subtle and more delicate sound.

genres.name: Somali Music
genres.description: Music developed by the Somali people.

genres.name: Son calentano
genres.description: Usually dominated by violin with accompaniment mainly provided by guitars and tamboras, occasionally dancers will stomp over a platform.

genres.name: Son cubano
genres.description: Cuban style popular from the 1920s to the 1950s that combines the structure of Spanish song-oriented styles with African rhythms and percussion.

genres.name: Son de pascua
genres.description: Lively instrumental Christmas songs from Central America composed in 6/8 or triple meter.

genres.name: Son huasteco
genres.description: Bold rhythmic structure, lively violin playing, and extensive use of falsetto.

genres.name: Son istmeño
genres.description: Developed in the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, traditionally played by guitar, requinto, marimba, and bajoquinto, usually played in 3/4 time.

genres.name: Son jarocho
genres.description: Mexican Folk Music from the Gulf Coast Mexican state of Veracruz, with both Spanish and indigenous influences.

genres.name: Son montuno
genres.description: Developed in the 1940s, characterized by more elaborate instrumental arrangements and larger ensembles typically adding a horn section, conga drums, and piano.

genres.name: Son nica
genres.description: Nicaraguan popular rhythm in distinctive guitar strums, with lyrics relating to the countryside and peasant life.

genres.name: Sonata
genres.description: Broad instrumental genre for one to three soloists that has changed significantly throughout its history, now typically a suite of four or fewer contrasting movements, at least one of which is written in sonata form.

genres.name: Songhai Music
genres.description: Music of the Songhai people of Mali, who descend from the ancient Songhai Empire which once ruled most of interior West Africa.

genres.name: Songo
genres.description: Cuban style originating in the late 1960s, combining elements from Rumba cubana and Son cubano with Jazz and Funk.

genres.name: Sonorism
genres.description: Techniques and forms that emphasize texture and timbre.

genres.name: Sophisti-Pop
genres.description: Incorporates influences from Jazz, classic R&B and Soul along with a slick, polished production style while retaining elements from its New Wave roots.

genres.name: Sotho-Tswana Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Sotho-Tswana ethnic family groups from southern Africa.

genres.name: Soukous
genres.description: Danceable, guitar-based style from the Congo area.

genres.name: Soul
genres.description: Originated in the African American culture of the 20th century, resulting from the combination of the ecstatic vocals of Gospel with the upbeat instrumentation of Rhythm & Blues, consisting of guitar, bass and percussion.

genres.name: Soul Blues
genres.description: Shares similarities with Soul and incorporates the eponymous soulful inflections of Gospel, Jump Blues and soul into the vocals.

genres.name: Soul Jazz
genres.description: Appeared during the 1950s when Gospel, Rhythm & Blues and later Soul started to influence the style of prolific Jazz musicians.

genres.name: Sound Art
genres.description: Incorporates elements from Experimental music and visual arts, with sound utilized as its primary medium and subject.

genres.name: Sound Collage
genres.description: Compositional method emphasizing the rough layering of sampled elements, presenting an impression similar to a visual collage.

genres.name: Sound Effects
genres.description: Non-musical audio works, including recorded sounds and sounds recreated synthetically or by other means, which are either sounds of known objects or abstract noise manifestations.

genres.name: Sound Poetry
genres.description: Emphasis is placed upon phonetics and the sounds of syllables rather than the meaning of the words themselves.

genres.name: SoundClown
genres.description: Scene focused on comedic, often ironic edits of pre-existing music, popular on SoundCloud in the mid-2010s.

genres.name: South American Music
genres.description: Rooted in the traditions of South America.

genres.name: South Asian Classical Music
genres.description: Meta-genre that covers the diverse forms of Classical Music from South Asia.

genres.name: South Asian Folk Music
genres.description: Meta-genre which covers all the Traditional Folk Music forms from South Asia.

genres.name: South Asian Music
genres.description: Traditional and modern regional music of India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Sri Lanka, which culturally have close connections.

genres.name: South Florida SoundCloud Rap
genres.description: Mid-to-late 2010s Hip Hop scene noted for its use of internet platform SoundCloud to promote and distribute music, as well as lo-fi production and transgressive approaches to rapping.

genres.name: Southeast Asian Classical Music
genres.description: Formal music developed in Southeast Asian countries (Burma, Cambodia, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, East Timor, Brunei Darussalam) usually in form of gong-chime orchestras such as gamelan, kulintang and pi phat.

genres.name: Southeast Asian Folk Music
genres.description: Meta-genre covering all folk forms from Southeast Asia, like Gondang, Hmong, Iban, Karen, Keroncong, Khmer, Lao, Lun Bawang, Molam, and Orang Ulu.

genres.name: Southeast Asian Music
genres.description: Geographic meta-parent that covers different forms with origins in Burma, Cambodia, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, East Timor, Laos, Singapore, and Brunei.

genres.name: Southeastern Brazilian Music
genres.description: Regional styles of diverse cultural expressions rooted in Southeastern Brazil that combine elements of African Music and European Music.

genres.name: Southern African Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of southern Africa.

genres.name: Southern African Music
genres.description: Encompasses Southern African Folk Music and more modern genres, consisting in a specific style of a worldwide popular genre mixed with or rooted in a local traditional folk genre, through South Africa, Lesotho, Botswana, Eswatini, Namibia, southern Angola, and Matabeleland region in southern Zimbabwe.

genres.name: Southern Brazilian Music
genres.description: Traditional music originating from Southern Brazil.

genres.name: Southern Gospel
genres.description: Initially sung A cappella by a Vocal Group quartet, sometimes with a pianist or guitar as accompaniment, with lyrics and messages primarily revolving around the teachings found within Christianity.

genres.name: Southern Hip Hop
genres.description: Hip Hop from artists based in the Southern region of the United States.

genres.name: Southern Metal
genres.description: Blues-influenced style that primarily incorporates Sludge Metal and Stoner Metal with metallic Southern Rock riffs.

genres.name: Southern Rock
genres.description: Emerged from the American South in the early 1970s, blending Blues Rock, Hard Rock, and Rock & Roll with elements of Country and Contemporary Folk.

genres.name: Southern Soul
genres.description: Soul primarily from the American South that was popular in the 1960s and 1970s, with a gritty and raw sound that places an emphasis on the groove, making it highly danceable.

genres.name: Soviet Estrada
genres.description: Emerged in the USSR during the early 1930s, and encompassed the dominating popular music style composed by government-approved songwriters and the primary repertoire of professionally trained performers.

genres.name: Sovietwave
genres.description: Scene of Synthwave that emerged in the early 2010s, taking its inspiration from Soviet Electronic electronic music and Soviet pop.

genres.name: Space Age Pop
genres.description: Inspired by the excitement and optimism of the Space Age during the 1950s and 1960s, frequently experimenting with futuristic sounds made possible by contemporary technology.

genres.name: Space Ambient
genres.description: Flowing and relaxing synthesizer-based music derived from Progressive Electronic, often oriented around imagery of outer space.

genres.name: Space Disco
genres.description: Emerged in Europe in the mid-to-late 1970s, characterized by layers of oscillating synth, space-oriented sound effects, and a futuristic sound inspired by contemporary sci-fi media.

genres.name: Space Rock
genres.description: Heavy use of synthesizers and guitar effects to create dense atmospheric soundscapes intended to evoke images of outer space and science fiction scenarios.

genres.name: Space Rock Revival
genres.description: Draws from the aesthetics and atmospheric soundscapes of Space Rock combined with the more minimal, back-to-basics approach of the Post-Punk era.

genres.name: Spacesynth
genres.description: Highly melodic, often instrumental futuristic strain, formed under the heavy influence of Space Disco, Progressive Electronic and, later, early Eurobeat.

genres.name: Spaghetti Western
genres.description: Epic, cinematic sound evoking imagery of the Wild West, featuring a Surf Rock-inspired guitar tone while taking inspiration from the melodies and harmonies of traditional Mexican Music.

genres.name: Spanish Classical Music
genres.description: Incorporation of Spanish Music within the context of Western Classical Music, particularly characterized by the use of the classical guitar.

genres.name: Spanish Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of Spain, widely diverse due to the distinct culture and traditions of the country's different regions.

genres.name: Spanish Music
genres.description: Music of Spain.

genres.name: Spectralism
genres.description: Compositional practice involving analysis, manipulation, and transformation of sound spectra.

genres.name: Speeches
genres.description: Rhetorical acts performed publicly wherein a speaker typically monologues around a particular topic.

genres.name: Speed Garage
genres.description: Primarily British style that paved the way for UK Garage, combining cut-up vocal samples and sped up four-on-the-floor Garage House rhythms with Jungle-esque basslines.

genres.name: Speed House
genres.description: Mixes busy, dirty sound design and intense drums derived from Bass House with fast tempos from 140-160 BPM, pumping basslines, and other UK Hard House influences.

genres.name: Speed Metal
genres.description: Fast tempos, double-time feel, aggressive riffs, precise, often virtuosic soloing and expressive vocal styles.

genres.name: Speedcore
genres.description: Exceedingly fast tempos, frequently above 300 BPM, and often aggressive themes and samples.

genres.name: Spiritual Jazz
genres.description: Emerged in the 1960s, marked by a mixture of Jazz with approximations of ethnic styles, religious music of non-Christian traditions, and the ecstatic, transcendental aspects of Free Jazz.

genres.name: Spirituals
genres.description: Predecessor to Gospel that began as unaccompanied singing by American slaves; shares some of the characteristics of Work Song.

genres.name: Splittercore
genres.description: Faster version of Speedcore with BPM ranging from around 600 to 1000.

genres.name: Spoken Word
genres.description: Usually unaccompanied vocal readings.

genres.name: Spouge
genres.description: Fusion of Calypso and Ska originating in Barbados during the 1960s and 70s.

genres.name: Spy Music
genres.description: Meant to evoke the action and drama of Spy films.

genres.name: Stand-Up Comedy
genres.description: Comedy where the performer speaks directly to their intended audience, with origins beginning in the late 19th century.

genres.name: Standards
genres.description: Traditional compositions originating from the 1910s and onward which have become widely known, performed, and recorded across the world.

genres.name: Starogradska muzika
genres.description: Translated as "old city music", this is the urban traditional music of Macedonia and Serbia.

genres.name: Staïfi
genres.description: Festive Chaoui genre that mixes local rural music with the zendali rhythm and modern instruments.

genres.name: Steel Band
genres.description: Ensembles made out of steel drums that often perform Standards, Calypso, and Western Classical Music with densely rhythmic and colorful arrangements.

genres.name: Stenchcore
genres.description: Heavier, more metallic form of Crust Punk drawing influence from Thrash Metal as well as Death Metal and Heavy Metal.

genres.name: Stereo
genres.description: Burmese Pop Rock genre which emerged in the mid-1960s.

genres.name: Stochastic Music
genres.description: Composition featuring guided indeterminism, where the following state is only partially determined by the preceding state.

genres.name: Stomp and Holler
genres.description: Highlights driving "stomping" rhythms and shouted group vocal harmonies, often drawing influences from Pop Rock, Indie Folk, and other genres, while maintaining a characteristically mellow and commercial sound.

genres.name: Stoner Metal
genres.description: Combines elements of Doom Metal with elements of Psychedelic Rock and Blues Rock to create a melodic yet heavy sound.

genres.name: Stoner Rap
genres.description: Heavily features lyrics about cannabis and stoner culture, usually with a laid-back flow and relaxing production.

genres.name: Stoner Rock
genres.description: Psychedelic timbres, raw production, and stylistic influence from Doom Metal and Heavy Psych.

genres.name: Stornello
genres.description: Italian folk poetry, generally improvised and handed down by street singers, carters or sellers.

genres.name: Straight Edge
genres.description: Developed in the early 1980s DC Hardcore Punk scene, promoting abstinence from the use of substances such as alcohol, tobacco, and other drugs.

genres.name: Street Punk
genres.description: Driven by Oi! style group vocals, catchy melodies, and aggressive songwriting akin to Punk Rock of the 1970s fused with Hardcore Punk of the 1980s.

genres.name: Stride
genres.description: Early form of Ragtime-derived Jazz with improvisational tendencies; named for the performers' left hand "striding" across the piano keyboard.

genres.name: String Quartet
genres.description: Small scale composition for an ensemble that consists of two violins, one viola, and one cello, with complex interplay and multiple (usually four) movements.

genres.name: Stutter House
genres.description: Emerged in the 2020s taking influences from Melodic House, Trance, and Future Garage; features distinctive chopping of vocal samples and pads.

genres.name: Sufi Music
genres.description: Covering the various musical traditions of Sufis.

genres.name: Sufi Rock
genres.description: Pakistani subgenre rooted in Sufi tradition, featuring South Asian instruments like the dhol, tabla, and sitar within a Rock band format with lyrics and imagery inspired by traditional Sufi poets.

genres.name: Sufiana kalam
genres.description: Classical music from Kashmir, the northernmost part of the Indian subcontinent.

genres.name: Sundanese Music
genres.description: Music of the Sundanese people.

genres.name: Sungura
genres.description: Zimbabwean style combining the guitar work of Soukous with the speed and texture of Benga and the strong bass of Township Jive.

genres.name: Sunset Strip Glam Metal
genres.description: 1980s Glam Metal scene based in West Hollywood, California, United States.

genres.name: Sunshine Pop
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1960s, characterized by a cheerful or wistful sound, light, lush production, and prominent vocal harmonies.

genres.name: Suomisaundi
genres.description: Finnish-based deviation of Psytrance with an emphasis on free-form experimentation and humor.

genres.name: Surf Music
genres.description: Evolved from late 1950s instrumental Rock & Roll in the USA, particularly associated with the surfing culture in Southern California.

genres.name: Surf Punk
genres.description: Punk Rock that incorporates elements of Surf Rock.

genres.name: Surf Rock
genres.description: Short instrumental songs with Rock & Roll rhythms overlaid with cheerful melodies played on reverb-drenched tremolo guitar.

genres.name: Sutartinės
genres.description: Unique form of polyphonic vocal music originating from a small area of Northeastern Lithuania.

genres.name: Swamp Blues
genres.description: Originated in Baton Rouge, Louisiana in the 1950s, with a laid-back and relaxed sound that takes influence from Zydeco and Cajun Music.

genres.name: Swamp Pop
genres.description: Uniquely Cajun style of Rhythm & Blues distinguished by tripleted pianos and a slow Blues structure.

genres.name: Swamp Rock
genres.description: Incorporates influences from the musical styles and traditions of Louisiana.

genres.name: Swancore
genres.description: High-register clean vocals and technical instrumentation drawn from Math Rock and Progressive Rock.

genres.name: Swedish Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional music of the Swedish people, commonly incorporating fiddle, accordion, flute, nyckelharpa, and/or voice.

genres.name: Sweet Jazz
genres.description: Early form developed by white bandleaders and highly popular with white audiences in the 1920s, emphasizing arrangements and strong melodies with a straighter rhythmic feel, de-emphasizing improvisation compared to "hot" Dixieland.

genres.name: Swing
genres.description: Distinctive rhythm and large backing rhythm section over which solos are performed.

genres.name: Swing Revival
genres.description: Born out of 1990s alternative music; sometimes incorporating elements from newer genres such as Rockabilly, Ska, and Punk Rock.

genres.name: Symphonic Black Metal
genres.description: Symphonic soundscapes, typically but not always synthesized.

genres.name: Symphonic Metal
genres.description: Incorporates elements of symphonic and Orchestral Music.

genres.name: Symphonic Mugham
genres.description: Introduces elements of Azerbaijani Mugham into the structure of the composition, played on a full western orchestra.

genres.name: Symphonic Prog
genres.description: Incorporates Classical Music elements that can manifest in longer form works that deviate from traditional popular song structures, and the use of lush keyboards to replicate Orchestral Music textures.

genres.name: Symphonic Rock
genres.description: Incorporates elements resembling Orchestral Music.

genres.name: Symphony
genres.description: Large-scale Western Classical Music works for orchestra, typically with four movements: 1) allegro, almost always in sonata-allegro form 2) a slow movement 3) scherzo or minuet 4) finale, typically allegro or rondo.

genres.name: Synth Funk
genres.description: Stripped-down and futuristic, driven by synthesizer melodies and often incorporating drum machines.

genres.name: Synth Punk
genres.description: Appropriates the harsh elements of Punk Rock but replaces the predominance of guitars with synthesizers and drum machines.

genres.name: Synthpop
genres.description: Led by melodic synthesizer sounds, often with reverberating drum machine patterns; commonly associated with the 1980s.

genres.name: Synthwave
genres.description: Rooted in 1980s synth music, characterized by large, throbbing "retro" synths and visual elements, often features upbeat percussion and/or epic, cinematic atmospheres.

genres.name: Syriac Chant
genres.description: Liturgical chant repertoire practiced within Syriac Christianity, comprising the East Syrian and West Syrian liturgical rites.

genres.name: Séga
genres.description: Mascarene Islands and Seychelles genre featuring a distinctive 6/8 rhythm.

genres.name: Sōkyoku
genres.description: Gained popularity during the Edo period, played with a koto or a guzheng and sometimes accompanied by shamisen and/or shakuhachi.

genres.name: T-Pop
genres.description: Mainstream Pop from Thailand made popular since the early 1980s, predominantly sung in Central Thai dialect and featuring westernized compositions ranging within various styles.

genres.name: Taarab
genres.description: Prominent violin, qanun (an Egyptian zither-like instrument), and sung Swahili poetry, often accompanied by African drums and other percussion.

genres.name: Tahitian Music
genres.description: Music of the Tahitian people.

genres.name: Taiko
genres.description: Modern style of ensemble drumming, sometimes called kumi-daiko.

genres.name: Tajik Music
genres.description: Music of the Tajik people.

genres.name: Talempong
genres.description: Gong-chime ensemble focused around the talempong kettle gong.

genres.name: Talempong goyang
genres.description: Blends traditional Talempong elements with contemporary Pop influences, often featuring a female vocalist, and encourages audience participation.

genres.name: Talking Blues
genres.description: American Folk Music with spoken or nearly spoken vocals; often features dry humor and social commentary.

genres.name: Tallava
genres.description: Mixture of Romani, Greek, Turkish, Albanian, and Slavic music, which incorporates Dance-Pop elements, and is very popular in Albania and Kosovo.

genres.name: Tamborera
genres.description: Panamanian popular genre which mixes local Tamborito with Cuban Music rhythms featuring the tambora as the main percussion instrument.

genres.name: Tamborito
genres.description: Folk music and dance from Panama dating back to the 17th century.

genres.name: Tamborzão
genres.description: Adds Afro-Brazilian percussive elements such as the atabaque sound into the Miami Bass kick drums.

genres.name: Tamil Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Tamil people.

genres.name: Tango
genres.description: Melancholic sound generally led by a guitar or bandoneon, originating in Buenos Aires by the late 19th century and gaining worldwide popularity from the 1920s to the 1950s.

genres.name: Tango nuevo
genres.description: Adds new elements into traditional Argentine Tango, most importantly the incorporation of Jazz and Western Classical Music.

genres.name: Tanjidor
genres.description: Betawi form of street music ensemble derived from colonial Marching Bands.

genres.name: Taoist Ritual Music
genres.description: Originating in chants and instrumental accompaniment for Taoist ritual practice.

genres.name: Tape Music
genres.description: Explores the nature of audio recorded to magnetic tape and the act of playing sound from it.

genres.name: Taquirari
genres.description: Developed by the indigenous peoples of eastern Bolivia, bringing in some elements of Hispanic Music, and featuring a syncopated rhythm.

genres.name: Taqwacore
genres.description: Punk subculture that emerged in the United States during the early 2000s, exploring Islam, its culture, and interpretations.

genres.name: Tarana
genres.description: Vocal composition with Persian or Arabic syllables and phonemes.

genres.name: Tarantella
genres.description: Fast upbeat tempo, switching between major and minor modes while gradually increasing in speed.

genres.name: Tarawangsa
genres.description: Sacred ceremonial music originating in the Rancakalong district, played with the jentreng harp and the tarawangsa bowed lute.

genres.name: Tarraxinha
genres.description: Heavy-hitting beats and electronic bass, putting less emphasis on melodies and vocals.

genres.name: Tassa
genres.description: Drum ensemble descended from a mixture of northern Indian drumming traditions.

genres.name: Tassu
genres.description: Rhythmic poetry that has been a part of Senegalese culture since ancient times.

genres.name: Tchink System
genres.description: Urban version of Tchinkoumé featuring traditional tchinkoumé rhythms, derived from zinli, and including contemporary instrumentation from the influence of R&B, Pop and Rock.

genres.name: Tchinkoumé
genres.description: Tradition from the central region of Benin around Savalou, played with water percussion.

genres.name: Tearout
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2000s, characterized by a gritty, aggressive sound and closely affiliated with early, deep Dubstep.

genres.name: Tearout [Brostep]
genres.description: Heavy and distorted, closely affiliated with Deathstep and other styles of Brostep.

genres.name: Tech House
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1990s taking influences from Techno, broadly characterized by minimalistic and repetitive melodies, focus on the bassline, and constant groove recognizable by prominent off-beat hi-hats.

genres.name: Tech Trance
genres.description: Late 1990s-emerging subgenre characterized by energetic percussion with loud kicks, filtered hi-hats and tribal drums; side-chained, detuned and repetitive leads, as well as other raw, distorted, and complex sounds influenced by Techno, Hard Trance and Electro House.

genres.name: Technical Death Metal
genres.description: Focuses on challenging, demanding songwriting and instrumental skill.

genres.name: Technical Thrash Metal
genres.description: Places great emphasis on complex songwriting and demanding instrumental parts.

genres.name: Techno
genres.description: Highly beat-driven, repetitive, and mechanical, typically featuring minimal chord variation and melodies, focuses on rhythms and timbral variety; generally produced for club environments.

genres.name: Techno Bass
genres.description: Minimal, stripped-down with an emphasis on low-frequency bass partitions.

genres.name: Techno kayō
genres.description: Offshoot of 1980s Kayōkyoku and Idol kayō incorporating characteristics from Synthpop.

genres.name: Technoid
genres.description: Influenced by the repetitive and mechanical sound of Techno.

genres.name: Techstep
genres.description: Futuristic, dark, and gritty sound; quantized and compressed drum breaks, distorted bass lines, and a focus on a sci-fi atmosphere and sampling sources.

genres.name: Tecnobrega
genres.description: Fast and electronic-based style that evolved from Brega calypso, particularly associated with peripheral areas of the city of Belém.

genres.name: Tecnofunk
genres.description: Raw and vulgar Tecnobrega and Funk brasileiro fusion developed in the late 2010s by DJs in Belém do Pará.

genres.name: Tecnomerengue
genres.description: Fuses basic Merengue rhythms with influences from Cumbia and Lambada, being largely synthesized, with live instruments usually limited to percussion and brass.

genres.name: Tecnorumba
genres.description: Blend of the themes and singing style of Rumba flamenca with the most commercial forms of House, Techno, and Makina.

genres.name: Teen Pop
genres.description: Oriented to teen audiences and almost always sung by teens.

genres.name: Tejano Music
genres.description: Mexican-American style infusing the conjunto Norteño ensemble with European dances and American popular music.

genres.name: Telugu Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Telugu people, one of the largest ethnolinguistic groups of India, mainly living in the states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

genres.name: Tembang Sunda Cianjuran
genres.description: Sung free-verse poetry in Sundanese language, usually by a solo vocalist, accompanied by a mellow-sounding Kacapi suling ensemble.

genres.name: Terror Plugg
genres.description: Harsher and noisier, with 808s distorted to create a high-frequency sound.

genres.name: Terrorcore
genres.description: Utilizes rhythms from earlier Gabber with a faster BPM (usually no more than 300) and darker approach.

genres.name: Teutonic Thrash Metal
genres.description: Influential German Thrash Metal scene originating in the early 1980s.

genres.name: Tex-Mex
genres.description: Mixes Rock & Roll, Blues, Country, and several types of Hispanic American Music, particularly Tejano Music.

genres.name: Texan Music
genres.description: Regional Music from the US state of Texas.

genres.name: Texas Psychedelia
genres.description: Influential, pioneering Psychedelic Rock scene active primarily in the mid- to late 1960s that grew out of the Texas Garage Rock scene.

genres.name: Thai Classical Music
genres.description: Emerged from the royal courts of Central Thailand around the 13th century, based on a traditional Thai sound-scale of seven tempered notes.

genres.name: Thai Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Thai people.

genres.name: Thai Music
genres.description: Music of the Thai people.

genres.name: Thall
genres.description: Utilizes rapid release bends and a precise playstyle while contrasting pitch-shifted high and low notes, with ambient sections for atmosphere and buildup.

genres.name: The Wave
genres.description: Group of American Post-Hardcore bands in the 2010s performing an aggressive style of '90s-inspired music in the wake of Emo-Pop's waning popularity.

genres.name: Theme and Variation
genres.description: Main theme followed by a number of variations on the theme.

genres.name: Third Stream
genres.description: A fusion of Jazz and Western Classical Music, with improvisation as a vital component.

genres.name: Third Wave Ska
genres.description: Expanded on the 2 Tone period, adding further Rock elements resulting in a heavier sound.

genres.name: Thrash Metal
genres.description: Blistering tempos, palm-muted, technical riffing influenced by Speed Metal, aggressive drumming utilizing double-kick and skank beats, and diverse vocal styles ranging from harsh to clean techniques.

genres.name: Thrashcore
genres.description: Fast tempos, brief song structures, and the occasional use of blast beats.

genres.name: Thumri
genres.description: Hindustani classical style based on North Indian folk literature.

genres.name: Tibetan Buddhist Chant
genres.description: Ritual vocal music of the Tibetan Buddhist faith characterized by its low pitch, droning repetitiousness, and frequent use of overtone singing.

genres.name: Tibetan Music
genres.description: Traditional and modern music of the Tibetan peoples, mainly produced in Tibet and also practiced in Bhutan, Nepal, and northern India, and influential on the traditions of Burma.

genres.name: Tibetan New Age
genres.description: Incorporates perceived elements of Tibetan Music, particularly singing bowls.

genres.name: Tigrinya Music
genres.description: Music of the Tigrinya, an ethnic group mainly found in Eritrea and Northern Ethiopia, the Tigray region more specifically.

genres.name: Timba
genres.description: Combines Salsa with other genres such as Hip Hop, Disco, Funk, Jazz and Rock.

genres.name: Timbila
genres.description: Tradition of the Chopi people of the Inhambane province of Mozambique, named for the mbila, the wooden xylophone-like instrument on which it is played.

genres.name: Tin Pan Alley
genres.description: Early era of popular song in the USA, broadly from the 1890s-1930s; influences include Ragtime, Vaudeville, and Parlour Music.

genres.name: Tivaner inngernerlu
genres.description: Pre-colonial Inuit Folk tradition centered around the qilaat (drum).

genres.name: Tizita
genres.description: Melancholy song popular in Ethiopia and Eritrea, using the qegnet mode and tuning system.

genres.name: Toada de Boi
genres.description: Slow, heavy-percussed tunes celebrating the folkloric Ox, originally from Bumba-meu-boi June parties in Northeastern Brazil.

genres.name: Toccata
genres.description: Virtuoso piece, usually for solo keyboard or plucked string instrument, characterized by its free rhythm, rapid fingerwork, and contrasting sectional writing.

genres.name: Tolai Rock
genres.description: Fuses the music of the Tolai people of Papua New Guinea with Rock.

genres.name: Tonada chilena
genres.description: Traditional folk from the Chilean countryside distinguished by its prominent melody.

genres.name: Tonada potosina
genres.description: Traditional folk sung in Quechua, played on charangos and guitarillas, with a catchy, lively rhythm.

genres.name: Tondero
genres.description: Backing to the fast-paced dance that originated in northern Peru in the region of Piura of the same name; bands consist of a singer, a small chorus, two guitarists, along with the cajón and sometimes a spoon player.

genres.name: Tone Poem
genres.description: Programmatic work, usually in a single movement, that is entirely based on external non-musical themes, ideas, tales, etc.

genres.name: Tontipop
genres.description: Spanish scene known for its exuberant, child-like sound drawing directly from British Twee Pop, as well as Yé-yé, Bubblegum, and Synthpop.

genres.name: Tosk Polyphony
genres.description: Polyphonic singing in the Toskëri region of southern Albania.

genres.name: Totalism
genres.description: Adds complex rhythmic structures and emphasis on surface energy to Minimalism.

genres.name: Touhou Music
genres.description: Stemming from doujin bullet hell video game franchise Touhou Project, including original music and derivative fan arrangements of varying styles.

genres.name: Township Bubblegum
genres.description: Synth-heavy Dance-Pop style popular in the South African townships in the 1980s and early 1990s.

genres.name: Township Jive
genres.description: Originating in the townships of South Africa, similar to Mbaqanga but bringing in Western pop elements.

genres.name: Toypop
genres.description: Avant-garde, naive, and child-like; explores the sonic capabilities of toy instruments.

genres.name: Toytown Pop
genres.description: Niche offshoot of British Psychedelic Pop most popular in the late 1960s and early 70s; typically featuring strong influence from Music Hall and Novelty, as well as the culture of Victorian and Edwardian Britain, and characterised by a whimsical, childlike atmosphere.

genres.name: Tracker Music
genres.description: Vertical text-based step-sequencer software sampler music in the first and second gen module formats like .MOD, .MED, .S3M, .XM and .IT.

genres.name: Tradi-moderne congolais
genres.description: Updates traditional Congolese music with electric instrumentation.

genres.name: Tradi-moderne ivoirien
genres.description: Blends traditional Ivorian songs, rhythms and instruments with modern electric and electronic instruments.

genres.name: Traditional Black Gospel
genres.description: Born out of Spirituals in the early 20th century with influence from Southern Gospel and Blues, often featuring passionate or energetic vocal performances, motifs of salvation, and testaments of hardship.

genres.name: Traditional Bluegrass
genres.description: Driving tempos, acoustic stringed instrumentation, and high vocal harmonies, adhering to the stylistic roots of the Bluegrass genre.

genres.name: Traditional Cajun Music
genres.description: Earliest and most "pure" form of Cajun Music, employing basic rhythms and frequent fiddle double stops.

genres.name: Traditional Country
genres.description: Closely aligned with American Folk Music and Blues roots, from country's inception in Appalachia and the American South until the popularity of Honky Tonk and Country Pop in the 1950s.

genres.name: Traditional Doom Metal
genres.description: Monotonous and heavy playing style; repetitive, rough, and sometimes atonal guitar riffs; a "rocking to sleep" bass; and influences from both Blues Rock and Psychedelic Rock.

genres.name: Traditional Folk Music
genres.description: Informed by a long history of tradition in a specific culture or region, mostly associated with the peasantry and non-aristocratic public.

genres.name: Traditional Maloya
genres.description: Derived from Traditional Séga, this is the original dance music of La Réunion.

genres.name: Traditional Pop
genres.description: Predominant form of Western commercial popular music in the pre-Rock & Roll era, particularly in the USA and starting with Tin Pan Alley; typically vocal-oriented with an orchestral arrangement.

genres.name: Traditional Raï
genres.description: Original folk of the popular Algerian Raï, combining various rural and cabaret styles with Bedouin rhythms.

genres.name: Traditional Séga
genres.description: Séga dance music born in the 18th century, before its later adoption of Western pop elements.

genres.name: Tragédie en musique
genres.description: French Opera genre developed by Jean-Baptiste Lully and Philippe Quinault in the second half of the 17th century, consisting of alterations made to the coeval Italian format to better fit the French language and please an audience more accustomed to the ballet de cour.

genres.name: Trallalero
genres.description: Polyphonic Traditional Folk Music originating in the Ligurian region of Genoa, in northern Italy.

genres.name: Trampská hudba
genres.description: Associated with the tramping lifestyle, typically mixing acoustic guitar driven Contemporary Folk with strong Country influences and vocal harmonies in peaceful, simple and relatively short songs.

genres.name: Trance
genres.description: Evolving, tension-building structures with rapid, minor arpeggios on top of a hypnotic, four-on-the-floor drum patterns at fast tempo around 130-150 BPM.

genres.name: Trance Metal
genres.description: Tempo between 130 and 160 BPM, played with keyboards and metal instrumentation, sung with harsh and aggressive vocals including many clean melodic styles; regularly uses elements of Melodic Death Metal, Symphonic Metal, and Electronic Dance Music.

genres.name: Trancestep
genres.description: Combination of Trance melodies and structure with the breakbeats, fast tempos, and rolling basslines of Drum and Bass.

genres.name: Trap
genres.description: Originated in Atlanta in the early 2000s; distinctive fast hi-hat sound and heavy bass at moderate tempos.

genres.name: Trap [EDM]
genres.description: Trap-influenced syncopated percussion with 808 samples and fast-paced hi-hats.

genres.name: Trap Dancehall
genres.description: Combines midtempo Dancehall rhythms and tempos with major elements borrowed from Trap, namely in percussion and drum rhythms.

genres.name: Trap latino
genres.description: Distinguished by its Reggaetón and Latin Rap roots, with smooth and moody production inspired by Alternative R&B and Contemporary R&B.

genres.name: Trap Metal
genres.description: Loud, distorted 808s and basslines, as well as aggressive vocals that are usually yelled or screamed.

genres.name: Trap shaabi
genres.description: Combining Trap percussion and rhythms with Egyptian Shaabi and especially Mahraganat.

genres.name: Trap Soul
genres.description: Mixes passionate vocals derived from Contemporary R&B with laid-back, nocturnal and atmospheric Trap production.

genres.name: Trapfunk
genres.description: Heavy beats and prominent bass, common in Trap, along with the energy and fast-paced funk rhythm.

genres.name: Tread
genres.description: Icy or futuristic synths with busy and high-tempo drum programming using distinctive 808 patterns.

genres.name: Tribal Ambient
genres.description: Combines the theory and atmosphere of Ambient with traditional instruments and sounds from around the globe.

genres.name: Tribal Guarachero
genres.description: Features percussion from Cumbia and Mexican Folk Music with upbeat Electro House-derived production and fast, triplet-oriented rhythmic patterns.

genres.name: Tribal House
genres.description: Prominent, syncopated rhythms of tribal drums such as toms and bongos on top of a House beat, usually resulting in a percussive, energetic sound, while ranging in mood.

genres.name: Trikitixa
genres.description: Form of Basque folk music characterized by the use of accordion and tambourine.

genres.name: Trip Hop
genres.description: Evokes a surreal, trippy, dreamy, and sometimes dark atmosphere with offbeat turntable scratches, light vocal melodies, and Hip Hop-influenced beats.

genres.name: Tropical House
genres.description: Offshoot of Deep House featuring slow tempos around 100-115 BPM, light percussion and acoustic instrumentation, setting out to create a relaxed, summery, beach-like atmosphere.

genres.name: Tropical Rock
genres.description: Combines influences from Country Rock and Caribbean Music to create an acoustic and breezy "island" themed sound.

genres.name: Tropicanibalismo
genres.description: Colombian scene born in the early 2000s with the intention of reinventing Colombian coastal music, from a more current and experimental approach.

genres.name: Tropicália
genres.description: Blends Brazilian popular styles with the influence of Anglo-American Psychedelia; emerged as part of Brazil's late-1960s counterculture.

genres.name: Tropipop

genres.name: Turkmen Music
genres.description: Music of the Turkmen people.

genres.name: Turntable Music

genres.name: Turntablism

genres.name: Tuvan Throat Singing

genres.name: Twa Music

genres.name: Twist

genres.name: Udmurt Folk Music

genres.description: Traditions of the people of Ukraine.

genres.name: Ultra

genres.name: Unakesa

genres.description: Incorporates a blend of Trap percussion set to the re-utilization of old samples, such as 1990s pop culture or old computer library sounds.
